name: Adventure: Valley of the Unknown
admission: Adventure is $3. Regular admission - Adults $13.75. Children 2-12 $8.75. Seniors $12.75.
description: Members of the Explorer Society have been conducting an archaeological dig in the Valley of the Unknown on a recently discovered island. In the middle of the valley is the Observatory - a towering ruin rumored to hold the Treasure of Knowledge. Unfortunately, the Observatory is locked - and only true explorers can open it! Crack the code: Our intrepid adventurers need your help uncovering the secrets of this recently discovered island. Use your wits, creativity, and keen skills of observation to navigate the island's three areas and decipher an ancient code. Solve the levels, gain the ultimate treasure: You'll have to gain access to the island's towering Observatory to complete your quest. Enter the correct code into the keypad and the doors of the Observatory will swing open! Listen closely - could your discovery lead to another level of hidden secrets?

name: Extreme Screen Film: Legends of Flight
description: Journey to an ancient civilization and go on an archaeological dig in Adventure.

name: Winter Safari Tours
description: The winter is a wonderful time to see and experience the Wilds at work. Exclusive Winter Safari Tours have been created for adults and children alike to experience the Wilds between the general visitor seasons. See and learn about rare and endangered animals during the winter months of November through March on these special safari tour programs. The Winter Safari Tours begin with a light lunch and short conservation program presented by an experienced program staff member. After lunch, visitors board a heated Safari Transport for a guided safari tour experience through the winter landscape. View large groups of animals, such as the Sichuan takin, Pere David's deer, Przewalski's wild horse, American bison, and many more, as they roam in the open pasture in their winter coats. The tour also includes an exclusive stop at the Rhino Management Center where you can get up-close and personal with southern white rhinos and greater one-horned Asian rhinos in their winter quarters. Other destinations may include the Mid-Sized Carnivore Conservation Center to see cheetahs and African wild dogs, or the Giraffe Barn. Reservations and pre-payment are required.

name: Winter Pearl Market
description: Find fresh seasonal produce and a wide range other goods from summer market favorites such as Sweet Thing Gourmet, IKC Designs, The Olive Orchard, Luxbohme and others. Credit cards and the Ohio Directions Card will be accepted. The Winter Market is in its second year of a two-year grant from the USDA Farmers' Market Promotion Program.

name: Salsa Tuesdays at Park Street Cantina
description: Join the hotness of Park Street Cantina and indulge in a great night of Latin dancing! And we've got the cure for those two left feet, so no worries! Participate in the dance lesson at 8pm and equip yourself with some jaw-dropping moves. Then hit the floor at 9pm and impress the crowds.

name: Spicy Salsa Tuesdays
description: JC Entertainment invites you to experience a great night of Latin dancing at the newly remodeled Mynt Ultralounge, come and try out Mynt's brand new and spacious WOOD dance floor! Dancers you will have an absolute blast!

name: Extreme Screen Film: Dolphins and Whales 3D
description: Dive into a new immersive and highly emotional adventure with Jean-Michel Cousteau's DOLPHINS AND WHALES 3D, which takes you from the dazzling coral reefs of the Bahamas to the warm depths of the waters of the exotic Kingdom of Tonga for a close encounter with the surviving tribes of the ocean.

name: Out Takes
description: Out Takes is the Gateway Film Center's monthly GLBT film. The series is a partnership with Stonewall Columbus and all proceeds benefit Stonewall Columbus. Showtime is the first Thursday of every month.

name: Exhibit: Paintings by Barbara Frentsos Butler
venue: Mowry Alumni Center, Ohio Wesleyan University
description: Rare Moments exhibit by Barbara Frentsos Butler, Class of 1947, of abstract painting on display in the Mowry alumni Gallery.

name: Exhibit: Fur, Fins, & Feathers
admission: Free July and August. Adults $10. Seniors and students $8. Children under 6 free. Free admission on Sunday
description: Fur, Fins, & Feathers, a family-friendly exhibition about animals in art, showcases works from CMA's permanent collection. This diverse exhibition includes a variety of media and styles such as Innuit stone carvings, wooden African headdresses, contemporary photography, and American folk art prints. Fur, Fins, & Feathers includes many works which visitors may not have seen before. Because the Museum is currently under renovation, CMA can highlight works from our permanent collection that are not normally on view. Enhanced programming related to the exhibition will include hands-on activities, tours, and visits from other community organizations such as Children's Theater and the Columbus Zoo and Aquarium.

name: Exhibit: Picasso at Denison, Steinlen, From Paris to New York
description: This student-researched exhibition of Pablo Picasso prints from the earliest phases of Picasso's career, referred to as his Blue Period (1901 -1904) and Pose Period (1904 - 1906) - reflects the artist's importance to 20th Century art history while celebrating the recent completion of conservation treatment of Denison's print collection. (Picasso at Denison).

name: Exhibit: Photographs by Leigh Rabby
description: Photographs by Leigh Rabby (OWU Class of 1992), in the Alumni Gallery in Mowry Alumni Center.

name: Writers' Group
description: The writers group is a place for writers from beginner to experienced to share their works and receive feedback from others. Bring your most recent work, either complete or in-progress, and talk about where it has been, is, and where it could be. The group is set up as a casual discussion group focusing around writing. We come together to chat about our shared interest in writing and to share our current work with each other. Each writer is encouraged to bring a short fiction/non-fiction sample of work each month. This work can be poetry, prose, or whatever other style of writing you prefer. We normally keep the work short, like a piece that can be shared in 5 to 10 minutes time. If you cannot bring any current work, please bring a short sample of another author's work that inspires you. For first time attendees, we encourage you to bring a few older works that you are proud of to share. It helps the group to get a better idea of what sort of writing you like to do.

name: Downtown Delaware's First Friday Celebration
description: Delaware, Ohio's downtown antique shops, gift boutiques, art galleries, restaurants and other attractions stay open late as part of Main Street Delaware's family-friendly First Friday celebration of the city.

name: 30-Year Ride: Honda's Ohio-Made Motorcycles
admission: Adults $10. Students $3. Seniors $8. Children 11 and under free.
venue: AMA Motorcycle Hall of Fame Museum
description: 30-Year Ride: Honda's Ohio-Made Motorcycles showcases 30 years of significant Honda motorcycles manufactured in Marysville, Ohio.

name: Ohio State Theatre: Breaking Ground: A Play Reading Series
venue: Drake Performance, The Ohio State University
description: Theatre graduate student organization The Syndicate and the Department of Theatre are sponsoring a series of staged readings in conjunction with the 2010 - 2011 main stage season.

name: Extreme Screen Film: Legends of Flight
description: Take the ultimate "flying experience" without leaving the ground on COSI's 7-Story Extreme Screen in the new feature giant screen film, Legends of Flight opening on November 3, 2010. Soar through 100 years of aviation history and the most influential airplanes that have inspired the next generation of airplanes including the Boeing 787 Dreamliner. You'll follow veteran test pilot Capt. Mike Carriker and get a true insider's look at how a modern aircraft is designed and built as well as feel the thrill of flying through a mountain glider, a Stearman bi-plane and the heart pounding excitement of a Harrier Jump Jet.

name: Columbus Food Adventures: Alt Eats Tour
description: Travel the world while without leaving Columbus. This tour's itinerary will introduce you to some of the best ethnic food in the city. We'll experience a taste of Zanzibar, eat Vietnamese sandwiches, sample Somali food, sample some Southern Indian food, and visit a Latino grocery store. Join us in our comfortable 14-passenger van, and learn about the cuisines and cultures of some of Columbus's finest immigrant kitchens.

name: Columbus Food Adventures: Short North Walking Tour
description: Take a leisurely stroll with us through the Short North. Not just an Arts district and home to the Monthly Gallery Hop, the Short North also boasts a wealth of dining and shopping opportunities. The Short North is packed full of boutiques, fine dining and nightlife and this tour is designed to show off some of the best that the Short North and Columbus have to offer.

name: 30-Year Ride: Honda's Ohio-Made Motorcycles
admission: Adults $10. Students $3. Seniors $8. Children 11 and under free.
venue: AMA Motorcycle Hall of Fame Museum
description: 30-Year Ride: Honda's Ohio-Made Motorcycles showcases 30 years of significant Honda motorcycles manufactured in Marysville, Ohio.

name: Shadowbox Live: The Naked Truth
description: Sketch comedy and rock 'n' roll get real this winter with Shadowbox Live's newest show, The Naked Truth. Take a peek behind closed doors where secrets are revealed one whisper at a time. A little racy and raw, The Naked Truth blends reality and fantasy into a comedy cocktail that will leave you begging for more.

name: Shadowbox Live: Love and Lies Lunchbox
description: Whether you let love rule or you live to get away with a little while lie, you'll like Shadowbox Live's newest themed matinee, Love and Lies Lunchbox. This 45-minute teaser will leave you feeling flirty and mischievous: a naughty and nice combination.

name: Geckos: Tails to Toepads
description: Geckos: Tails to Toepads brings leaping lizards to COSI Jan. 18-May 8. With their bulging eyes, sticky toepads and surprisingly squawky voices, these remarkable reptiles can be seen in naturalistic habitats and explored through hands-on activities.

name: Creative Chords II: Group Piano Lessons with Bradley Sowash
description: Build on your piano skills in a fast-faced, fun and creative atmosphere. This course is a continuation of Creative Chords I. However, if you know the basics (reading simple rhythms in treble and bass clef) and would like to start playing again or for the first time, this class is for you! We will cover scales, chords, and learning fake well-known tunes such as "On Top of Old Smokey" and "Twinkle, Twinkle". Text and music are provided with weekly handouts. Practice on a home piano or keyboard is expected.

name: Creative Chords IV: Group Piano Lessons with Bradley Sowash
description: Creative Chords IV is a fun and creative approach to playing pop/jazz lead sheets using common chord patterns, improvising, and personalizing tunes. The instructor will select repertoire based on the desires and ability levels of the participants. Practice on a home piano or keyboard is expected.

name: Orchid Forest
admission: Adults $11. Seniors and students $9. Children $6. Children under 2 free.
description: The Conservatory's Pacific Island Water Garden comes alive with the warmth and color in the midst of winter. Waves of hundreds of colorful, tropical orchids are arranged on arches, descend from trees and complement lush, green foliage. Make a winter escape into the Orchid Forest.

name: Exhibit: Edward Weston: Life Work
address: One College and Main, Columbus, OH 43209
description: This groundbreaking exhibit features an outstanding grouping of vintage prints from all phases of Weston's five-decade career. Previously unpublished masterworks are interspersed with well-known signature images. Works are from the collection of Michael Mattis and Judith Hochberg.

name: Exhibit: Here's Looking At You: New Portraits by Ohio Artists
address: Riffe Center, 77 S. High St., Columbus, OH 43215
description: Curated by Kay Koeninger, the exhibition features 14 Ohio artists who stretch the idea of what a portrait can be. Through their eyes, we see not only the world but ourselves and others in a transformative new light. They are not constrained by a past art form but are energized and profoundly inspired by it, using a variety of mediums - from photography to charcoal to stoneware to acrylic painting - to create unforgettable portraits.

name: Exhibit: Seventh Dream of Teenage Heaven
venue: Columbus College of Art & Design Canzani Center
description: Seventh Dream of Teenage Heaven explores what it means to long for a return to the vitality and glory of an idealized past. While "nostalgia" is often summoned to convey a yearning for the reclamation of something lost, for the return of some bygone era, "saudade" is at times a more appropriate description. Originating in 15th-century Portugal when friends and family were missing at sea or war - but not confirmed dead - saudade lends the sense of possibility, the potential of recovery, the likelihood of seeing them again. It offers a fissure into which the realization of return is there. Hope remains alive and well. With this in mind, Seventh Dream of Teenage Heaven investigates how once-glorified and lyrical pasts - physical, mental, material, and spiritual - can again be claimed in present and future moments.

name: Exhibit: Homage to Bearden: Piecing it Together
description: Romare Bearden (1911-1988), an American artist of African-American heritage, is widely acknowledged as one of the most talented and original visual artists of the twentieth century. Original Romare Bearden works from private collections highlight this exhibition. Selected collage artists from Ohio provide accompanying 2 & 3 - dimensional work.

name: Ohio Statehouse Sesquicentennial
address: Broad St.& High St., Columbus, OH 43215
description: Red, white and blue patriotic bunting will adorn the west columns of the Ohio Statehouse throughout 2011. The bunting will draw attention to the significance of the Statehouse's year-long sesquicentennial celebration. Special events and activities are planned throughout the year.

name: Cocktails at the Conservatory
description: Enjoy the botanically-themed monthly featured cocktail or a full bar selection along with small plate hors d-oeuvres. DJs from Encore Entertainment create the musical ambience beginning at 5:30 p.m. At dusk, the Palm House glows with James Turrell's LED installation, Light Raiment II. $10 minimum at the door: receive $10 tokens for food and beverage.

name: Shadowbox Live: The Naked Truth
description: Sketch comedy and rock 'n' roll get real this winter with Shadowbox Live's newest show, The Naked Truth. Take a peek behind closed doors where secrets are revealed one whisper at a time. A little racy and raw, The Naked Truth blends reality and fantasy into a comedy cocktail that will leave you begging for more.

name: Geckos: Tails to Toepads
description: There are more than 1,000 species of Geckos living across the globe from balmy tropical beaches and lush rainforests to frigid mountain slopes and parched deserts. They range from shadowy nighttime hunters to neon-colored nectar eaters that scamper around in daylight. Welcome to the Gecko's world!

name: HOOT Family Film Series
admission: Free with a suggested donation of a canned good
description: HOOT is a monthly festival of films, music and activities designed for Central Ohio families and children. On the final Saturday of each month, families are invited to enjoy stimulating games, story readings, and music from around the world. The Shazzbots, a popular local kids band, will provide music between short films.

name: Walk With a Doc
address: 9466 Columbus Pike or 1500 Polaris Pkwy., Columbus, OH 43035
venue: Highbanks Metro Park or Polaris Fashion Place
description: Start your Saturday right. Walk with a Doc is free and open to anyone interested in taking steps for their health. Come alone or bring loved ones, and enjoy a rejuvenating walk in the park. Board-certified cardiologist Dr. David Sabgir, other specialists, and additional healthcare professionals can provide support and answer questions. Among the free activities are: blood pressure checks, healthy snacks, recipes and information to make better lifestyle changes, and opportunities to talk with the docs. The walks are held most Saturdays. Please check WalkWithADoc.org to confirm times and locations.

name: Exhibit: Crossing the BLVD: strangers, neighbors, aliens in a new America
description: Come to the OSU Urban Arts Space and see Crossing the BLVD: strangers, neighbors, aliens in a new America. The artists started the project in 1999 when they began conducting workshops for new immigrants to recount their experiences. Eleven years later, Crossing the BLVD has grown into a multifaceted documentation, consisting of an award-winning book, CD, website, performances, public radio documentaries, and traveling exhibition.

name: HOOT Family Film Series
admission: Free with a suggested donation of a canned good
description: HOOT is a monthly festival of films, music and activities designed for Central Ohio families and children. On the final Saturday of each month, families are invited to enjoy stimulating games, story readings, and music from around the world. The Shazzbots, a popular local kids band, will provide music between short films.

name: Echoes in Time Theatre: Protection, Pay and the Long Road to Freedom
description: Listen to the story of one soldier from the United States Colored Troops as he tells how the colored soldier fights for not only the freedom of his race but his own personal to freedom to join the white soldiers fighting the war that threatens to divide the Union.

name: Ohio State Theatre: Othello
venue: Roy Bowen Theatre, The Ohio State University
description: Often called Shakespeare's most intimate tragedy, Othello is a timely play of race, politics, and the marriage bed. A young public figure on the political rise and esteemed general in the service of Venice, Othello has recently wed Desdemona, the daughter of a senator. When he promotes Michael Cassio to be his lieutenant, the brilliant, politically ambitious, and passed over Iago is enraged and plots revenge. Othello aspires to belong to Desdemona's world and instead becomes victim to its bigotry and his own inner demons through Iago's keen psychological manipulation.

name: Anna Deavere Smith: Let Me Down Easy
description: One of the foremost solo theater artists of our time, Anna Deavere Smith pioneered the journalistic style of portraying multiple real-life characters with texts drawn verbatim from her own interviews with her subjects. She now returns with her latest production, Let Me Down Easy, which incisively examines coping with illness, injury, survivorship, and mortality.

name: Ohio State Theatre: Spring's Awakening
venue: Thurber Theatre, The Ohio State University
description: Challenging too many taboos to be performable when first written in the late 19th century, Spring's Awakening was almost universally regarded as brazen pornography. Set in a small German town in the 1890's, adolescent boys and girls grope their way towards knowledge and maturity against the blocks set up by parents and teachers in the name of morality. Melchior, fearless in his pursuit of the truth, manages to retain his freedom of spirit, but his friends are not so lucky or strong.

name: Phoenix Theatre for Children: Charlotte's Web
description: Wilbur must be "Some Pig" because Charlotte, the spider, has written those words in her web. Charlotte's sacrifice for Wilbur proves that she is some spider as well. This classic story has warmed the hearts of audiences for generations.

name: Bring Up the Lights! 2011 CATCO-Phoenix Gala
description: Join us at Franklin Park Conservatory on Saturday, February 26, 2011 for our very first gala as CATCO-Phoenix! As we raise the curtain on our new combined company, we present the gala in a new venue - with all of our usual theatrical flair! The evening begins with cocktails and hors d'oeuvres in the historic Palm House inside the lighting installation Light Raiment II by internationally renowned artist, James Turrell. The party continues with dinner in the Grand Atrium catered by Cameron Mitchell Catering. This intimate space is perfect for mingling with fellow theatre-lovers, catching up with old friends and making new ones. Be among the first to learn about the 2011-12 season, as well as more about our arts partnership and collaboration, in addition to the At-Risk programming in our schools which delivers over 6,000 hours of special courses to kids in need! We're planning a special treat to share with you to highlight the experience and the impact of these leading-edge programs! The evening will conclude with dessert and a live auction themed to CATCO-Phoenix's work in our community.

name: Shadowbox Live: Rent
description: Based on Puccini's opera La Boheme, Rent tells the story of a group of young Bohemians struggling to live and love in modern New York City.

name: Jumpin' Jaks (Jazz and Kids) with Rebecca Ogden, The Music Lady
description: Dance, sing, listen, play, and learn about music- from ragtime to jazz- in a fun and creative environment. Jumpin' Jaks offers preschoolers, ages 3-5 and their parent or caregiver, the opportunity to explore American music in all its forms.

name: A Day of the Arts for All
description: AEO is a statewide, juried, visual arts exhibition and tour promoting inclusive environments and advances those pursuing a creative career. The Opening Ceremony features an exhibition of all the selected art work, more than 90 pieces, and presentation of awards in Youth, Emerging, and Professional categories as well as Best in Show and People's Choice. Following the event, the artwork is divided into tours and travels around Ohio.

name: Buckeye Quarter Midget Racing
description: Buckeye Quarter Midget Racing Association Sponsored Event. This event features indoor quarter midget racing for children 5 to 16 years of age. Bring the whole family out to see this unique and fun event!

name: Jason Aldean w/ Eric Church and JaneDear girls
Chords and Scales to Progressions with Tim Cummiskey
description: Advance your guitar skills in a fun and relaxed environment. Review basic scale theory and chord construction with an end goal of playing American standards and jazz compositions of the 20th century. This is an applied theory class with students learning to play and applying the examples discussed in class.

name: Digital Composition and Recording with James Allison
description: In this class, learn the fundamentals of music composition, and then expand into composition and arrangement for bands, singers, film scores, or commercials. Discussion will also include music marketing, licensing, and ways to get your music heard by others. Students should have basic skills, and understanding of music theory, and have dabbled a bit in songwriting.

name: Intermediate to Advanced Jazz Guitar Concepts, Session II with Tim Cummiskey
description: Continue advancing your skills, from style and technique to theory, while expanding your guitar repertoire. This class is a continuation of the fall session, but new students with advanced skills are welcome.

name: Vocal Ensemble with Rachel Sepulveda
description: Share the fun of singing with other who loves to swing and shout just as much as you do! Explore a wide range of songs and styles, from the Great American Songbook to Motown and a cappella. Participants should be able to recognize and hold pitch and have some basic reading abilities. Some choral/ensemble experience is recommended but not required.

name: Practical Music Theory with Stan Smith
description: Explore scales, harmony, and form in various styles of music to enhance performance, composition, and arranging skills. Directed listening and discussion will round out the class, designed for the student who is interested in strengthening their skills, both in theory and practice.

name: Rock Ensemble with Dennis Hodges
description: Get ready to rock! Rock Ensemble is a hands-on, performance- oriented class with a focus on songs by a variety of artists. Some experience with your instrument is recommended. Guitarist should know bar chords, minor pentatonic scales, and some reading of simple charts/or tab knowledge.

name: All Ears- Using your Ears in Drum Set Performance with Cedric Easton and Ryan Jewell
description: Develop your ears in this drum set class. Great drummers are great listeners who can respond to the many subtleties of the ensemble. Explore a variety of styles, from gospel and funk to pop and rock and roll, and the role of the drum set in the rhythm section.

name: Live Recording with Andrew Dodson of Central City Recording
description: Learn the basics of the live recording process, from running ProTools to setting up a live recording session- the apply what you learned by recording the Vocal Ensemble class at the Jazz Academy. Complete the class by mixing down and mastering the recording.

name: Jason Turner Music Series
description: Wild Goose's Concert series, WGC Presents, returns with some of Columbus' best and brightest rock bands. WGC Presents happens every fourth Wednesday and features local, regional and national artists.

name: Columbus Gay Men's Chorus: Vox: One Hit Wonders
description: You know you love them! Those one hit wonders that creep into your mind and have you humming them all day long. Who sings that song? Who knows, but it's catchy! Join Vox once again at the Columbus Performing Arts Center to take a trip down memory lane and enjoy the talented voices of our auditioned ensemble.

name: Bill Frisell: Not So Fast: The Music of Speedy West and Jimmy Bryant
description: Frisell and Leisz return with bassist Dennis Crouch and drummer Don Heffington to premiere another Wex-commissioned piece that has its origins in a musical introduction from Helm, in this case to the timeless country jazz of pedal steel guitarist Speedy West and his guitar partner, Jimmy Bryant. Although many music fans view jazz and country and western music as rolling on distinctly separate tracks, the two genres have met at many intersections, and Frisell is one of today's most prominent exponents of their melding trajectories. The great Territory bands (regional jazz big bands) of the 1930s and 1940s, like Walter Page's Oklahoma City Blue Devils with Count Basie, had counterparts in such western swing bands as Bob Wills and the Texas Playboys. In the post-WWII period, when big bands were on the wane, small bebop combos were on the rise with players trading fast phrases in intricate and harmonically complex tunes. At the same time, compact groups of pickers like Speedy West and Jimmy Bryant in California crafted equally virtuosic instrumental interplay with lightning-quick licks and cleverly nimble compositional turns.

name: Jazz On The Avenue: Jazz in Motion
description: This concert will feature Columbus-born Bobby Pierce currently residing in Los Angeles and Columbus' own Bobby Floyd striking the keys harmoniously in this "one-of-a-kind" evening of "up-tempo" jazz music you do not want to miss! A procession of music from pianos to organs will synthesize your senses.

name: Six String Concerts: Danny Schmidt and Carrie Elkin
The Columbus Symphony: Schubert's Unfinished
description: Guest conductor Gunther Herbig will lead the Columbus Symphony in a program featuring a trio of composers from the Romantic and Classical periods. The program will include Mozart's Symphony No. 36 ("Linz"), Schubert's Symphony No. 8 ("Unfinished"), and Dvorak's Symphony No. 8. WOSU's Christopher Purdy will hold a free, pre-concert lecture about the program for ticket holders one hour prior to each performance on the fourth floor of the Ohio Theatre's Galbreath Pavilion.

name: Women in Music Columbus: Sundays at the Huntington
description: A recital presented by members of Women in Music Columbus featuring the Sonora Trio (Erica Donahoe, violin, Linda Bollas, cello, and Laura Flowers Benson, piano). Elizabeth Fleisher, piano, Lisa Imondi, jazz singer, and Cynthia Mahaney, soprano.

name: 16th Annual All Mopar Winter Swap Meet
description: Ohio's Largest one day indoor Mopar only swap meet and outdoor car corral.

name: Central Ohio Home & Garden Show
admission: Adults $10. Children 12 and under free. Parking $5.
description: Wander through fragrant lush, full-size gardens in the dead of winter at the Central Ohio Home & Garden Show. The show was recently honored with the highly prestigious "Show of the Year," awarded by the National Association of Consumer Shows. The Central Ohio Home & Garden Show is renowned for its breathtaking live gardens. The show is the region's most exciting and interactive home and garden show, featuring more than 400 exhibits and attractions.

name: Exhibit: Shared Intelligence: American Painting and the Photograph
admission: Adults $10. Seniors and students $8. Children under 6 free. Free admission on Sunday
description: Inspired by the Georgia O'Keeffe Museum Research Center's 2006 3-day symposium, Painting and Photography in American Art: Sources, Ideas and Influences, 1890s to the Present, this exhibition of 75 paintings and photographs explores the productive and fraught relationship of these two mediums in American modern art that has been ongoing since the last decades of the 19th century. It focuses on the work of painters for whom photography has been essential, among them Robert Bechtle, Chuck Close, Thomas Eakins, Audrey Flack, David Hockney, Georgia O'Keeffe, Ben Shahn, Charles Sheeler, and Andy Warhol. This traveling exhibition also includes works from CMA such as our Norman Rockwell and Kehinde Wiley.

name: Benjamin Duke and Tony Shumski
venue: ROY G BIV Gallery for Emerging Artists
description: ROY G BIV Gallery is proud to present the work of Benjamin Duke and Tony Shumski. This exhibition featuring large-scale painting and photography.

name: The Texas Chair Project by Damian Priour
description: The Texas Chair Project by Damian Priour features miniature chairs in a variety of media by 80 artists. Coordinated by Texas artist Damian Priour, the project's only requirement was that each chair fit inside an 8x8x8-inch box. Materials used to create the chairs include clay, felt, bronze, buttons, buttons, lead, and twigs, even sawdust.

name: Exhibit: Upper Arlington Middle Schools
description: Enjoy works by students creating art in our schools. Students from Hastings, Jones, St. Agatha, St. Andrew, and Wellington share their artworks in the Concourse Gallery.

name: Black History Month at the Ohio Statehouse
address: Broad St.& High St., Columbus, OH 43215
description: The Ohio Statehouse will celebrate Black History Month throughout February with a special display, free historical performances each Tuesday at noon and special tours of the George Washington Williams Room. Visitors can also enjoy a special soul food menu at the Capitol Cafe each Wednesday in February.

name: Black Tie Blue Jackets Style Show
description: For the fifth consecutive year, Columbus Blue Jackets players and their wives and girlfriends, along with local pediatric cancer heroes, will model the latest fashions in a charity style show to benefit the fight against pediatric cancer.

description: The Catholic Women's conference is a one day event whose mission is to provide opportunities for women to deepen their relationship with Jesus Christ, to grow in their realization of their dignity as women and to strengthen their commitment to be a disciple of Christ. This year's speakers will include Teresa Tomeo, Dr. Pia de Solenni and Deacon Michael Gaitley, MIC.   Schedule: 7:30-8:30 Registration; 8:30-9:30 Mass with Bishop Campbell; 9:30-9:45 Reconciliation Talk; 9:45-10:45 Reconciliation and Breakfast; 10:45-11:45 Teresa Tomeo; 11:45-12:45 Dr. Pia de Solenni; 12:45-2:00 Lunch; 2:00-3:00 Fr. Michael Gaitley; 3:00 Chaplet of Divine Mercy and Closing Prayer

name: Hawaiian Luau
description: The John F. Wolfe Palm House will be transformed into a tropical paradise with family activities, island themed food and drink, and two performances by the Canal Winchester High School's Steel Drum Band.

name: Mid American Exotic Bird Society - 18th Annual Bird Fair
description: Pet owners, Breeders, and Bird Fanciers come see the 18th Annual Bird Fair. In addition to birds from across the country, the show includes a number of vendors who sell bird-related items such as toys, play gyms, cages, seeds, vitamins, tee shirts, diets, treats, birds, and more at bird fair prices! Hourly raffles! Angel the performing Cockatoo will be present as always!   The special guest speaker this year will be Dr. Jamie Lindstrom at 12pm and secondly Elise at 1pm who will give a lecture on Basic Bird Care for the Younger Bird Owner.

name: Anna Deavere Smith: Listening to America
description: MacArthur fellow and Pulitzer Prize nominee Anna Deavere Smith has said, "I try to embody America by embodying its words." The development of Smith's solo production Let Me Down Easy allowed the artist to observe health care in America from a variety of perspectives, including those of patients, doctors, policymakers, and pastors. From over 300 extensive interviews, Smith created a series of poignant portraits of individuals confronting serious illness, mortality, and a complex healthcare system. Join us for a conversation with Smith, Steven G. Gabbe, MD, CEO of OSU's Medical Center and prominent legal scholar Patricia Williams, about the process of creating Let Me Down Easy and the past, present, and future of medical care in the United States.

name: Columbus' 199th Birthday Party
description: Do you LOVE Columbus? If your answer is YES, then join CHS in celebrating Columbus' 199th Birthday. Mark your 2011 calendar. Columbus Historical Society will also be honoring an individual, organization and company with the prestigious Lucus Sullivant Gift Award in recognition of their contribution to the great city of Columbus.

name: The Flight of Tulugaq (O Voo de Tulugaq)
description: Seen against the Alaskan wilderness sky, two ravens emerge from a flock and engage in a spontaneous ballet of gravity-defying twists, turns, and plunges.

name: February Family Films: African American Books to Movies
description: The February Family Film Series will have 4 films on Thursday's in honor of Black History Month. The packages will include refreshments and allow for dialogue after each film. Community facilitators and/or local Media personalities that are experts in their field will lead the dialogue either by knowledge or interest.

name: Thurber House Evenings With Authors: Paula McLain
description: Join Thurber House and Paula McLain for a reading and discussion of her latest book, The Paris Wife (fiction). A beautifully evocative story told in the voice of Ernest Hemingway's first wife, Hadley. Familiar real-life characters such as F. Scott and Zelda Fitzgerald, Gertrude Stein, Ezra Pound provide the vivid background to this story of love and betrayal.

name: Ohio State University Ice Hockey vs. Ferris State
venue: Value City Arena at the Jerome Schottenstein Center

name: Columbus Blue Jackets vs. Phoenix Coyotes
Ohio State University Ice Hockey vs. Ferris State
venue: Value City Arena at the Jerome Schottenstein Center

name: Ohio State University Men's Basketball vs. Indiana
venue: Value City Arena at the Jerome Schottenstein Center

name: Ohio State University Women's Basketball vs. Wisconsin
venue: Value City Arena at the Jerome Schottenstein Center

name: Shadowbox Live: Love and Lies Lunchbox
description: Whether you let love rule or you live to get away with a little while lie, you'll like Shadowbox Live's newest themed matinee, Love and Lies Lunchbox. This 45-minute teaser will leave you feeling flirty and mischievous: a naughty and nice combination.

name: Shen Yun Performing Arts
description: Experience the beauty and grandeur of China's 5,000-year history with Shen Yun Performing Arts. Portraying ancient legends and modern tales of courage, compassion, and grace through exhilarating and uplifting music and dance performances, Shen Yun has delighted audiences over 100 cities across five continents. Over 800,000 live audience members have witnessed the incredible talents of more than 100 gifted Shen Yun dancers and musicians.

name: Actors' Theatre: Trojan Women
description: This production will be co-directed by John S. Kuhn and Janetta Davis. Carolin Hanhnemann, Chair of the Classics Department at Kenyon College, will be serving as dramaturg. Trojan Women is a searing look at the aftermath of the Trojan War. This classic Greek play explores the tragedy of war and asks the question, "What happens to the innocent victims?"

name: Center Stage Players: Rent
description: Jonathan Larson's Pulitzer-prize winning Broadway musical based loosely on Puccini's opera La Boheme. It follows a year in the lives of seven friends living the disappearing Bohemian lifestyle in New York's East Village. AIDS and both its physical and emotional complications pervade the lives of Roger, Mimi, Tom, and Angel; Maureen deals with her chronic infidelity through performance art; her partner, Joanne, wonders if their relationship is worth the trouble; Benjamin has sold out his Bohemian ideals in exchange for a hefty income and is on the outs with his former friends; and Mark, an aspiring filmmaker, feels like an outsider to life in general, always behind the camera recording the events but never playing a part.

name: I Love You, You're Perfect, Now Change
description: This musical celebration of the mating game takes on the truths and myths behind that contemporary conundrum known as the relationship. Act I explores the journey from dating and waiting to love and marriage. Act II reveals the agonies and triumphs of in-laws, newborns, trips in the family car and pick-up techniques of the geriatric set. This hilarious revue pays tribute to those who have loved and lost; to those who have fallen on their face at the portal of romance; to those who have dared to ask, Say, what are you doing Saturday night?

name: Mike Epps with Sheryl Underwood
description: From the big screen to the stage - get ready for Mike Epps! Comedian and actor Mike Epps has generated quite a buzz among his peers and within the industry for being one of the funniest comedic actors emerging in the Hollywood spotlight.

name: CAPA: The Second City's Fair and Unbalanced
description: Chicago's legendary comedy theatre just celebrated its 50th anniversary, and their alumni list reads like a who's who of American comedy - Alan Arkin, Joan Rivers, Robert Klein, Peter Boyle, John Belushi, Dan Aykroyd, Bill Murray, Gilda Radner, Martin Short, John Candy, Bonnie Hunt, Julia Louis-Dreyfus, Chris Farley, Mike Myers, Steve Carell, Tina Fey, and countless others. The Second City 's Fair & Unbalanced takes unbridled, comic pleasure in the foibles of our politicians, celebrities, and even our significant others. No institution escapes the satiric eye of The Second City - from the blowhards of the Beltway to the Hollywood elite.

name: Echoes in Time Theatre: Victoria Woodhull: I Decline To Stand Up as the Frightful Example
description: According to her contemporaries, Victoria Woodhull was a woman 100 years ahead of her time. Although few have heard of her today, she was one of the most famous women in the country when she ran for president of the United States in 1872. She advocated many things taken for granted today: the 8-hour work day, graduated income tax, social welfare programs and profit sharing, for example. Listen as Victoria expounds on her views.

name: A Midsummer Night's Dream
description: Presented as part of OSU's partnership with the Royal Shakespeare Company's "Stand up for Shakespeare" initiative, this 60-minute abridged version is intended to introduce young audiences to the joys of Shakespeare and his language. A Midsummer Night's Dream is a lighthearted comedy of love, magic, and mayhem that follows the adventures of two young couples, a bumbling troupe of actors, and mischievous fairies.

name: Terminus by Mark O'Rowe
venue: Thurber Theatre, The Ohio State University
description: As the National Theatre of Ireland, Abbey Theatre in Dublin has a long and distinguished track record of supporting promising talent and daring new productions. Playwright Mark O'Rowe, who first gained wide attentions as the writer of the hit play Howie the Rookie and the cult film Intermission, is a case in point. His lyrical and lacerating poetic language soars through the visceral show TERMINUS.

name: Columbus Children's Theatre: Stuart Little
description: This is the endearing classic tale about a mouse named Stuart Little who is born into an ordinary New York family. Everyone around Stuart liked him very much -- except for Snowbell the cat. Aside from the usual things a mouse would dislike about New York City, Snowbell was at the top of Stuart's list because it was Snowbell who frightened away his dear friend, Margalo. And this is where Stuart's adventure really begins. At the age of seven he sets out into the world to find his friend and a little bit of himself also.

name: International Performing Arts for Families: Baobab
description: The striking masks and puppetry of this tale based on West African storytelling traditions captivate the young and the young at heart. Baobab tells of a baobab tree that stands watch over a drought-stricken village and of a little boy who goes on a quest filled with challenges and excitement. This show also features incredible live music played on traditional African instruments. For ages 4 and up.

name: Joseph and the Amazing Techicolor Dreamcoat
Gallery Players: Curtains
description: The winter musical is Curtains, written by Rupert Holmes, with music by John Kander and lyrics by Fred Ebb. Curtains, based on the original book and concept by Peter Stone, is a send-up of backstage murder mystery plots. Set in 1959 Boston, the play follows the fallout when an untalented star is murdered during her opening night curtain call. Can a police detective who moonlights as a musical theater fan save the show, solve the case, and maybe even find love before the show reopens, without getting himself killed?

name: Broadway Across America: Les Miserables
description: Cameron Mackintosh presents a brand new 25th anniversary production of Boublil & Schonberg's legendary musical, Les Miserables, with glorious new staging and spectacular reimagined scenery inspired by the paintings of Victor Hugo. This new production has already been acclaimed by critics, fans and new audiences and is breaking box office records wherever it goes.

name: Shadowbox Live: Fantasies
description: This spring, escape reality and enter a realm with no boundaries with Shadowbox Live's newest themed show Fantasies. Deliciously delusional original sketch comedy and rock 'n' roll prove that in Fantasies anything is possible.

name: Theatre Daedalus: Caught in the Act Again
description: Theatre Daedalus is thrilled to present our second annual fundraising event, Caught in the Act Again, an evening of short plays conceived, written, and performed within 48 hours. More than three dozen theatre artists will gather from around the country - scripts will be written overnight and the top plays will be selected and staged in the culmination of this exciting weekend!

name: CATCO: What the Butler Saw
description: A psychiatric clinic becomes a comic carnival of chaos as mistaken identities, attempted seductions, red herrings, lost relatives, and political intrigues explode in this classic British sex farce.

name: Gregory Maqoma and Shanell Winlock: Southern Bound Comfort
description: This special pair of duets with live music features award-winning dancers Gregory Maqoma and Shanell Winlock. Maqoma, artistic director of the internationally recognized Vuyani Dance Theatre, recently choreographed the opening event of the World Cup in South Africa. Also from Johannesburg, Winlock is now based in London, where she is celebrated for her work with Akram Khan's company. Maqoma's piece, Southern Comfort, looks at how perceived ideas shape human experience. A reflection of behavior, attitudes, and reactions, this humorous and passionate piece features highly charged partnering with whiplash turns. It peels back the fragile veneer of appearances that conceal the power games people play.

name: Ohio Indoor Kart Series
admission: $15. children (7 to 11): $6, Kids under 7 admitted free
description: Indoor professional go-kart racing on a 1/10-mile concrete oval track located inside the O'Neill Building. Fun for the entire family.

name: Preschool Zone! Greens (ages 3-5)
description: Winter greens are so sweet and tasty that even veggie-averse kids will be tempted to taste the green monster smoothie, kale chips, and pesto we cook up in this vitamin rich class.

name: PBJ & Jazz Concert: Liquid Crystal Project
description: PBJ & Jazz concerts are 1-hour long interactive concerts designed to introduce jazz and American music to young children and their families. Featuring some of Columbus' finest musicians and ensembles, PBJ & Jazz concerts are hosted by former Columbus Music Hall owner and retired music educator Rebecca Ogden and are a great introduction to live music for the youngest audience member.

name: St. Patrick's Day Celebration
description: Come to Dublin, Ohio on the greenest weekend of the year! Bring the entire family to stay and play on Saturday, March 12th and enjoy our annual St. Patrick's Day Celebration. It includes a pancake breakfast and a miles-long community parade filled with bands, leprechauns, floats and all-things-Irish. Then, spend some time exploring the Historic District hopping for Irish imports, taking in some Celtic entertainment, sipping an Irish tea, tasting some scones or Irish potato chowder and having fun!

name: African Mask Making Workshop
description: Artist and Education Director Todd Camp explore meaning and the beauty of regional African masks through a slide show and discussion. Participants will be presented with a variety of recycled materials including: plastics, wood scraps, beads, fabric, and paint from which to choose. Everyone will take home a wonderful creation and new insight on African masks. This fun filled workshop is for 3rd-6th graders.

name: Blooms & Butterflies
admission: Adults $11. Seniors and students $9. Children $6. Children under 2 free.
description: Experience the emergence of exotic butterflies and watch their release into the Franklin Park Conservatory's Pacific Island Water Garden. Dozens of species from around the world take flight and feed on tropical blooms. The Butterfly Emergence Center and hands-on activities interpret the butterfly's life cycle are featured.

name: Kid Only Zone! Mexican Night (ages 8-12)
description: Build-your-own burritos, "Chipotle-style." Kids will prepare all the components to fill the burritos, then sit down to a meal together while you enjoy some time off!

name: The Revolve Tour
description: Awesome music, real-life stories, drama, and a ton of fun combine for a high-energy, inspirational, encouraging 2-day weekend event for teen girls! At The Revolve Tour, we understand what teens dream about but we also know that God's plan for their lives is bigger and better than even they can imagine. Our Dream On tour is designed to inspire girls to put their dreams in God's hands.

name: Baby Bonanza & Kid's Expo
admission: Adults $4. Grandparents $3. Children 12 and under free.
description: The Baby Bonanza and Kid's Expo is Ohio's largest and premier maternity, baby and kid's expo! Now in its 5th year, the award-winning Baby Bonanza and Kid's Expo specifically focuses on expectant parents and those families with children up to 10 years of age. Consumers are attracted from all over the state of Ohio and beyond.

name: Beco's Birthday
description: Coco and Phoebe's bouncing baby boy is turning 2 years old! Experience this one of a kind birthday party and see what special presents the Zoo gives their 1300 lb bundle of joy. Bring the family and celebrate with us!

name: Ohio Cattlemen's Association - Ohio Beef Expo
description: Hosted the third weekend in March each year, the Ohio Beef Expo is Ohio's premier beef industry event. This is the 24th anniversary of the Ohio Beef Expo. Ranked as the ninth largest event hosted in Central Ohio, Expo attracts over 25,000 attendees annually. This year's event will feature seven breed sales, ten breed shows, and one of the biggest junior shows in the state. The centerpiece of the Expo, the trade show, boasts over 100 vendors from 13 states. Exhibitors in this year's trade show represent all segments of the industry from cattle handling equipment to show supplies, clothing to feed, genetics, and novelty items, and much, much more

name: Pete Yorn with special guest Ben Kweller
Jazz Arts Group's Inside Track: Chris Thomas King
description: Initially known for his audacious fusion of blues and hip-hop, Chris Thomas King reached a whole new audience starring in and scoring music for the Coen Brothers film O Brother, Where Art Thou?, not only appearing on the award-winning soundtrack, but establishing himself as a serious dramatic actor as well. King has continued to act in and score motion pictures including the Oscar winning Ray. King has also written and recorded more than 150 songs that are in demand for license to motion pictures, documentaries and television programs. The new album Sketches of Treme, is Chris Thomas King's first full-length studio album since the release of the Handy nominated Rise, in 2006. The tour will feature these new songs as well as fan favorites including songs from the movies Ray and O Brother.

name: Lady Gaga
venue: Value City Arena at the Jerome Schottenstein Center

name: Jazz it up! - Basie, Buddy & Benny
description: Enjoy live jazz from one of the world's finest big bands, the Columbus Jazz Orchestra. Led by Artistic Director Byron Stripling, the former lead trumpeter and soloist with the Count Basie Orchestra, the CJO presents more than 40 concerts each season. Take a backstage tour of the majestic Southern Theatre before the concert and meet Byron after the show.

name: Women in Music Columbus: Music For a While
description: Tyler Wayne Smith, countertenor singing Bach, Handel, Schubert, Brahms, Strauss, and Jake Heggie's humorous Countertenor's Conundrum.

name: City Music: Altan
description: No Irish traditional band in the last dozen years has had a wider impact on audiences and music lovers throughout the world. "Under no circumstances should they be missed in concert" - Irish Echo

name: Early Music in Columbus: The Early Interval
address: 1 College and Main St., Columbus, OH 43209

name: The Columbus Symphony: Verdi Requiem
description: A passionate setting of the Requiem mass that spans the heights and depths of musicality, this  is a piece with operatic drama evoking the awesome power of the last judgment.

name: Chamber Music Columbus: Brentano String Quartet
description: Since its inception in 1992, The Brentano String Quartet has been singled out for its technical brilliance, musical insight, and stylistic elegance. Since 1999, the Brentano has had the honor of being the first-ever ensemble-in-residence at Princeton University .

name: ProMusica Chamber Orchestra: Mozart and More
description: Goulding will perform Mozart's "Violin Concerto No. 5" and Vaughan Williams' "The Lark Ascending." Additionally, the concert will include Bach's "Orchestra Suite No. 1 in C Major" and Faure's "Pavane."

name: Six String Concerts: Richard Shindell with Nels Andrews
ProMusica Chamber Orchestra: Mozart and More
description: Goulding will perform Mozart's "Violin Concerto No. 5" and Vaughan Williams' "The Lark Ascending." Additionally, the concert will include Bach's "Orchestra Suite No. 1 in C Major" and Faure's "Pavane."

name: Spicy Salsa Tuesdays
description: JC Entertainment invites you to experience a great night of Latin dancing at the newly remodeled Mynt Ultralounge, come and try out Mynt's brand new and spacious WOOD dance floor! Dancers you will have an absolute blast!

name: Columbus Jazz Orchestra: Basie, Buddy & Benny
description: Jazz royalty takes center stage as the CJO celebrates Count Basie, Buddy Rich and the King of Swing, Benny Goodman. As the drummer for the world-famous Count Basie orchestra and Mel Torme, Butch Miles quickly became renowned for his swinging big band style and fiery technique. One of jazz's top clarinetists of the past 30 years and an equally skilled tenor-saxophonist, Ken Peplowski has been an important force in keeping swing alive and vital. Join Byron and company as we celebrate the three Bs of jazz! The Columbus Youth Jazz Orchestra (CYJO) is proud to perform prior to Sunday's afternoon matinee at 1 p.m.

name: Music in the Atrium: John Sherman
description: Celebrate Saint Patrick's Day with masterful Celtic guitarist John Sherman.

name: Columbus Gay Men's Chorus: Musicians in Harmony
description: ProMusica, Columbus Gay Men's Chorus and Columbus Children's Choir come together to present this special weekend event on March 18 and 19 at the Lincoln Theatre.

name: New Albany Symphony: Beethoven's Triple Concerto and Season Gala
venue: Jeanne B. McCoy Community Center for the Arts
description: Join us for our season finale and be inspired by this triple treat! We welcome to the stage a family of musical talent performing Beethoven's Triple Concerto, Maestro Luis G. Biava on cello, his wife Ariane Sletner on violin, his aunt Blanca Uribe on piano, and his father Luis O. Biava on the podium.

name: The Columbus Symphony: Bolero
description: Conducted by CSO Music Director Jean-Marie Zeitouni and featuring guest pianist Katherine Chi, the program will include Stravinsky's Jeu de cartes, Prokofiev's Piano Concerto No. 1, Messiaen's Oiseaux exotiques, and Ravel's Bolero.

name: Central Ohio Symphony: March Concert
description: The 120 voices of the Capriccio! Choir, OWU Choral Art Society and guest soloists will fill the stage for one of the most popular works of the 20th century: Carl Orff's fabulous 'Carmina Burana'. Also on the program is John Williams' Harry Potter suite, recently voted favorite piece of classical music by young adults.

name: Women in Music Columbus: Sundays at the Huntington
description: This concert will feature the winners of the Young Artists' String Competition and the winners of the Scholarship Competition. Both competitions are sponsored by Women in Music Columbus. The Young Artists' String Competition is for young people up through high school. The Scholarship Competition is for college music majors both undergraduate and graduate.

name: Kitchen Fundamentals: Cupcake Decorating 101
description: Learn basic cupcake decorating techniques using butter cream and royal icing. For $5, take home a pastry bag & tip set.

name: From the Pubs of Ireland Candlelight Dinner
description: Enjoy a hearty Irish pub meal followed by a rollicking evening of Irish melodies, humorous drinking songs and a wee bit of Irish wit and wisdom, all by the Ohio Village Singers. Advance reservations required by March 7.

name: Meatless Meals
description: Whether eating meatless on lenten Fridays or just looking to reduce your intake of saturated fat, this class will introduce you to a few new recipes to include in your meatless menus, including Black Bean Lasagna, Seafood Risotto, and Tofu & Pineapple Fried Rice. Featuring Laura Robertson Boyd.

name: St. Patrick's Day Re-invented!
description: Forget Corned Beef and Cabbage in the crock pot, these recipes are great for a St. Patrick's Day get-together. Included will be a sampling of local beers from Columbus Brewery. Menu: Ploughman's Platter, Dubliner Stuffed Chicken Breasts with Beer Braised Cabbage, Black and Tan Mac 'N' Cheese, Pint of Stout Cake. Featuring Chef Meghan Morris.

name: Charcuterie/Smoking
description: Charcuterie is the act of curing meat by salt, smoke, or dehydration. Home cooks will learn how to apply these concepts to their cooking to delicious effect. Participants will enjoy a light meal featuring cured meat and stuffed sausage to take home. Featuring Rachel Tayse Baillieul.

name: Seeds to Grow and Eat!
description: Seeds, the starting germ of a plant, can be eaten, sown, or sprouted. We will explore all three options in this family workshop. We will cook three snacks from seeds and create an indoor herb garden to take home. Featuring Rachel Tayse Baillieul.

name: Winter Concert
venue: Sullivant Theatre, The Ohio State University
description: Undergraduate and Graduate Contemporary Dance Choreography.

name: BalletMet Open Rehearsal
description: These open rehearsals provide a glimpse into the creative process and a sneak peek of an upcoming production. After the rehearsal, guests can participate in a question and answer session with the artists.

name: Columbus Dance Theatre: Courage
description: Courage, a new evening length work by Tim Veach will highlight the month of March. This collaborative, multi-media work will feature an original score for string quartet by Carpe Diem member Korine Fujiwara. The work confronts what it means to be courageous in the face of fear, injustice, and the unknown.

name: BalletMet: BalletMet Up Close
description: Step into spring with the action-packed BalletMet Up Close, in the BalletMet Performance Space. Audiences will feel the energy and intensity of movement and watch the dancers power through the diverse mix of new works from guest choreographers and BalletMet dancer Jimmy Orrante, plus Harrison McEldowney's hilarious Group Therapy.

name: DanceAfrica!
description: Back by Popular Demand: DanceAfrica embodies tradition, as well as a spirit of change and growth reaching back into the past and forward into the future, embracing the links between cultures across the African Diaspora, always bearing the message, "Peace, love, and respect for everybody!" Dr. Charles "Chuck" Davis, founder and Artistic Director of the African American Dance Ensemble will perform magic with local dancers and rhythms deeply rooted in the traditions of Africa.

name: Dance & Drum Workshop with Thiossane West African Dance Institute
description: Workshop includes a warm up, instruction of basic movement and introduction of dance origins that will provide an opportunity to understand the language of the drum as it relates to the techniques.

name: Columbus International Auto Show
description: More than 448,000 visitors came to the auto show last year. See what's new in the auto industry and the hottest cars around.

name: SPACE - Small Press & Alternative Comics Expo
description: The Midwest's largest exhibition of small press, alternative and creator-owned comics will have more than 180 exhibitors.

name: Memories Scrapbooking Expo
description: Public event for scrap bookers, rubber stampers and paper crafters. Shopping, classes, make-and-takes, demos, crop parties and prizes. Lots of fun for the entire family.

name: Exhibit: Upper Arlington High School
description: Enjoy works by students creating art in our schools. Students at Upper Arlington High School and Wellington bring their artwork for visitors to view in the Concourse Gallery.

name: Exhibit: Expression: Colors of Spring
description: March is Multiple Sclerosis Awareness Month in Ohio. As an effort to rise awareness about the disease and the people it affects Akrona Galleries will be hosting an art exhibit by artists living with MS and their family members.

name: Exhibit: Forever Free: Abraham Lincoln's Journey to Emancipation
description: Why did a nation founded on ideals of freedom and equality tolerate for so long one of the harshest labor systems the world has known? A traveling exhibition looks for answers to this question by tracing Abraham Lincoln's gradual transformation from an antislavery moderate into "The Great Emancipator," who began the process to free all slaves with a revolutionary war-time proclamation in 1863. The Forever Free exhibit offers Ohioans an opportunity to learn more about how the long and brutal Civil War influenced Abraham Lincoln's decision on emancipation of the slaves. The exhibit reveals how Lincoln's values and beliefs guided him through the greatest moral conflict of his time to become one of our greatest Presidents.

name: Exhibit: Gene Friley: All about Evenatom
description: Professor Emeritus Eugene Friley, The Ohio State University class of 1947 (BFA) and class of 1949 (MFA), taught in the ceramics program for more than 40 years. He entered OSU in 1939 and became a ceramic engineering major, but placed his studies on hold to serve in the Air Force as a B-29 bombardier in World War II-Pacific Theatre. After the war, he returned to OSU, finished his degrees as a ceramic art major and joined the faculty. Friley's studio work includes ceramics, drawing, painting, public art and garden sculptures. With innovative uses of ceramic materials, figurative forms and playful organic designs, nature's presence abounds in his art. All about Evenatom features thematic reliefs and ceramic sculptures with explorations of diverse and compelling subjects, such as black holes and Einstein's formula.

name: Exhibit: Image-Self: Ardine Nelson
description: Department of Art Professor and 2008 Guggenheim Fellow Ardine Nelson developed a collaborative project with 23 students that address the question, How does one understand self through image? Throughout the summer and fall Nelson created large-scale formal studio portraits of students. Each student was given a copy of her portrait, and full liberty to alter it-in any manner she chose-to more fully and corporeally capture and reflect her understanding of self. Support provided by the Department of Women's Studies and the Coca-Cola Critical Difference for Women Research on Women, Gender and Gender Equity Grant.

name: Exhibit: Double Sexus: Hans Bellmer and Louise Bourgeois
description: This two-gallery presentation marks the U.S. debut of a major exhibition from Berlin, Germany, that explores connections and contrasts between two influential and historically significant artists. Louise Bourgeois (1911-2010), a famed sculptor who received the Wexner Prize in 1999, and Hans Bellmer (1902-1975), a German sculptor and photographer often associated with surrealism, are both noted for their investigations of sexuality, desire, gender, and the body. Featuring sculpture, photography, and works on paper, the show examines their expressive approaches to these provocative topics. Organized by the Nationalgalerie, Berlin, in cooperation with the Wexner Center.

name: Exhibit: Nathalie Djurberg
description: Nathalie Djurberg is a Swedish-born installation artist who dramatizes feminist and psychoanalytic concerns using claymation video, music, and sculpture. She often uses all three in concert to create immersive gallery environments. Her carefully crafted animation and painterly use of color infuse her sculptures and films with a peculiar beauty that frames her psychic explorations.

name: Exhibit: Pipilotti Rist
description: The renowned Swiss artist - a pioneer of using moving images in installation art - makes her solo debut in Columbus with a new site-specific project for one gallery. Her recent videos are driven by her interest in the transformative power of color. Often filled with whimsy, they toe the line between fantasy and reality. She makes the commonplace seem expected and fascinating by taking familiar subjects, such as the body, and divorcing them from traditional representations through her manipulation of color. Her videos and installations create wholly familiar yet strangely sensual environs. Her project for the Wexner Center will use her recent ideas as a platform for a wholly new work.

name: Arnold Sports Festival
address: 400 N. High St., 200 W. Nationwide Blvd., 405 Neil Ave. and 300 W. Broad St., Columbus, OH 43215
admission: $15 EXPO ticket or $10 in advance. An EXPO ticket provides admission to Fitness EXPO and most sport events.
venue: Greater Columbus Convention Center, Nationwide Arena, The LC, Veterans Memorial
description: The Arnold Sports Festival, co-produced by California Governor Arnold Schwarzenegger and Jim Lorimer, is the largest multi-sport festival in the nation. The March 3-6 event will attract an estimated 175,000 attendees to see nearly 18,000 athletes competing in 45 sports and events, including 12 Olympic sports. The Arnold Fitness EXPO, a highlight of the festival, takes place at the Greater Columbus Convention Center. It features more than 700 exhibit booths offering the latest in fitness apparel, equipment, training tools, nutrition and entertainment. New to the festival in 2011 are an IFBB sanctioned Bikini International competition, the Arnold Sports Film Festival, the Arnold Track and Field Championships, the Arnold Hockey Challenge, and the Ultimate Teen Challenge, a weightlifting event.

name: Arnold Sports Film Festival
description: The Arnold Sports Film Festival will be held March 4-6, 2011 in Columbus, Ohio, in conjunction with the Arnold Sports Festival. The Arnold Sports Film Festival will be committed to the discovery, nurture and presentation of the best short-form international filmmaking focused on personal athletic endeavor. The ASFF will complement and extend the largest multi-sport event in the world, which was founded in 1989 by California Gov. Arnold Schwarzenegger. Filmmakers of all ages will be invited to submit films less than 15 minutes in length to the ASFF in a variety of categories including narrative, documentary, animated, and broadcast films. The films should explore the lives, efforts, inspirations, and hopes of people striving for achievement in individual athletic pursuits ranging from bodybuilding to boxing, gymnastics to judo, table tennis to weightlifting, grappling to skateboarding.

name: Art At The Arnold
description: A three day drawing and painting competition using athletes as models and The Arnold Sports Festival as a backdrop! Cash prizes will be awarded for the best art produced during this three day event.

name: City Wide Talent Showcase : Best Ever
Short North Gallery Hop
address: North High Street from Goodale Boulevard to Fifth Avenue, Columbus, OH 43201
description: The first Saturday of every month, thousands of visitors converge on the strip, the epicenter of the High Street experience. They come to celebrate art and partake in an evening of sights, sounds, food, shopping, and cosmopolitan fun. Countless art experiences. District specials. Prize drawings. Ramped up entertainment. Unexpected surprises. Join us for an unforgettable experience.

name: Columbus RV Supershow
description: The Columbus RV Supershow presented by Airstream takes place March 11-13 in the Celeste Center and Lausche Building. Shake off that cabin fever and dream about warmer weather when you come out to the Columbus RV Supershow! See hundreds of the latest recreational vehicles, including Pop-Up campers, Van Conversions, Travel Trailers, Fifth Wheels, and Motorhomes.

name: Kobie Boykins
venue: Jeanne B. McCoy Community Center for the Arts
description: A dynamic young engineer at NASA's Jet Propulsion Laboratory, Kobie Boykins is on the frontline of Mars exploration. Boykins designed the solar arrays that power the remarkable Mars Expedition Rovers, Spirit and Opportunity, which continue to send back data from our nearest planetary neighbor more than six years after being deployed. He is currently working at NASA's Mars Science Laboratory, preparing the actuators for the next mission. Boykins' other projects have included work on the Mars Pathfinder mission and the Ocean Surface Topography Mission, taking measurements by satellite of the Earth's oceans.

name: Ohio Deer and Turkey Expo
description: Target Communications Corp presents the 19th annual Ohio Deer & Turkey Expo March 18-20. The state turkey calling championship will be Saturday in the DiSalle Center Auditorium. All seminars during the Ohio Deer & Turkey Expo are free after you have purchased a general admission ticket.

Krupp is an Ohio resident who currently divides his time between Columbus and Cincinnati. He has shown in galleries in the United States and Singapore and at art fairs in New York and Chicago. How did our perceptions of America's food production system change from bounty to dread? And what can past corporate persuasions tell us about the present and future? Films include The Man in the Doorway (American Cyanamid, 1956), a dystopian parable explaining why societies starve and die; The Color of Health (American Bakers Association, 1954), an existentialist epic on children and nutrition; and the newly discovered vegetable-patch comedy Gardening Made Easy (Henry Charles, 1949).

name: Nuremberg: Its Lessons for Today
description: Nuremberg trials of top Nazi officials were the first to use film extensively as evidence, and the first to be extensively documented, both aurally and visually. Although the trials lasted eleven months, only 25 hours of footage was made available to the filmmakers of Nuremberg: Its Lesson for Today, which was intended to be an authoritative record of the trials and the Nazi crimes. Released in West Germany, the film was ultimately suppressed in the U.S. for a myriad of possible reasons.

name: Jazz Arts Group's Inside Track: The Birth of the Cool
description: As jazz's bebop movement flourished during the late 1940s with its fast-paced rhythms from virtuosos like trumpeter Dizzy Gillespie and saxophonist Charlie Parker, trumpeter Miles Davis headed off in a new direction. Taking cues from the innovations learned in Parker's group, Davis, along with his nonet, recorded 12 songs in a two-year span that, when released together on one album, became known as Birth of the Cool. In 1949, arranger Gil Evans's New York basement apartment, where various jazz musicians had gathered, became ground zero for the nonet's formation. For the three recording sessions that took place Jan. and April 1949 and March 1950, Davis used the unlikely instruments of French horn and tuba, something first brought to light by the Claude Thornhill Orchestra, of which Evans was the principal arranger. Davis also enlisted the more traditional baritone and alto saxophones, trumpet, trombone, piano, bass and drums to complete the nonet. This instrumentation, coupled with the likes of Davis on trumpet, baritone saxophonist Gerry Mulligan, pianist John Lewis, alto saxophonist Lee Konitz and drummers Kenny Clarke and Max Roach, created a warm, relaxed, albeit "cool," sound that would become the standard for West Coast jazz.
