name: Creative Writing Workshop with Mimi Brodsky Chenfeld
address: Riffe Center, 77 S. High St., Columbus, OH 43215
description: Return of the WRITE people! Join educator, author and writer Mimi Brodsky Chenfeld for another round of aerobics for the imagination in the Riffe Gallery.

name: Gallery Talk and Poetry Reading
description: Visiting Artist Marjoire Welish will be in the gallery to discuss her current exhibition Before, During and After: The story of a work. In addition Ms. Welish will be reading some poetry from some of her published works.

name: CAPA: My Mother's Italian, My Father's Jewish, and I'm in Therapy!
description: In this one-man, award-winning, off-Broadway comedy show, you'll meet the myriad of astounding characters in Steve Soloman's family through actor Ron Tobin's unique perspective and gift for storytelling. You may recognize someone you know, love, and tolerate in your own family when you spend an evening learning about this boisterous crew and Steve's quest to defend himself against those people whose only purpose in life is to add chaos to his.

name: Echoes in Time Theatre: Pigs in the Streets!
description: Mrs. Francis Trollope, from England, toured America in 1827 and settled in Cincinnati, Ohio, for a time. On her return to England, however, she brought herself into notice by publishing Domestic Manners of the Americans in 1832, in which she gave an unfavorable account of American society. In the opinions of some of her critics, it was somewhat exaggerated account of the subject.

name: Celtic Woman: Songs From The Heart Tour
Actors' Theatre: The Male Animal
description: Dee Shepherd will direct this production. The Male Animal is one of Thurber's most popular plays. It takes a comic look at life in a Midwestern University that looks and sounds very much like OSU.

name: Available Light Theatre: Skyscrapers of the Midwest
admission: Pay what you want, $1 to whatever
description: More than a year in the making, this genre-bending adaptation of Josh Cotter's critically-acclaimed graphic novel follows two young siblings through the joys and pain of their innocent, 1980s childhood in the heartland, complete with dinosaurs and giant robots.

name: CAPA: Complexions Contemporary Ballet
description: Founders Desmond Richardson and Dwight Rhoden, along with their New York City-based company of dance thoroughbreds have awakened audiences to a new, exciting genre that combines the best of athleticism, lyricism, technical training, and experience. The company's foremost innovation is that dance should be about removing boundaries, not reinforcing them. Whether it be the limiting traditions of a single style, period, venue, or culture, Complexions transcends them all, creating an open, continually evolving form of dance that reflects the movement of our world - and all its constituent cultures - as an interrelated whole.

name: Bread and Circus Theatre: A Midsummer Night's Dream
description: This production introduces a new generation of young actors to the joys of the Bard. Ahhh, the thrill of high school romances! Magic (or maybe just hormones run amuck) abounds as two young couples fight, fall in and out of love, and find themselves pawns in a game played for the amusement of a couple on the verge of a divorce, Coach of the Football team Oberon and Head Cheerleading Coach Titania. Meanwhile, in Shakespeare's most delightful subplot, a group of very bad actors from the Thespian club find themselves caught up in the same game, and one, Nick Bottom (the Assistant Principal who always wanted to be on the stage), gets turned into a donkey. All's well that ends well, however, and all ends well indeed in the Bard's most happy conclusion.

name: Broadway Across America: Mary Poppins
description: The world's most famous nanny is coming to you! Combining the best of the original stories by P. L. Travers and the beloved Walt Disney film, the Tony Award-winning Mary Poppins is everything you'd hope for in a Broadway musical and more. Produced by Disney and Cameron Mackintosh, the show includes such wonderful songs as Chim Chim Cher-ee, A Spoonful of Sugar, Let's Go Fly a Kite and, of course, Supercalifragilisticexpialidocious.

name: Synergy: Dance-Drama-Music
description: Poetry in form and motion, Company members grace the stage weaving back and forth in intricate patterns dictated by the music, and the joy in their souls. Join us for an evening where Mind, Body and Soul come to life!

name: Columbus Blue Jackets vs. Chicago Blackhawks
Columbus Blue Jackets vs. St. Louis Blues
Columbus Blue Jackets vs. Buffalo Sabres
NCAA Men's Gymnastics Championships
venue: St. John Arena, The Ohio State University

name: Columbus Clippers Baseball vs. Toledo Mud Hens
Columbus Clippers Baseball vs. Louisville Bats
PaddlePalooza ! Ohio's Outdoors Expo
description: Show features include an indoor kayak demo pool and certified instructors from Columbus Outdoor Pursuits, as well as ongoing seminars on subjects including car-topping equipment and techniques, camping tent selection, rigging kayaks for fishing, selecting the right mountain bike, and new product intros and reviews. Exhibits will feature the latest in canoes, kayaks and paddle gear, mountain bikes, camping equipment and fly fishing tackle from local retailers, while canoe rental liveries and guides will display what they offer Ohio outdoor adventure-seekers. Local paddling, hiking, biking and related clubs will share information and answer questions on all things outdoors at PaddlePalooza!

name: Columbus Clippers Baseball vs. Indianapolis Indians
Too Many Cooks: The Olive Orchard
description: This month, join WGC and The Olive Orchard in an olive oil tasting. Come taste some favorite savory and sweet goodies that can be made with various flavored Olive Orchard olive oils. Too Many Cooks features local chefs and culinary artists and provides a space to feature their passion, whatever it may be. Whatever your interest you are bound to find something that resonates at Too Many Cooks. Join us the second Sunday of every month for an intimate conversation with the food artisans that are making Columbus a tastier place to live.

name: Solo Dinners: The Art of Cooking for One: Practical Cooking Class with Chef RB
description: When a bowl of cereal just won’t satisfy your craving for a home-cooked meal.  Learn techniques and recipes for making fresh, nutritious dinners WITHOUT tons of leftovers. Each class is taught by Chef Laura Robertson-Boyd and takes place at Wild Goose Creative.

name: SoupOFF
description: Warm up the Winter with a delicious culinary competition where home cooks compete for the best soup in Columbus! We'll have plenty of samples and food to try, even a cooking demonstration for how to make a great dish the whole family will love. Great door prizes and fun for all ages.

name: Root Beer Tasting
description: Join us for the second in a series celebrating everything that is earthy, spicy, and sweet about root beer.  We will be tasting 10 of the finest root beers available in Columbus (including our own Frostop).

name: The Lee Brothers: Cooking as a Family
venue: Jeanne B. McCoy Community Center for the Arts
description: Siblings Matt and Ted grew up in Charleston, South Carolina. When they left to attend colleges in the Northeast, they so missed the foods of their hometown that they founded The Lee Bros. Boiled Peanuts Catalogue, a mail-order catalogue for southern pantry staples like stone-ground grits, fig preserves, and, of course, boiled peanuts.

name: Mid Ohio Ford Club Presents Columbus Spring Super Swap Meet
description: Over 1,000 vendors present with cars and accessories for sale. This show features acres and acres of Ford and Mercury new parts, used parts, literature, collectibles and cars for sale. You can't see it all in one day!

name: Buckeye Model Train & Railroad Show
description: Golden Spike Entertainment presents the Buckeye Model Train & Railroad show. This is Ohio's largest combination model train and railroad memorabilia show. Be sure to check out this unique event

name: Ohio State Rabbit Breeders Show & Sale
description: The Ohio State Rabbit Breeders Show & Sale returns to the O'Neill Building April 30 - May 1.   This is the largest state rabbit show in the country featuring around 12,000 rabbits. 45 different breeds will be represented with around 15 commercial and 20 private vendors present with tons of rabbit items and products for sale.

name: Exhibit: Fur, Fins, & Feathers
admission: Adults $10. Seniors and students $8. Children under 6 free. Free admission on Sunday
description: Fur, Fins, & Feathers, a family-friendly exhibition about animals in art, showcases works from CMA's permanent collection. This diverse exhibition includes a variety of media and styles such as Innuit stone carvings, wooden African headdresses, contemporary photography, and American folk art prints. Fur, Fins, & Feathers includes many works which visitors may not have seen before. Because the Museum is currently under renovation, CMA can highlight works from our permanent collection that are not normally on view. Enhanced programming related to the exhibition will include hands-on activities, tours, and visits from other community organizations such as Children's Theater and the Columbus Zoo and Aquarium.

name: Exhibit: Shared Intelligence: American Painting and the Photograph
admission: Adults $10. Seniors and students $8. Children under 6 free. Free admission on Sunday
description: Inspired by the Georgia O'Keeffe Museum Research Center's 2006 3-day symposium, Painting and Photography in American Art: Sources, Ideas and Influences, 1890s to the Present, this exhibition of 75 paintings and photographs explores the productive and fraught relationship of these two mediums in American modern art that has been ongoing since the last decades of the 19th century. It focuses on the work of painters for whom photography has been essential, among them Robert Bechtle, Chuck Close, Thomas Eakins, Audrey Flack, David Hockney, Georgia O'Keeffe, Ben Shahn, Charles Sheeler, and Andy Warhol. This traveling exhibition also includes works from CMA such as our Norman Rockwell and Kehinde Wiley.

name: Exhibit: Double Sexus: Hans Bellmer and Louise Bourgeois
description: This two-gallery presentation marks the U.S. debut of a major exhibition from Berlin, Germany, that explores connections and contrasts between two influential and historically significant artists. Louise Bourgeois (1911-2010), a famed sculptor who received the Wexner Prize in 1999, and Hans Bellmer (1902-1975), a German sculptor and photographer often associated with surrealism, are both noted for their investigations of sexuality, desire, gender, and the body. Featuring sculpture, photography, and works on paper, the show examines their expressive approaches to these provocative topics. Organized by the Nationalgalerie, Berlin, in cooperation with the Wexner Center.

name: Exhibit: Nathalie Djurberg: Human Behavior
description: Nathalie Djurberg is a Swedish-born installation artist who dramatizes feminist and psychoanalytic concerns using claymation video, music, and sculpture. She often uses all three in concert to create immersive gallery environments. Her carefully crafted animation and painterly use of color infuse her sculptures and films with a peculiar beauty that frames her psychic explorations.

name: Exhibit: Pipilotti Rist: The Tender Room
description: The renowned Swiss artist - a pioneer of using moving images in installation art - makes her solo debut in Columbus with a new site-specific project for one gallery. Her recent videos are driven by her interest in the transformative power of color. Often filled with whimsy, they toe the line between fantasy and reality. She makes the commonplace seem expected and fascinating by taking familiar subjects, such as the body, and divorcing them from traditional representations through her manipulation of color. Her videos and installations create wholly familiar yet strangely sensual environs. Her project for the Wexner Center will use her recent ideas as a platform for a wholly new work.

name: Exhibit: Tour of the ADA Mural: Liberty, Justice, and Access for All
description: The Journey: What does the ADA, access, and inclusion mean to you? 27 artists with disabilities from across Ohio answered that question in response to a call for art in June. 11 of these artists traveled to Columbus July 23 - 25 to create a mural celebrating the 20th anniversary of this milestone legislation. Designed by artist, Kong Ho, the mural incorporated an array of images and words and now stands 6 feet tall and 30 feet wide. In addition to the artists, approximately 40 community members volunteered their time to assist with its construction. Together these Ohioans created a piece of art and advocacy that celebrates ability, inclusion, and looks ahead to work that must be done in the next 20 years.

name: Capital University's Student Art Exhibition
address: One College and Main, Columbus, OH 43209
description: This multimedia juried exhibition showcases a variety of works created by the students of Capital University.

name: Exhibit: Jazz! Art Quilts in Performance
description: Jazz! Art Quilts in Performance is an exhibit that celebrates quilts as an art form in the cultural prime of jazz. The quilts celebrate the cultural heyday of jazz as art, music and craft. The magnificent quilts of renowned quilter, educator and jazz advocate, Dr. Marlene O'Bryant Seabrook (Charleston, SC), will be showcased along with traditionally styled Quilts from the African Parish House Quilters of Columbus.

name: Exhibit: Mother Artists at Work: Laboring
description: Mother Artists at Work explore laboring, a theme playing on the dual meaning of the process of becoming a mother as well as the toiling of an artist. Featuring works in 2-D & 3-D mixed media, painting, enameling, fiber and photography. The mission of MAW, a non-profit association of mothers working in the arts, is to support and promote artists who are mothers through networking, professional development, and exhibit opportunities, as they work to keep career and family in balance.

name: Mid Ohio Cat Fanciers Cat Show
Short North Gallery Hop
address: North High Street from Goodale Boulevard to Fifth Avenue, Columbus, OH 43201
description: The first Saturday of every month, thousands of visitors converge on the strip, the epicenter of the High Street experience. They come to celebrate art and partake in an evening of sights, sounds, food, shopping, and cosmopolitan fun. Countless art experiences. District specials. Prize drawings. Ramped up entertainment. Unexpected surprises. Join us for an unforgettable experience.

name: Thurber House Literary Series: Anna Quindlen
description: Anna Quindlen will appear with friend and fellow Pulitzer Prize winner Connie Schultz, columnist for The Plain Dealer. Among the topics will be Quindlen's most recent novel, Every Last One. A wine-and-hors d'oeuvres reception will precede the event.

name: 18th Annual Equine Affaire
description: The Equine Affaire returns to the Ohio Expo Center April 7th through the 10th.   The nation's premiere equine exposition & equestrian gathering will feature four days of educational clinics, seminars, and demonstrations by top professionals in the horse industry, as well as an extensive trade show, Breed Pavilion, Youth Pavilion & evening entertainment. The Pfizer Fantasia is a Musical Celebration of the Horse (separate ticket required).

name: Equine Affair
admission: Adult $14 or a 4-day pass $48. Child $8 or a 4-day pass $28.
description: The 17th annual Equine Affaire is expected to draw an attendance of more than 100,000 for the four-day event. Horse owners and enthusiasts can meet and learn directly from some of the world's most accomplished horse people, as well as see some of the country's finest horses. More than 200 clinics, seminars and demonstrations will take place. Returning this year is the Pfizer Fantasia - A Musical Celebration of the Horse, which takes place nightly in the coliseum. New this year is the Canine Affaire, a subset of the main event focusing on dog care and training.

name: Paws in the Plaza
description: Join other dogs as they bring their owners to stroll through the paths, river walks, pet friendly shops, and visiting vendors and businesses in downtown Olde Gahanna. Exhibits vary monthly including free nail trimmings, animal communicator, caricature artist, souvenir photos, raffles, giveaways, artist sketches, rescues and more!

name: Bill Cunningham New York
description: New York Times photographer Bill Cunningham has been chronicling fashion trends and society parties for the Times Style section for decades in his columns "On the Street" and "Evening Hours." Now you can take an inside look at his world in this delicate, funny, and often poignant portrait, wonderfully seasoned by interviews with uptown doyennes such as Tom Wolfe, Brooke Astor, and Vogue editor Anna Wintour, who jokes, "We all get dressed for Bill."

name: Opera Ball 2011
description: Join Opera Columbus for our annual fundraiser, held at the Atrium at Nationwide Plaza in downtown Columbus. Opera Ball features a catered dinner, open bar, live music (performances by Opera Columbus Artists and the Rick Brunetto Big Band), and a live and silent auction.

name: Quilting Workshop
description: No one wanted to miss a traditional quilting "B", as this was a major social occasion and chance for gossip; if you weren't there yours could be among the names bandied about over the frame! Quick, grab your grandchildren and join us for a unique opportunity to share stories with them and learn traditional quilting techniques from some of Greater Columbus' finest quilt artists. This multi-generation experience is not to be missed!

name: Earth, Paws and Claws
description: Hop over to the Columbus Zoo and Aquarium and join us for our annual Eggs, Paws and Claws Event with an Earth Day twist. This event returns bigger and better then ever. Now with more treat stations, kid friendly entertainment and seasonal themed animal enrichment activities than ever before. Don't miss a visit with the Bunny!

name: Cardinal Cluster Dog Show
description: The Cardinal Cluster Dog Show returns to the Buckeye Building April 23 & 24. The Central Ohio Kennel Club Inc. presents the Cardinal Cluster Dog Show with more than 150 AKC registered breeds to show & sell. Numerous dog vendors will be present.

name: 2011 Decorators' Show House
description: The Spanish-revival style home was built in 1928. It sits on almost two acres.

name: Feline Wine and Dine: A Pawsitively Purrfect Evening
description: Please join us for a fun evening with good food, lively music, and a fabulous auction at the first annual Feline Wine and Dine.

name: Mind, Body & Soul
description: The King Arts Complex and the Ward Family YMCA will present "Mind, Body & Soul" during April - Minority Health Month in Ohio. This community event will provide health information in a positive and fun atmosphere. This day of arts therapy, fitness activities, performances and presentations is free and open to the public.

name: Opening Reception: Annual Senior Art Show
description: Featuring the Juried works of Denison Studio Art Majors.

name: CCAD Art Sale
description: Take home great art and support local artists - all admission fees fund student scholarships and art sales go directly to an artist on the rise.

name: Arnold Party with the Pros
description: The 2011 Arnold Party with the Pros will offer night long fun, drinks, dancing, music, and entertainment. All the top celebrities who annually attend and participate in the Arnold Sports Festival weekend will be center stage. We hope you will join us in supporting this premier event.

name: Early Music in Columbus: Hopkinson Smith
address: 1 College and Main St., Columbus, OH 43209

name: The Columbus Symphony: Cirque De La Symphonie
description: It's a feast for the ears - and the eyes - as acrobats, jugglers, and aerialists from Cirque du Soleil join the Columbus Symphony Orchestra for a magical evening under the big top.

name: CityMusic: Brasil Guitar Duo
description: Equally at home on a Classical or a World Music series, the Duo's innovative programming features a seamless blend of traditional and Brazilian works, resulting in a full global touring schedule and numerous critically acclaimed recordings.

name: Music in the Atrium: Mike Morgan
description: Don't miss Jackson, Ohio, songwriter Mike Morgan, whose songs have been recorded by country artists Conway Twitty and Ed Bruce.

name: Roger Guenveur Smith: Juan and John
description: In his latest show, Obie Award-winning solo performer Roger Guenveur Smith brings to life the charged story of two baseball greats: Juan Marichal, one of the first pro stars to emerge from the Dominican Republic, and Ohio's own John Roseboro. As Juan and John unfold, it's 1965 and Watts and Vietnam are burning. So is la Republica Dominicana, where U.S. troops are involved in a "peacekeeping" mission. In San Francisco, it's the hometown Giants versus the Los Angeles Dodgers, and Giants pitcher Juan Marichal versus Dodgers catcher John Roseboro. Their confrontation at home plate erupts into the most notorious on-field fight in baseball history, a bloody brawl during which Marichal assaults Roseboro with his bat.

name: Jazz On The Avenue: A Melodious Celebration of the Art of Romare Bearden
description: Dayton native, Pianist Khalid Moss and The Kinkajoo Ensemble will perform music inspired by Bearden's Art accentuated with a visual presentation of the art of Romare Bearden.

name: ProMusica Chamber Orchestra: Denk performs Beethoven
description: American classical pianist Jeremy Denk takes the stage for an evening that pairs classics with a world premiere. The Orchestra will perform Wagner's "Siegfried Idyll," a commission and world premiere by Evan Chambers and Beethoven's "Piano Concerto No. 1" featuring Denk. On Saturday, local high school musicians will perform side-by-side ProMusica musicians for a special collaboration featuring Copland's "Hoe-Down."

name: Women in Music Columbus: Sundays at the Huntington
description: A recital by members of Women in Music Columbus featuring Laura Koh, violin; Byrdie Lorenz, soprano, accompanied by Billie Nastelin, piano; Jennifer Marcellana, mezzo soprano; Trio: Carol 'Winans, flute, Joy Norris, clarinet, Elaine Clark, piano; Trio: Joy Norris, clarinet, Marilyn Boyd, clarinet, Pat white, piano.

name: Columbus Jazz Orchestra: A Night at the Apollo
description: Beg, scream and shout as the CJO pays tribute to the soul of American culture, the Apollo Theater! The world famous Apollo Theater is so much more than a historic landmark - it is a source of pride and a symbol of brilliance of American artistic accomplishment. With its rich history and continued significance, the Apollo Theater, considered the bastion of African-American culture and achievement, is one of the most fascinating chronicles in American history. We'll celebrate music greats like Dinah Washington, Gladys Knight, James Brown, Otis Redding, Same Cooke and many others whose careers were launched by this legendary finishing school! The Columbus Youth Jazz Orchestra (CYJO) is proud to perform prior to Sunday's afternoon matinee at 1 p.m.

name: Carpe Diem: Banjo Mojo
description: Discover the hypnotically beautiful sound of banjo and strings, with a program ranging from renaissance madrigals to traditional old-timey folk songs. Graeme Boone (Ohio State University) is a magician, creating unique colors and textures that weave together with the strings for an unforgettable evening.

name: ProMusica Chamber Orchestra: An Evening of Brass and Organ
venue: Pontifical College, Josephinum St Turibius Chapel
description: Join us in our second home at the St. Turibius Chapel of the Pontifical College Josephinum!

name: Tenebrae
description: The Cathedral Schola's annual performance of music for Tenebrae, including Allegri's famous Miserere, has become one of the Cathedral's most popular events.

name: CityMusic: Beyond the Pale
description: For over a decade Toronto's Beyond the Pale has been making its distinctive brand of boundary-busting Eurofolk fusion, mixing Klezmer, Balkan, and Romanian styles with an eclectic range of North American influences.

name: Central Ohio Symphony: April Concert
description: The April concert will feature Ohio composer Deborah Netanal's 'Sounds of an Ancient City' based on her impressions of Jerusalem; Beethoven's monumental 'Emperor' piano concerto with Ohio guest artist Judit Bach, and the magical and picturesque 'Scheherazade'.

name: Chamber Music Columbus: Fry Street Quartet
description: Founded in Chicago in 1997 under the mentorship of the cellist of the renowned Vermeer Quartet, the Fry Street Quartet explores the medium of the string quartet and its life-affirming potential, receiving prestigious awards and rave reviews around the world.

name: Ashville Viking Festival
description: Presenting a living history event that reenacts a Viking All-Thing from a thousand years ago. Featuring a 40 ft. replica Viking Long Ship. There will be a variety of entertainment, including music, dance, and swordplay. Also on hand: crafts demonstrations, period merchandise to buy, a variety of food, and a children's area with crafts and storytellers. Canned food donation to the Ashville Food Pantry is requested.

name: Basic Bicycle Maintenance
description: Get your bike ready for spring! Chris Sharp, from roll: on Lane Avenue, demonstrates basic fixes for keeping a bicycle in top shape.

name: The Night Abraham Lincoln Died
description: Hear firsthand accounts of Abraham Lincoln's death, including a previously-unpublished letter from his wife! Grandview resident Caroline Van Deusen visits with stories, letters and memorabilia from her family's presidential friendships-her great-great-grandfather advised Lincoln, and her great-great-grandmother was a loyal friend of Mary Todd Lincoln!

name: Thurber House Evenings With Authors: Kristin Hannah
description: New York Times best-selling author, Kristin Hannah has written 18 novels including the mega-hits Firefly Lane, True Colors, and Winter Garden. Her latest, Night Road, is an emotionally complex novel about a mother of twins and one reckless night that promises to shatter the family, seemingly forever. It is a story that raises profound questions about motherhood, loss, identity, and forgiveness. An exquisite novel, Night Road showcases Hannah at the top of her form.

name: National DNA Day: A Fun Workshop!
description: How does the real science of human genetics differ from what's shown on TV crime shows? Celebrate National DNA Day (April 15) in this hands-on workshop!

name: Civil War and Ohio Statehouse Sesquicentennial Ohio National Guard Encampment & Ceremony
address: Broad St.& High St., Columbus, OH 43215
description: The Ohio National Guard, in partnership with the Ohio Statehouse and Ohio Historical Society will celebrate the 150th anniversary of the first Ohio unit mustered into federal service for the American Civil War. The event is the statewide kickoff weekend for the Ohio Civil War 150 celebration. Visitors will have the opportunity see an 1861 encampment as well as a modern day encampment, meet "Abraham Lincoln," see a variety of homeland defense vehicles and witness ceremonies honoring the history of America's armed forces.

name: Dead of Winter Bash
description: The Dead of Winter Bash is a costume gala and art auction to benefit orphaned children in Ethiopia. The party is open to the public, and will feature music, dancing, drinks, hoers d’oeuvres and desserts, live auctions, and chances to win cool prizes. Attendees should come dressed as a famous dead person. Tickets are $50 a person, and all proceeds from ticket sales and auction items will benefit Ethiopian Orphan Relief. Ethiopian Orphan Relief is a 501(c)(3) non-profit corporation that works to improve the living conditions and lives of orphaned children in Ethiopia.

name: Opening Reception; Before, during and after: the story of a work
description: Marjorie Welish is an American artist, critic, and poet. This exhibition is comprised of the artist book, Oaths? Questions? (Granary Books, 2009) as well as works from which the book derives or is a direct response.

name: Gallery Conversations: Piecing For Cover (A Warm Collaboration)
description: Piecing for Cover is an interactive and collaborative textile event promoting creativity within our community, as well as awareness of those without heating in the winter months. It took place on February 25, 2011, and the quilt produced by the artists will hang in the Wild Goose Creative gallery the month of March.  Join us for a gallery reception and a conversation with the artists on Thursday the 17th.

name: OSU Dance: MFA Concert: Teoma Naccarato & Maree ReMalia
venue: Sullivant Theatre, The Ohio State University
description: Teoma Naccarato: Personal narratives and memories, bodies and text explored in a group work on stage and in film. Maree Remalia: Solo performance springing from many voices through community workshops and shared authorship of movement and text.

name: Columbus Dance Theatre: Columbus Dances Fellowship Concert
description: An exciting highlight to next year's Season will be the creation of the Columbus Dances Fellowship Concert. CDT, in partnership with the Greater Columbus Arts Council, will host an annual concert of dances chosen from the local dance community with funding provided by GCAC. Five fellowships of $2000 each will be awarded to choreographers through an adjudication process in the fall of 2010.The five dances chosen will then be presented on a concert free to the public.

name: BalletMet Open Rehearsal
description: These open rehearsals provide a glimpse into the creative process and a sneak peek of an upcoming production. After the rehearsal, guests can participate in a question and answer session with the artists.

name: BalletMet and Shadowbox: 7 Deadly Sins
description: The season concludes with the ultimate rock and roll ballet, the world premiere 7 Deadly Sins, an original collaboration with Shadowbox. Anger, envy, gluttony, greed, lust, pride and sloth are on the menu with deliciously wicked choreography by guest artists including Dwight Rhoden (former principal dancer, Alvin Ailey American Dance Theater, director, Complexions Contemporary Ballet) and new compositions and arrangements of music performed live by Shadowbox's house band, BillWho?.

name: Luck 'o the Irish Craft for Kids
description: Kids can celebrate St. Patty's day and make a Luck 'o the Irish craft. Each child will make a shamrock themed photo frame and door hanger. The class is offered to children ages 3-12 and is free of charge. Register by March 14. Children ages 9 and under must be accompanied by an adult.

name: Flower Power Spring Craft for Kids
description: Welcome spring with the Just for Kids Flower Power craft. This class is offered for children ages 3.

name: The MAC Writers Group
venue: Peggy R. McConnell Arts Center of Worthington
description: This Worthington centric group, led by David Bell, will continue to meet at the MAC every other Friday to write, read, share and offer feedback. Come and enjoy the art of writing and share your work with others in the group.

name: Speak Easy
description: Wild Goose Creative believes everyone has a story to tell. To give those stories a voice we're proud to offer, Speak Easy, Columbus's premier event for live storytelling! It's simple: an audience, an open microphone, and great stories. Hilarious, gripping, poignant, you'll hear it all. Come to listen or come to tell as people from across Columbus offer their stories live on stage! This month's theme is all about those moments where life sneaks up on us, whips us around, and leaves us standing with our jaws on the floor. Sometimes we're the messenger trying not to get shot, sometimes we're the ones being ambushed. Either way it can be a wild ride. Don't miss what's sure to be a great night of tales!

name: FREE Writing Workshop
venue: Peggy R. McConnell Arts Center of Worthington
description: A great opportunity to hone your writing skills. Topics include: Revisiting Story Structure, Writing Books for Children, Characters and Thirty Steps to Being a Better Writer.

name: Thurber House Literary Series: Suze Orman
description: Suze Orman will discuss her first book in four years, The Money Class: Learn To Create Your New American Dream, to be published in March.

name: Jazz Arts Group's Inside Track: Chris Thomas King
description: Initially known for his audacious fusion of blues and hip-hop, Chris Thomas King reached a whole new audience starring in and scoring music for the Coen Brothers film O Brother, Where Art Thou?, not only appearing on the award-winning soundtrack, but establishing himself as a serious dramatic actor as well. King has continued to act in and score motion pictures including the Oscar winning Ray. King has also written and recorded more than 150 songs that are in demand for license to motion pictures, documentaries and television programs. The new album Sketches of Treme, is Chris Thomas King's first full-length studio album since the release of the Handy nominated Rise, in 2006. The tour will feature these new songs as well as fan favorites including songs from the movies Ray and O Brother.

name: Shilpa Ray and Her Happy Hookers
J. Roddy Walston and The Business
Phoenix Theatre for Children: Charlotte's Web
description: Wilbur must be "Some Pig" because Charlotte, the spider, has written those words in her web. Charlotte's sacrifice for Wilbur proves that she is some spider as well. This classic story has warmed the hearts of audiences for generations.

name: Guitar Lessons for Kids
description: This 6 week series will begin Tuesday, March 1 and meet every Tuesday night. Students will need to bring their own acoustic guitar (many parents have purchased inexpensive guitars at Target.)

name: Worthington Community Theatre: The Curious Savage
venue: Peggy R. McConnell Arts Center of Worthington
description: In this warm-hearted comedy, widow Ethel Savage hides ten million dollars in negotiable bonds. In order to get their hands on the money, her children admit her to a sanitarium. There, she meets various social misfits who seem saner than her "normal" family, who put the fun back in dysfunctional! Will kindness and decency prevail?

name: Mom & Me Sign Language II
description: The Mom and Me Sign Language II is the second class in our sign language series. This class is designed to build on the foundation that families have learned in Mom and Me Sign Language I. Families will expand their vocabulary skills and learn how to put all of their knowledge together to communicate in American Sign Language. Students will make crafts and participate in games that will help reinforce their learning.

name: Theater Classes for Kids
description: This class is for children ages 9-15 who love a little drama! Learn the vocabulary, techniques and skills of acting in theater productions. The students will take the skills they have learned and participate in a performance on Thursday April 14, 2011. Performance will be held on the Town Hall's historic stage.

name: Spanish for Beginners
description: Learn how to pronounce and spell almost every word in the Spanish language in this new class. Students will also develop reading comprehension skills. Spanish for Beginners is a free class and is open to adults 18 and over.

name: Hit & Run Happy Hour
description: That's right folks! The Hit & Run is back for 2011 and we are excited! On the 3rd Wednesday of each month, we are going to be hosting the hottest art social/ happy hour in Columbus! Some of the Hottest Artists/Crafters in Columbus showcasing their work with Live Music, Local Food, and Happy Hour Beverages!

name: Tween Scene Fun
description: Attention kids ages 10 - 12, we have a cure for your boredom on Friday night! Join us for an evening of video gaming, board games, crafts and more at Town Hall.

name: Backyard Science Day
description: Spring is here! Discover the science you can find in your own backyard. Look through microscopes, examine fossils, and learn how plants transform the landscape.

name: Let's Make Some Noise
description: Open to children ages 3 through 12, kids will make 4 musical instruments using household items.

name: Childish Issues: Evelyn Davis
venue: Peggy R. McConnell Arts Center of Worthington
description: Davis's mixed-media works are created to examine the symbiotic relationship of childhood and adulthood. She looks back at games, toys and other paraphernalia of the 1970's and 1980's and the deep social undertones they address, such as war, immigration, and corruption.

name: Coming Home to Roost; Marty Shuter
venue: Peggy R. McConnell Arts Center of Worthington
description: With her ceramic sculptures, Shuter uses the chicken motif to make a sly commentary on sexuality, stereotypes and identity. Born and raised in Worthington, Marty has taught across the country and also instructs for the MAC.

name: Mike Salrin: Effects of Time
venue: Peggy R. McConnell Arts Center of Worthington
description: Salrin's photography is distinguished by rusted metal, peeling paint, or just the grime of an empty warehouse.

name: Ohio Plein Air
venue: Peggy R. McConnell Arts Center of Worthington
description: Observe real artists in action. Every Saturday during the month, the Ohio Plein Air meets at the MAC to paint. Drop in and experience that "open air" painting happening inside during the winter months.

name: Economic Crisis in Europe: How Corruption Led to the Rise, and Fall, of Ireland
venue: Hamilton-Williams Campus Center, Ohio Wesleyan University
description: The 8th Annual Corinne Lyman Lecture on International Studies features Elaine Byrne, Ph.D. of Trinity College in Dublin, Ireland speaking about Economic Crisis in Europe: How Corruption Led to the Rise, and Fall, of Ireland

name: John Glenn to Speak at Statehood Day Event
address: Broad St.& High St., Columbus, OH 43215
description: Former Ohio Sen. John Glenn will join Ohio's history and preservation advocates at the Ohio Statehouse March 1 in recognition of Ohio's statehood and to promote the state's rich heritage. Glenn will address the group at lunch. To commemorate Sen. Glenn's career as an astronaut, the Ohio Historical Society will bring some of its aerospace collections to display during the event.

name: Better Living Through Economics: John Siegfried, PH.D.
description: The Woltemade Center for Economics, Business, and Entrepreneurship hosts John Siegfried, Ph.D., professor of economics at Vanderbilt University and secretary-treasurer of the American Economic Association, discussing "Better Living Through Economics".

name: Exhibit: Shared Intelligence: American Painting and the Photograph
admission: Adults $10. Seniors and students $8. Children under 6 free. Free admission on Sunday
description: Inspired by the Georgia O'Keeffe Museum Research Center's 2006 3-day symposium, Painting and Photography in American Art: Sources, Ideas and Influences, 1890s to the Present, this exhibition of 75 paintings and photographs explores the productive and fraught relationship of these two mediums in American modern art that has been ongoing since the last decades of the 19th century. It focuses on the work of painters for whom photography has been essential, among them Robert Bechtle, Chuck Close, Thomas Eakins, Audrey Flack, David Hockney, Georgia O'Keeffe, Ben Shahn, Charles Sheeler, and Andy Warhol. This traveling exhibition also includes works from CMA such as our Norman Rockwell and Kehinde Wiley.

name: Monthly Anime Adventure: Japanese Culture and Anime
description: Join us at the OSU Urban Arts Space for the Monthly Anime Adventure, a series of talks, discussions and multimedia events all centered on Japanese animation. This month's topic is Japanese Culture and Anime, and will look at Japanese traditional and modern culture and its visible influence in anime; including daily rituals, manners, political and civil history and mythology.

name: Girls Rock Columbus with Iyania Vanzant
description: The Lincoln Theatre Association (LTA) has partnered with The Columbus Women & Girls Mentoring Society (WGMS) to present Dr. Iyanla Vanzant as part of the first annual Girls Rock Columbus, an event designed to educate, empower, and celebrate the girls and women of central Ohio. Vanzant, a renowned motivational speaker and worldwide advocate for the empowerment of women, will be the keynote speaker at the public ceremony on Thursday, March 3. The evening's program will also include presentation of the first "Woman of Passion, Purpose, and Pursuit Awards" to nine local recipients, as well as spoken word, vocal, and dance performances from local artists.

name: Exhibit: Alterations
venue: Beeghly Library Gallery, Ohio Wesleyan University
description: Alterations, an exhibit of clothing and accessory items transformed into sculptural garments to demonstrate identity, body image, and self esteem in contemporary culture.

name: Exhibit: Artwork by Diane Almendinger
venue: Mowry Alumni Center, Ohio Wesleyan University
description: An exhibit of works in permanent ink on canvas and paper by Diane Almendinger, OWU emeritus professor of art history.

venue: Richard M. Ross Art Museum, Ohio Wesleyan University
description: The History of the Future, an exhibition of photographs by Michael Berman and Julian Cardona. This exhibit will include photographs related to U.S./Mexican border issues and Mexican migration, and is part of OWU's 2010-2011 Sagan National Colloquium Program.

name: Evening Programs Perkins Observatory
description: Content varies based on sky conditions, but may include a planetarium show, observatory tours, and star gazing with the 32-inch Schottland Telescope.

name: Exhibit: Art in the House: Ceremonial Objects
description: Columbus Metropolitan Library and Friends of the Library proudly present Greater Columbus Arts Council's Art in the House: Ceremonial Objects. The artworks in this show are by Art in the House, an out of school time arts program for children 5-11 years old and are inspired by the exhibit Ceremonial Objects currently on display at The Frank Museum of Art at Otterbein University, Westerville, Ohio.

name: Exhibit: The Naturalists
description: There is a clear amount of scientific method to the way each of these artists approach their chosen subjects classifying, categorizing, and organizing, but also a degree of the romantic, humorous, political or metaphorical. Diane Stemper, Erin Holscher-Almazan and Francis Schanberger, continue the long tradition of artists taking inspiration from the natural world.

name: Dead of Winter Bash
description: The Dead of Winter Bash is a costume gala and art auction to benefit orphaned children in Ethiopia. The party is open to the public, and will feature music, dancing, drinks, hoers d'oeuvres and desserts, live auctions, and chances to win cool prizes. Attendees should come dressed as a famous dead person. Tickets are $50 a person, and all proceeds from ticket sales and auction items will benefit Ethiopian Orphan Relief. Ethiopian Orphan Relief is a 501(c)(3) non-profit corporation that works to improve the living conditions and lives of orphaned children in Ethiopia.

name: Winter Quarter Exhibitions Reception
description: Celebrate and experience the Winter Quarter exhibitions with the artists and curators. Crossing the BLVD: strangers, neighbors, aliens in a new America intimately reveals the lives of new immigrants and refugees through images, stories and sounds. The 2011 Arts Scholars Juried Exhibition searches for a way to prolong our sensations and feelings to make them immortal. Domestic Matters explores the intimate geographies and everyday life practices in the Agrarian South. Reception guests will also witness the first of Domestic Matters' installation performance series.

name: Exhibit: For The Person Who Has Everything
venue: ROY G BIV Gallery for Emerging Artists
description: ROY G BIV Gallery is proud to present; For The Person Who Has Everything, featuring the work of Samantha Hookway, Janet Macpherson and Zepher Potrafka.

name: Westin Columbus Wedding Show
description: This upscale Four Diamond Columbus, Ohio historic hotel will be showcasing the beauty of their historic Grand Ballroom along with a few of their preferred vendors. At 2:00pm, an actual wedding ceremony will take place. All attendees are invited. Door prizes will include roundtrip airfare for two anywhere in the continental United States, a pearl necklace, restaurant and concert certificates, and an overnight stay a the upscale Westin Great Southern Hotel. Admission includes parking. Champagne and hors d' oeuvres served.

name: Next Decade in Cosmology
description: New Vistas in Astronomy" lecture: "The Next Decade in Cosmology" by David Weinberg.

name: Domestic Matters: A Performing Installation
description: This interactive exhibition comes to life as dancers fill the space, performing new and recreated pieces of choreography by Mair Culbreth, Dante Brown and Amanda Byars Wickens. Dancers will inhabit Nicole Bauguss's visual structures and prompt a dialogue about ritual, intimacy and memory within the landscape. After the performance, the audience is welcome to take part in a special food-related lesson or activity.

This event will feature brand new work by all of our gallery artists, live music, and catering by Two Caterers! It will be a blow out party to re-invent our gallery! description: The All Student Spring Show art exhibit.

name: Whacked at the Winery, Murder Mystery Dinner
description: At Wyandotte we make the wine, but we don't solve the mysteries. That is YOUR job! Once again, someone has been ‘Whacked at the Winery’, and the culprit is right here among us. Join us for an evening of fun, food, music, and mayhem. Dinner includes Carfagna's homemade Italian chicken sausage with peppers and onions, whole grain penne pasta in a basil marinara sauce, Cesar Salad, garlic bread and of course our famous gourmet wine cakes for dessert! Join us for a gallery reception and a conversation with the artists on Thursday the 17th.

description: American honeymooners in Hungary are trapped in the home of a Satan- worshiping priest when the bride is taken there for medical help following a road accident.

name: The Community Film Series: Man's Favorite Sport
description: The Community Film Series film ""Man's Favorite Sport, ""a 1964 comedy about an uptight fishing outfitter who is lured into a fishing derby by a flirtatious prankster (Rock Hudson, Paula Prentiss).

name: Night Catches Us: Introduced by Tanya Hamilton
description: In 1976, after years of mysterious absence, Marcus (Anthony Mackie, The Hurt Locker ) returns to the Philadelphia neighborhood where he came of age in the midst of the Black Panther movement. Although his reappearance is greeted with suspicion among his family and former neighbors, he finds acceptance from an old friend (Kerry Washington, Ray) and her daughter. Old secrets slowly emerge as the members of this community come to terms with their revolutionary past and try to figure out a path forward.

name: Every Man for Himself
description: Godard called Every Man for Himself his "second first film," a reference to Breathless (1960), his actual first feature, and his return to film after a ten-year detour into video, a journey that many critics and devotees failed to make with him. Jacques Dutronc plays a slick, perverse videomaker (named Paul Godard!) whose relationships with his TV host ex-lover (Nathalie Baye) and a remorseless prostitute (Isabelle Huppert) is knitted together with Godard's trademark narrative and formal complexity. Godard's often-hilarious provocations on the interplay of sex and capitalism culminate in a four-person, Rube Goldbergian sex machine that has to be seen to be believed. (87 mins., 35mm)

name: Pinned
description: In Lakewood, Ohio, two young men are fighting for one dream: to become a state wrestling champion. Lance Palmer captains the St. Edward Eagles. He's a 3-time state champion who hits the gym before opening his Christmas presents and wrestles 600-lb. bears. Matt Curley, captain of the Lakewood Rangers, comes from a broken home and endures starvation hoping to be his school's first champion in 50 years.

name: Nostalgia for the Light
description: Chilean filmmaker Patricio Guzman is best known for his series of indispensable films that document the history and legacy of dictator Augusto Pinochet's brutal regime (1973 to 1990). In Nostalgia for the Light, Guzman continues his excavation of his country's recent past. He journeys to Chile's Atacama Desert, home to some of the world's largest telescopes and, it is speculated, to the remains of many executed political prisoners. Guzman poignantly connects an astronomer's search for celestial bodies with the search by a handful of women for the remains of loved ones beneath the desert's arid terrain. (90 mins., video)

name: Littlerock: Afterschool
description: Littlerock follows a pair of sightseeing Japanese siblings who are marooned in the small California town of Little Rock when their car breaks down. Even with a sizeable language barrier, they start hanging out with a group of aimless locals, and fumbling romances and friendships follow. A charming tale of outsiders and discovery, Littlerock is the winner of numerous audience and jury awards at film festivals around the world (as well as receiving a Gotham Award for "Best Movie Not Playing at a Theater Near You".

name: Putty Hill and Hamilton
description: Yorker The talented Matt Porterfield is revealing himself as a major new American filmmaker. Here's your chance to see two of the films that have made his name. Porterfield introduces the films to start each evening and answers questions between them.

name: The Community Film Series: Double Indemnity
description: The Community Film Series film "Double Indemnity", a film noir masterpiece that features an insurance agent who is conned into helping a scheming wife murder her husband (Fred MacMurray, Barbara Stanwyck, 1944).

name: And Everything Is Going Fine
description: And Everything Is Going Fine provides an intimate portrait of brilliant playwright and actor Spalding Gray, as described by his most critical, irreverent, and insightful biographer: himself.

name: The Community Film Series: The Man Who Shot Liberty Valance
description: The OWU Department of English and Strand Theatre present the Community Film Series screening of The Man Who Shot Liberty Valance, a classic Old West movie that was director John Ford's last masterpiece (John Wayne, Jimmy Stewart, 1962).

name: Ballast and Beeswax
description: Among the most critically praised independent films of recent years; Ballast tells the powerful, gentle tale of a single mother in the Mississippi Delta-one of the poorest regions in the country struggling to provide for herself and her son. A sudden act of violence forces her to rely on the brother-in-law she's always been wary of while she forges a new life for her family. The New York Times astutely noticed what a watershed film Ballast is, calling it ""a serious accomplishment and a welcome sign of a newly invigorated American independent cinema. (96 mins., 35mm)

name: His Girl Friday
description: Among the very finest comedies that Hollywood has ever produced, His Girl Friday follows a conniving but irresistible newspaper editor (played by Cary Grant, a master of rapid-fire banter and physical humor) as he desperately tries to woo back his star reporter (Rosalind Russell, more than the equal to Grant). The reporter just happens to be the editor's ex-wife, and she's ready to settle down with a new beau (Ralph Bellamy, the lug of lugs in one of his best roles). Hawks keeps everything moving at a furious pace as romance and professional competition come together in a scintillating battle of the sexes. (92 mins., 35mm)

name: The Community Film Series: Breakfast on Pluto
description: The OWU Department of English and Strand Theatre present the Community Film Series screening of Breakfast on Pluto, a movie about a foundling who has a woman's soul trapped in a man's body. Actor Gillian Murphy was nominated for a Golden Globe for his performance. (Produced in Ireland and Jordan, 2005.)

name: Two Gates of Sleep and Decay of Fiction
description: One of the rare American indie films to premiere at the Cannes Film Festival and the latest from a longtime indie director combine for this double feature.

name: Monday Night Live
description: Travis Hoewischer and Wild Goose Creative present a first-of-its-variety variety show, featuring some of the best creative comedy minds and brilliant musicians the capital city contains. No show will be the same, but each may include live and filmed sketches, improv and standup comedy, as well as other one special musical guest for each show. MNL will be hosted once monthly, on every first Monday.

name: I Love You, You're Perfect, Now Change
description: This musical celebration of the mating game takes on the truths and myths behind that contemporary conundrum known as the relationship. Act I explores the journey from dating and waiting to love and marriage. Act II reveals the agonies and triumphs of in-laws, newborns, trips in the family car and pick-up techniques of the geriatric set. This hilarious revue pays tribute to those who have loved and lost; to those who have fallen on their face at the portal of romance; to those who have dared to ask, Say, what are you doing Saturday night?

name: Columbus Food Adventures: Short North Walking Tour
description: Take a leisurely stroll with us through the Short North. Not just an Arts district and home to the Monthly Gallery Hop, the Short North also boasts a wealth of dining and shopping opportunities. The Short North is packed full of boutiques, fine dining and nightlife and this tour is designed to show off some of the best that the Short North and Columbus have to offer.

name: Columbus Food Adventures: All Dessert Tour
description: Join us on this van-based tour featuring some of the best desserts in Columbus. This tour will start at the acclaimed Pistacia Vera in German Village, visit the new Sugardaddy's downtown location to sample some of their sumptuous brownies and blondies, and then head north to the Pattycake bakery in Clintonville. Of course no dessert tour of Columbus would be complete without Jeni's splendid ice cream, so we will visit their new Clintonville location to try some of their newest seasonal flavors. Finally, we'll finish our tour with a fabulous dessert cocktail created by mixologist extraordinaire Cris Dehlavi at M Restaurant (there will be a non-alcoholic drink option available for those under 21 or who do not wish to consume alcohol).

name: Get Crocked! at Wyandotte Winery
description: Enjoy a hot dish of Crockery cooking at its finest! You can enjoy a steaming bowl of homemade soup, stew, or chili, with rustic bread, and a glass of Wyandotte Winery wine!

name: Columbus Food Adventures: Alt Eats Tour
description: Travel the world while without leaving Columbus. This tour's itinerary will introduce you to some of the best ethnic food in the city. We'll experience a taste of Zanzibar, eat Vietnamese sandwiches, sample Somali food, sample some Southern Indian food, and visit a Latino grocery store. Join us in our comfortable 14-passenger van, and learn about the cuisines and cultures of some of Columbus's finest immigrant kitchens.

name: Solo Dinners: The Art of Cooking for One: Practical Cooking Class with Chef RB
description: When a bowl of cereal just won't satisfy your craving for a home-cooked meal. Learn techniques and recipes for making fresh, nutritious dinners WITHOUT tons of leftovers. Each class is taught by Chef Laura Robertson-Boyd and takes place at Wild Goose Creative.

name: Root Beer Tasting
description: Join us for the second in a series celebrating everything that is earthy, spicy, and sweet about root beer. We will be tasting 10 of the finest root beers available in Columbus (including our own Frostop).

name: Ohio Beef Expo
description: Hosted the third weekend in March each year, the Ohio Beef Expo is Ohio's premier beef industry event. This is the 24th anniversary of the Ohio Beef Expo. Ranked as the ninth largest event hosted in Central Ohio, Expo attracts over 25,000 attendees annually. This year's event will feature seven breed sales, ten breed shows, and one of the biggest junior shows in the state. The centerpiece of the Expo, the trade show, boasts over 100 vendors from 13 states. Exhibitors in this year's trade show represent all segments of the industry from cattle handling equipment to show supplies, clothing to feed, genetics, and novelty items, and much, much more

name: Ysaye & Friends
description: Referred to as “The King of the Violin” and the world’s first modern violinist, Eugene Ysaye was a Belgian violinist, composer, and conductor. His intensely technical, neo-Romantic style triggered the inspiration for this program, which features Ballade and Polonaise by Henri Vieuxtemps; Poeme by Ernest Chausson; Ysaye’s Solo Sonata No. 4; and Sonata by Cesar Franck. Vieuxtemps was Ysaye’s mentor and a prominent advocate of the Franco-Belgian  violin school. Chausson composed Poeme for Ysaye, and it has been speculated that Ysaye wrote or substantially revised its violin part to showcase his giant palette of tonal color. Franck gifted this Sonata to Ysaye as a wedding present. Its four movements are believed to represent the four stages of life: childhood, adolescence, adulthood, and maturity.

description: The OWU Department of Music's Park Avenue Jazz Ensemble. The ensemble is conducted by Larry Griffin, OWU professor of music.

name: Central Ohio Symphony: OWU Choral Art Society and Capriccio!

Also on the program is John Williams' Harry Potter suite, recently voted favorite piece of classical music by young adults.

name: Death By Banjo
venue: Peggy R. McConnell Arts Center of Worthington
description: Thursday Night Concert Series continues with Death By Banjo.  Once, every Blue Moon, the MAC offers an additional concert to experience.  As the name implies, Death by Banjo is bluegrass and beyond. On fire with creativity, Death by Banjo is a conflagration of musical styles fueled by intense, driving 5-string banjo. They have played blues, swing, jazz, rock, country, old time, Irish, folk, classical and, of course, bluegrass. Together, they share a passion for sincere, earthy music and the ability to create it with energy, joy and enthusiasm.

name: Lebowski Fest
venue: Skully's and Columbus Square Bowling Palace
description: Lebowski Fest is a celebration of all things related to the 1998 Coen brothers cult comedy, "The Big Lebowski." Fans of the film (aka "Achievers") come from far and wide to drink white Russians, throw some rocks and party with an array of Dudes, Walters and Maudes (not to mention a nihilist or two). It's a two-day party that typically opens with live performances and screening of the film the first night and concludes with a raucous bowling party the following night. The First Annual Lebowski Fest was in 2002 in Louisville, but subsequent fests have been held in New York, Los Angeles, Chicago, Las Vegas, Austin, Seattle, London and Edinburgh. While the Coen brothers continue to maintain a safe distance from the madness they created, the fest has earned the blessing of the Dude himself, Jeff Bridges, who attended the fest in L.A. and even stuck around to sing a few songs.

In 1999, Richard married the very accomplished American cellist Julie Adams and settled in the Nashville, TN area. When they play together, it will melt your heart.

description: The 2011 Capital City Half Marathon will feature four races: the Capital City Half Marathon (13.1 miles); the inaugural Capital City Quarter Marathon (6.55 miles); the popular Commit To Be Fit Fun Run/Walk (3 miles) and the Capital Kids Mascot Chase. The new course will guide runners through five distinct Columbus neighborhoods before finishing in the Arena District in downtown Columbus.

name: Film Festival: Bogey and Huston
description: John Ford & John Wayne. Scorsese & De Niro. Kurosawa & Toshiro Mifune. Directors have teamed up with certain actors again & again with amazing results.

name: Market to Market Bicycle Adventure
description: Two of Columbus' premiere independent, locally-owned specialty foods markets are returning with an event that debuted with great success last October: Market to Market. The Hills Market and North Market share not only a philosophical connection: one that makes it a priority to provide and promote the best Ohio has to offer to consumers, but also a physical connection: the Olentangy River Greenway (or more commonly, the Olentangy Bike Trial). Join both markets on Saturday, May 1, as they connect to celebrate Ohio-made foodstuffs, the opening of the farmers market and bicycling season with "Market to Market": a cross-city local foods-centric bike ride, for amateurs and aficionados alike.

name: Theatre on the Lawn: Robin Hood
description: The Carriage Place Players, from Carriage Place Recreation Center in northwest Columbus, perform this popular play on our outdoor stage. Bring a blanket or chair, and enjoy theatre on our lawn!

name: Cinevent
admission: $20 a day. Full event $40 or $35 in advance
venue: Ramada Plaza Hotel and Conference Center
description: Cinevent is a gathering of fans of silent and early sound films, and of collectors of motion pictures and related items. Movie screenings are available from mid-day Friday to mid-day Monday (with a few hours off to sleep!) each Memorial Day Weekend. Dealers fill over 170 tables full of film, video, sound recordings, posters, stills, lobby cards, books, autographs - everything imaginable associated with film.

name: Tour Of the Scioto River Valley
description: There are many rides, but only one is America's Bicycle Touring Classic. The Tour Of the Scioto River Valley, better known by its acronym, TOSRV. Say TOSRV to bicycle riders around the nation, and they'll know you mean this event. Started by a father-and-son outing in 1962 before quickly growing into the nation's largest bicycle touring weekends. TOSRV was the first to help raise the profile of the bicycle American life and was the inspiration for many of the mass-participation cycling events across the country and range in age from 2-93. Held on Mother's Day weekend the event starts at the Ohio Statehouse grounds and makes its way to Portsmouth some 105 miles south. Avoiding the large hills of southern Ohio, the first 50 to 60 miles are a series of slight grades to short steep hills. The remaining miles into Portsmouth are relatively flat for a total of 105 miles.

name: Martial Arts Battle Of Columbus
description: The 35th Battle of Columbus Martial Arts World Games takes place May 28th & 29th in the Lausche Building. Over 1,000 awards, 100 masters, and 30 rings in this WUMA sanctioned event. Besides the competition there will be workshops and demonstrations, numerous vendors present to introduce top equipment, a Bruce Lee collection and Asian Art Exhibit.

name: The MAC Writers Group
venue: Peggy R. McConnell Arts Center of Worthington
description: This Worthington centric group, led by David Bell, will continue to meet at the MAC every other Friday to write, read, share and offer feedback. Come and enjoy the art of writing and share your work with others in the group.

name: Civil War Comes to Columbus
description: Even though there were no battles fought in Columbus, Ohio, during the Civil War, the City was knee-deep in plans and actions regarding it. Come along with Capital City Tours as we walk in the footsteps of Union soldiers and doomed Confederate prisoners, fiery abolitionists and desperate runaways, heroes, villains and ordinary people struggling to survive one of the most extraordinary times in our nation's history. Brother against brother, father against son. Never has this country been socially strained as much. Join us as we explore Columbus' Civil War past.

name: Columbus Food Adventures: Taco Truck Tour
description: Taco trucks serve up far more than just tacos, and nobody knows Columbus's expansive taco truck scene better than Columbus Food Adventures. This van tour will explore the taco trucks of West side, taking you to some of our favorites and providing you with the best of Mexican food in Columbus. Each stop includes a tasting, and the tour is structured with an emphasis on individual truck specialties as well as the diversity of regional cuisine found at these trucks. If you want to find out what the buzz has been about, or want to learn more about authentic Mexican food, this is the tour for you. This tour is suitable for those who have never visited a taco truck as well as those who are looking to explore new trucks and dishes.  In addition to sampling food and drink from 5 different trucks, you will learn all about the different dishes, meat choices, and how to order at a taco truck.  This tour is not suitable for vegetarians.

name: Ohio Plein Air
venue: Peggy R. McConnell Arts Center of Worthington
description: Observe real artists in action. Every Saturday during the month, the Ohio Plein Air meets at the MAC to paint. Drop in and experience that "open air" painting happening inside during the winter months.

name: 2 Day Spring Break Ceramics OPEN Studio
venue: Peggy R. McConnell Arts Center of Worthington
description: Spend your break at the MAC and take a whirl on the wheel or build your masterpiece. The instructor will provide you with inspiration and guidance.

name: U.S. and Asia Pacific Economic Trends & Issues
description: Kurt Tong is the Economic Coordinator for the Bureau of East Asian and Pacific Affairs, organizing bureau-wide efforts on economic policy issues. He is also U.S. Senior Official for Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC), managing all aspects of U.S. participation in that organization.

name: The Ladies of Longford with Craig and Kara Markley
venue: Peggy R. McConnell Arts Center of Worthington
description: Presented by Atlrusa International Of Columbus Ohio Foundation.  Contemporary Celtic concert with proceeds improving the economic well being and quality of life in our communities through a number of organizations.

name: Poetry
description: Winner for Best Screenplay at the Cannes Film Festival, Poetry follows a Korean woman who develops a passion for poetry as she deals with the onset of Alzheimer's disease. Cajoled out of a sixteen-year retirement by director Lee, Yun Junghee gives an unforgettable performance as the indefatigable grandmother who must cope not only with her looming illness but also an elderly stroke victim under her care and her surly grandson who has been accused of participating in a gang rape that led to the victim's suicide. (139 mins., 35mm)

name: The Banff Mountain Film Festival
description: Each year, the Banff Mountain Film Festival presents the most creative and inspiring examples of outdoor adventure filmmaking from around the world. See award-winning selections from last fall's festival, focusing on such activities as BASE jumping, skiing, mountain biking, and snow boarding. Check back here for a complete program lineup. (program app. 150 mins., video)

name: Disco and Atomic War
description: Disco and Atomic War is a light-hearted reflection on the influence of Western pop culture on the dissolution of the Soviet Union.

name: Rare Films from the Baseball Hall of Fame
description: For the eighth year in a row, we're celebrating the opening of a new baseball season with cinematic treasures from the National Baseball Hall of Fame that will entertain baseball fans and cinephiles alike. Dave Filipi, the Wexner Center's curator of film/video, introduces the clips. (Program app. 120 mins., video)

name: Shoah (First Era)
description: This epic documentary (12 years in the making, over 9 hours in length, and now re-released on the occasion of its 25th anniversary) changed the way we think about the Holocaust. Featuring interviews with survivors, bystanders, and perpetrators from across Europe, mostly Poland and Germany, Shoah is drawn from over 300 hours of contemporary conversations with these witnesses, along with footage of overgrown sites of unspeakable horrors, including the concentration camp at Auschwitz.

name: Bill Plympton Idiots and Angels
description: One of Americas most acclaimed, outrageous, and brilliant independent animators, Bill Plympton visits to introduce and discuss his two most recent films.

name: Shoah (Second Era)
description: This epic documentary (12 years in the making, over 9 hours in length, and now re-released on the occasion of its 25th anniversary) changed the way we think about the Holocaust. Featuring interviews with survivors, bystanders, and perpetrators from across Europe, mostly Poland and Germany, Shoah is drawn from over 300 hours of contemporary conversations with these witnesses, along with footage of overgrown sites of unspeakable horrors, including the concentration camp at Auschwitz.

name: Uncle Boonmee Who Can Recall His Past Lives
description: Winner of the Palme d'Or at the 2010 Cannes Film Festival (from a jury headed by Tim Burton), Uncle Boonmee is a magical, surreal trip through the mind of a man in the countryside of Thailand contemplating reincarnation at the end of his life. Surrounded by loved ones and caretakers, he is visited by the spirits of his deceased wife and long-lost son (the latter in the form of a giant monkey ghost). During his travels through the jungle to a remote hilltop cave, he sees what might be his previous lives pass before him.

name: The Strange Case of Angelica
description: Manoel de Oliveira is not only the oldest working filmmaker but the only active filmmaker to have started working in the silent era! And he's still one of today's most vital filmmakers as evidenced by this latest effort. The Strange Case of Angelica is an enchanting tale about a young photographer who falls madly in love with a woman he can never have, except in his dreams. Summoned to take the last photograph of Angelica, a young bride who mysteriously passed away, the photographer finds that the woman comes to life when he looks through his lens. From that moment, he will be haunted by Angelica day and night. (94 mins., 35mm)

name: I Just Wanted to Be Somebody; The Smell of Burning Ants; Human Remains; King of the Jews
description: Get ready for tomorrow night's visit by Jay Rosenblatt with this selection of his distinctive shorts. If his plane arrives on time, he may come by to introduce tonight's films too. Director Atom Egoyan calls him ""an exquisite artist who makes beautifully crafted miniatures.

name: The D Train; Phantom Limb; Afraid So; The Darkness of Day
description: Jay Rosenblatt introduces four more of his remarkable shorts and answers questions from the audience. Director Atom Egoyan calls him "an exquisite artist who makes beautifully crafted miniatures." In Rosenblatt's latest, The D Train, an elderly man reflects on his life. (2011, 5 mins., video). Phantom Limb offers the director's meditation on the loss of his brother as a child. (2005, 28 mins., video) Afraid So is a short film about anxiety (2006, 3 mins, video). In The Darkness of Day, the director creates a haunting rumination on suicide inspired by the death of a friend 20 years ago. (2009, 26 mins., video).
