name: Columbus Children's Theatre: The Three Little Pigs
description: Once upon a time there were three little pigs: Salty Bacon Pig, Porkella Chop Pig and Hamuel Bone Pig. They each set out to seek their fortune and build a home, one of straw, one of wood and one of brick; when they each encounter the Big Bad Wolf. But unlike the familiar fairy tale is the Wolf really bad? Maybe there are things going on we don't know about? Learn what really happened in one of CCT's most popular shows ever, full of laughter, fun and audience participation!

name: OSU Theatre: Eurydice
venue: Roy Bowen Theatre, The Ohio State University
description: Sarah Ruhl creates a tale based on the Greek myth of Orpheus that is exhilarating as we enter a surreal world, as lush and limpid as a dream (The New Yorker). On the day Eurydice is to marry her true love Orpheus, a misstep sends her to the surreal depths of the Underworld, where she has a surprising reunion and ultimately must decide whether to follow Orpheus back to the land of the living. The New York Times described Eurydice as a magical play with gripping emotional potency, a love letter to the world.

name: Echoes in Time Theatre: Should They Stay or Should They Go
description: It's the late 1840s and John Johnston, the first federal Indian agent in Ohio , ponders the course of his actions that has led to the removal of the last of the Native Americans from Ohio. Come listen as Johnston ponders aloud his actions over the past several years regarding the Federal government, the Native Americans and their subsequent removal from Ohio.

name: OSU Theatre: The Camouflage Project
venue: Thurber Theatre, The Ohio State University
description: The Camouflage Project is a devised piece created in collaboration with the Department of Theatre, Advanced Computing Center for the Arts and Design (ACCAD) and The Mershon Center. This new work is based on two aspects of clandestine activity in World War II: theatre artists who were conscripted to help in the war effort through their ability to produce a range of camouflage and women agents who were working behind enemy lines. The performance storyline highlights the work of women agents, many whose accomplishments have been concealed, erased or obscured for a variety of reasons

name: Bread and Circus Theatre: Zack
description: The half-witted son of a wedding purveyor, Zack has a good heart and cheerfulness that are far greater assets than his brother's crafty greed. This charming and uplifting story tells in the most amusing fashion how Zack eventually wins self-respect and his bride.

name: International Performing Arts for Families: The Tragical Life of Cheeseboy
description: Inside a magical traveling theater tent, a storyteller shares an enchanting and timeless tale. Cheeseboy's home planet has been reduced to a bubbling fondue. Where are his parents? How did he become marooned on earth? Wondrous, funny, and achingly familiar, Cheeseboy's journey leads him toward a new life filled with independence and new possibilities. Utilizing magic lantern-style shadow puppetry and ingenious "treasure boxes," this poignant performance will touch children and adults, too. For ages 7 and up.

name: Gallery Players: The Action Against Sol Schuman
description: Rounding out the season will be Jeffrey Sweet's drama, The Action Against Sol Schuman. Sol Schumann, a devout American Jew and beloved father of two grown sons, is accused of unspeakable crimes he allegedly had committed many years earlier. The two central forces of the drama are his sons, who in the course of tracking through the maze of legal, moral and personal issues on the sins of their father, also must come to terms with their relationships with him as their father's children.

name: Wex Lab: Improv Theater for Teens
description: Teens are invited to bring their best performances and explore new material in an improv theater workshop that includes drama games with Peter Cutts, a top-notch professional director and actor visiting the Ohio State from Britain. He'll bring his extensive experience in stage, film, and radio (offcutts.com) to this one-day intensive studio workshop. The group will be kept small and will fill quickly, so teens are asked to register early.

name: Actors' Theatre: The Scarlet Pimpernel
description: The Scarlet Pimpernel is a swashbuckling, romantic adventure set in the time of the French Revolution.

name: Central Ohio Folk Festival
description: This festival is always held on the first full weekend (including Friday) of May and is held at the Battelle-Darby Creek Metro Park. The Festival features 30 or more mini-concerts and teaching workshops, with a main-stage concert Saturday evening.

name: Civil War Encampment
address: Broad St.& High St., Columbus, OH 43215
description: The recently completed Ohio Statehouse hosted Civil War soldiers on their way to battle. Learn what camp life was like during the Civil War. Walk among soldiers' tents, see how to fire the cannon every hour and help the Ladies Aid Society deliver comfort to the troops. Historical re-enactors from 1st Ohio Light Artillery, Battery A and other groups will demonstrate Civil War life, cooking and medical practices. School tours are the focus on Friday and the public is welcome both days. Fun for the whole family!

name: Outdoor Health and Fitness Expo
description: If you are a runner or have family or friends that are, then you are going to want to make sure you get signed up for our Sasquatch 5K Trail Run/Walk. Unlike traditional 5Ks that are run on the streets, this run takes you through the trails of beautiful Camp Lazarus! If you aren’t a runner but want to learn more about staying healthy, then join us for our Family Hike and Expo following the run.

name: Pirate Weekend
description: Pirate re-enactors from around the country will participate in activities aboard the ship. They will storm the ship at 2 PM from the Scioto River and in the park.

name: Young Soloists 2011
description: The Young Soloists Ohio program started in 2003 to showcase outstanding talent in vocal and/or instrumental music presented by artists with disabilities in inclusive settings.

name: 7th Annual Birding by Ear Weekend
description: This workshop is a great way to learn bird vocalizations, meet new birding friends, see abundant grassland birds, learn to connect habitats with their inhabitants, and explore the uncharted bird spots at the Wilds. Classes and activities are available for beginner, intermediate, and expert birders. This weekend is facilitated by Al Parker, accomplished naturalist and professionally trained wildlife biologist.

name: Avian Photography Weekend
description: Head out on safari in search of migrating birds amid spectacular scenery - without ever leaving Ohio - at the Wilds, designated an "Important Bird Area" by the Audubon Society. At a pace that allows ample time to explore the decisive visual moments, you'll learn photo techniques from expert photographers and build your portfolio of stunning flora, landscapes, and wildlife during this exclusive opportunity. This weekend is facilitated by Jerry Jividen and Barbara Jividen of Naturally Wild Photo Adventures.

name: Green on the Green, A Big Green Fest!
address: St. Rt. 161 & High St., downtown Worthington, Worthington, 43085
description: Green on the Green, which first started in Worthington, Ohio in May of 2010, is back and better than ever! Not only will the original Worthington event double in size in 2011, but also we're adding more food, fun and live music. What Is Green on the Green? It's a free, one day, community festival providing visitors with a sampling of ways to go green including opportunities to buy re-purposed or recycled items, learning to appreciate native plants and animals, and educating folks on how to use less energy, produce less waste or adopt sustainable practices.

name: Zoombezi Bay Opening Day
description: Another fun-filled summer awaits you! Grab your swimsuits and get prepared for the return of the thrilling slides, extreme waves and rivers!

name: 4th Friday: Back to Nature
description: Find out what you've been missing right outside your backdoor during 4th Friday: Back to Nature in Historic Uptown Westerville. Enjoy activities and displays about plants, animals and various ways to enjoy wildlife and the great outdoors. The event will feature live entertainment, extended shopping hours and plenty of children's activities.

name: Family Friday Night
description: COSI stays open late for family-friendly fun the last Friday of every month! You can explore science, discover fun, and stay late! General admission is only $8 after 5 p.m. and includes all of COSI's permanent exhibitions plus a movie on the 7 story Extreme Screen theater, a savings of $11.75!

name: Dinosaurs: Explore, Escape, Survive
description: Dinosaurs stomp into COSI next summer in an exhibition featuring life-like animatronics dinos, simulator pods where you hunt, eat, and flee predators, and a maze where you'll uncover facts and fossils like a paleontologist in a Mesozoic adventure.

name: GrillMasters Festival
description: North Market will celebrate its sixth Grillmasters Festival over Memorial Day Weekend. The event has been expanded to two days this year and will emphasize grilling, techniques and sauces (the smoke) as well as putting a little bite into your recipes with spices and hot sauces (the fire). North Market Grillmasters Festival will take place May 28 and 29 and feature special barbeque and fiery foods vendors, cooking demonstrations, culinary contests, live music and entertainment for the kiddies.

name: Native American Traditional Pow Wow
admission: Weekend pass $15. Adults $7. Seniors and students $3. Children 5 and under free.
description: Native Americans celebrate their heritage and gather as their forefathers did in a traditional pow wow. Come learn about and enjoy native singing, dancing, food, music, arts and crafts. Come join the circle and celebrate the resiliency of our nations. Love, learn, honor, respect and have fun! Feel free to bring a chair.

name: And You Will Know Us By The Trail of Dead, Surfer Blood
Tim McGraw
venue: Value City Arena at the Jerome Schottenstein Center

name: Usher
venue: Value City Arena at the Jerome Schottenstein Center

name: Rock On The Range
address: One Black & Gold Boulevard, Columbus, OH 43211
description: Rock On The Range, America 's premier destination rock festival, is set for its Fifth Anniversary blowout. The Friday night Anniversary Party will feature some of the world's craziest throwback rock artists, to be announced in the coming weeks. Best of all, tickets to the Anniversary Party will be absolutely FREE with every ROCK ON THE RANGE weekend ticket purchase.

name: Nashville at The MAC: Thom Shuler & Friends
venue: Peggy R. McConnell Arts Center of Worthington
description: Musicians and songwriters have been drawn to Nashville, the Music City since the early 1900's, performing and producing songs of many different styles and genres. True to the uniqueness of the music, the MAC is presenting a series of performances, workshops and critiques by those who have risen to the top in the Nashville music business.

name: ProMusica Chamber Orchestra: Rhapsody in Blue Benefit & Concert
description: Prepare to be dazzled as pianist Gabriela Montero, internationally acclaimed for the revival of the lost art of classical improvisation, joins the Orchestra to close the season in style with the raw passion and poetic musicality of spontaneous composition. Montero will join the Orchestra on Friday, May 6 at the Southern Theatre to perform Gershwin's "Rhapsody in Blue."

name: Music in the Atrium: Maggie Green
description: Bossa nova & samba - sung in Portuguese - and American jazz standards by terrific Columbus vocalist Maggie Green.

name: Young Soloists 2011
description: The Young Soloists Ohio program started in 2003 to showcase outstanding talent in vocal and/or instrumental music presented by artists with disabilities in inclusive settings. Annually, VSA Ohio selects three musicians under the age of 25, as the Young Soloists of the Year. This is a state-level program of the International Young Soloist contest sponsored by VSA in Washington, DC. Winners of the international contest receive a cash prize and perform at the John F. Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts. The three winners are awarded cash prizes from $500 to $1,000 and will perform at the awards ceremony and silent auction benefiting VSA Ohio in May 2011.

name: Carpe Diem: The American Songwriter
description: Back by popular demand, American singer/songwriter Willy Porter will present new songs and fan favorites. Following a successful concert at BoMA this past March, we have invited Mr. Porter to return and present another weekend of fabulous arrangements of his songs with CDSQ.

name: Chamber Music Columbus: Cavani String Quartet
description: The Spring Festival Weekend allows students of any ability level, school age through adult, to participate in coachings and workshops with the Cavani String Quartet and CMC Faculty.

name: The Neville Brothers
venue: Jeanne B. McCoy Community Center for the Arts
description: The differences between the four Neville Brothers are as dramatic as the similarities that unite them. The source of the similarities is passionate funk, a feeling for blues-soaked deep pocket grooves that is the basis of their greatness and exalted place in our cultural history. For over 30 years The Nevilles have provoked, entertained and excited audiences around the globe.

name: The Pleasure of the Cup: Drinks of the Speakeasy
description: Join us in a trip back through time to a world of "blind pigs," bathtub gin and flappers. As you visit select Ohio Village buildings, listen to cool jazz tunes and sample some favorite drinks of the Prohibition era, like the "Mary Pickford" and "Satan's Whiskers." Be sure to watch out for the Anti-Saloon League members or, worse yet, the police! Must be 21 years of age.

name: Slainte Thursdays
description: Experience why Irish is an Attitude in Dublin during Slainte Thursday. Historic Dublin's multi-sensory grazing event features music, arts, casual shopping and upscale dining. It is a monthly opportunity for visitors to stroll, mingle and browse among quaint shops and attractive streetscapes--taking in Dublin's quaint historic district set upon the banks of the scenic Scioto River. Slainte [Slon-sha] is a friendly and welcoming Gaelic or Celtic Toast, similar to the English toast & To Your Health.

name: Columbus Jazz Orchestra: CJO By Request
description: You decide what the orchestra will play on this special all-request performance! Byron will be taking your requests throughout the year for this all-request show to cap off the season. Hear the best of the CJO, your personal favorites and more!

name: Six String Concerts: Eddie From Ohio
Concerts on the Creek
description: Enjoy free outdoor concerts.

name: Spring Concert
venue: Sullivant Theatre, The Ohio State University
description: Senior Projects, and other Undergraduate and Graduate Contemporary Dance Choreography.

name: Columbus Dance Theatre: New Dance Project
description: The Company Season concludes with New Dance Project in May. This concert features new original work by local and nationally recognized choreographers. Carpe Diem String Quartet will provide live musical accompaniment for this evening of premieres.

name: OSU Dance: Dance Uptown
venue: Mershon Auditorium, Wexner Center for the Arts
description: Choreographers Michael Kelly Bruce with BB King music; Susan Hadley with 60's Girl Band music; Olivier Tarpaga with live drumming and rock; LA Artist Sabela Grimes with hip hop.

name: Creekside Paddle Boats
description: Beginning Memorial Day to Labor Day.

name: Romantic Full Moon Canoe Trip
description: Join us to experience canoeing by the light of the full moon. The moons bright light reflects off the shimmering Hocking River to provide a truly romantic experience. Let your senses guide you in the wonders of nighttime canoeing. We push off at sunset and descend back to the canoe livery for an evening of relaxation. As the moon rises to light the way, you will be able to watch the wildlife setting in for the night.

name: Romantic Full Moon Canoe Trip
description: Join us to experience canoeing by the light of the moon. On this date we will canoe under the Waxing Crescent Moon. As the Moon moves around the Earth it becomes more illuminated and provides light that reflects off the Hocking River. In addition to the moon, we also provide tiki torches for each canoe to help navigate the river. The tiki torches also help in viewing the wildlife that will be settling in for the night. We push off at sunset and descend back to the canoe livery for an evening of relaxation. We will depart from the Canoe Livery an hour before sunset to Trip 1 Crockett’s Run. The trip is approximately 5 miles and 2 hours. We float back to the canoe livery and a roaring bonfire, roast smores, and enjoy a night of live entertainment.

name: Raptor Photo Shoot
description: Expand your raptor identification skills and your portfolio of stunning raptors in natural landscapes, during this exclusive opportunity. Staff from the Columbus Zoo and Aquarium will be on-hand with many birds of prey to photograph; all you need is a camera. Learn photo techniques from expert photographers, Jerry Jividen and Barbara Jividen of Naturally Wild Photo Adventures.

name: Flaming Torchlight Canoe Trip
description: Join us to experience canoeing by the light of the moon. On this date we will canoe under the Waxing Crescent Moon. As the Moon moves around the Earth it becomes more illuminated and provides light that reflects off the Hocking River. In addition to the moon, we also provide tiki torches for each canoe to help navigate the river. The tiki torches also help in viewing the wildlife that will be settling in for the night. We push off at sunset and descend back to the canoe livery for an evening of relaxation. We will depart from the Canoe Livery an hour before sunset to Trip 1 Crockett’s Run. The trip is approximately 5 miles and 2 hours. We float back to the canoe livery and a roaring bonfire, roast smores, and enjoy a night of live entertainment.

name: Asian Festival
description: The 17th annual Asian Festival showcases Asian culture and heritage with free admission, free parking and free shuttle services. 15 Asian ethnic groups are represented in this event, which will feature performances by outstanding artists from all over the world, along with hands-on art demonstrations, interactive dance, ethnic music, Tai Chi and martial arts workshops. Performance focus for 2011 is Philipino and Korean. Eat delicious Asian cuisine and enjoy art and crafts, and Asian games including Mahjong, Takraw and table tennis. Don't miss the Dragon Boat Exhibit in Genoa Park.

name: Thurber House Evenings With Authors: James B. Stewart
description: The author of the huge bestsellers, Den of Thieves and Disney War, James B. Stewart focuses his investigative eyes on the epidemic of perjury that is sweeping the national justice system in his latest triumph, Tangled Webs: How False Statements Are Undermining America: From Martha Stewart to Bernie Madoff. With many prosecutors, investigators, and participants speaking for the first time, Tangled Webs goes behind the scene of the trials of media and homemaking entrepreneur Martha Stewart; top White House political adviser Lewis "Scooter" Libby; home-run king Barry Bonds; and Wall Street money manager Bernard Madoff.

name: Ohioana Book Festival: Celebrating Ohio's Authors
description: The annual Ohioana Book Festival will feature noted Ohio writers, representing a diversity of literary styles and genres. Featured authors will participate throughout the day in panel discussions, readings and book signings.

name: Happy 100th Birthday, Edison!
description: The east wing of the Edison Middle and Intermediate School in Grandview Heights will be 100 years old in 2011!

name: Thurber House Literary Series: Justin Cronin
description: Justin Cronin also author of The Summer Guest and Mary and O'Neil, will appear.

name: Yappy Hour
description: Yappy Hour is back! Bring your dogs for a friendly mingle on the Library Lawn. We'll have treats, animal-themed music, and visits from local pet businesses & veterinarians.

name: May Herb Day
description: Join the Ohio Herb Education Center for May Herb Day. Activities include cooking demonstrations, entertainment, children's activities, and plant sales!

name: Mother's Day Brunch at Ohio Village
description: Treat your mother to an afternoon of food, fashion and fun at Ohio Village. Enjoy a delicious brunch in the American House Hotel, followed by "In Mother's Drawers," a historic fashion show featuring women's and children's fashions through the years in the Town Hall. Give her a Mother's Day treat she'll long remember!

name: Annual Senior Art Exhibition
description: Featuring the Juried works of Denison Studio Art Majors.

name: Exhibit: Same Difference and Other Meditations
description: New York artist Una-Kariim Cross investigates the very complicated subject of identity in Same Difference and Other Meditations, part of a larger project that takes the Human Genome Project as its starting point.

name: Retrospective: Charlie Chaplin
description: One of the most beloved, revered, and controversial film artists of the 20th century, Charlie Chaplin created some of our greatest film comedies, and his Little Tramp endures as one of the most internationally recognizable fictional characters. Born in England, Chaplin quickly became Hollywood royalty with an approach to comedy that emphasized character and pathos over more common varieties of slapstick. Although he enchanted audiences the world over, his tumultuous romantic life and political views were the subject of constant scrutiny by the FBI. Accused of Communist sympathies, he was denied reentry to the United States after attending the premiere of Limelight in England in 1952 and only returned in 1972 to receive an honorary Oscar.

name: Exhibit: Inside Looking Out
description: Inside Looking Out is a dual exhibition inspired by the windows, natural light and surrounding landscape of the Dublin Arts Council gallery. Painter David Jewell, who currently lives in Athens, Ohio, often creates interior scenes where a window, its light and view are significant parts of the composition. His landscapes will offer an interesting counterpoint to the interiors. Ceramicist Sara Gallo, who lives and works in Philadelphia, provides complement and contrast through an installation of glazed objects that are often displayed on walls in constellation-like compositions.

name: Exhibit: Tour of the ADA Mural: Liberty, Justice, and Access for All
description: The ADA Mural will be on display during Ohio Arts Day and 2011 Governor's Awards for the Arts in Ohio. The Journey: What does the ADA, access, and inclusion mean to you? 27 artists with disabilities from across Ohio answered that question in response to a call for art in June. Designed by artist, Kong Ho, the mural incorporated an array of images and words and now stands 6 feet tall and 30 feet wide. In addition to the artists, approximately 40 community members volunteered their time to assist with its construction. Together these Ohioans created a piece of art and advocacy that celebrates ability, inclusion, and looks ahead to work that must be done in the next 20 years.

name: Exhibit: Street Talk and Spiritual Matters: Aminah's Mt. Vernon Avenue
description: Aminah Robinson's RagGonNons, paintings, drawings, hogmawg sculptures, prints and books about Mt. Vernon Avenue, bring to life the heart of this African-American community that flourished on the eastside of Columbus until the early 1960s. The work typifies Aminah's passion with remembering and documenting the past in order to move forward. Aminah emphasizes the economic vibrancy and social activity of the neighborhood and also raises complex racial and political issues that were at play at the time. At the heart of the exhibition, are the scroll-like Memory Maps in which Aminah records every detail of the lively street life of Mt. Vernon Avenue. The street's storefronts, churches, theaters, and offices are the backdrop for Aminah's depictions of The Brownyskin Man, Umbrella Man, Organgrinder and dozens of other figures that populate the street. Many of these figures are also represented in sculptures, prints, and cloth paintings that demonstrate the artist's use of diverse media and techniques. The Memory Maps became the basis for Aminah's published book, A Street Called Home. Visitors will be able to gain insight into Aminah's creative process by examining her original art for the book and the study that preceded it. The time span represented in the work ranges from the early part of the twentieth century to the 1960s when construction of the interstate highway, urban planning, and civil rights demonstrations dramatically changed the tenor of the neighborhood. In an effort to bring the work alive and provide context for the art, we are video-taping individuals who have memories and stories about the street.

name: Ysaye & Friends
description: Referred to as "The King of the Violin" and the world's first modern violinist, Eugene Ysaye was a Belgian violinist, composer, and conductor. His intensely technical, neo-Romantic style triggered the inspiration for this program, which features Ballade and Polonaise by Henri Vieuxtemps; Poeme by Ernest Chausson; Ysaye's Solo Sonata No. 4; and Sonata by Cesar Franck. Vieuxtemps was Ysaye's mentor and a prominent advocate of the Franco-Belgian  violin school. Chausson composed Poeme for Ysaye, and it has been speculated that Ysaye wrote or substantially revised its violin part to showcase his giant palette of tonal color. Franck gifted this Sonata to Ysaye as a wedding present. Its four movements are believed to represent the four stages of life: childhood, adolescence, adulthood, and maturity.

They have played blues, swing, jazz, rock, country, old time, Irish, folk, classical and, of course, bluegrass. description: The Ohio Statehouse is celebrating and honoring important women in the history of Ohio throughout the month with tours of the Ladies' Gallery, a special exhibit and a program with Ohio's First Woman Adjutant General, Major General Deborah A. Ashenhurst.    An exhibit focusing on Harriet Taylor Upton features artifacts once belonging to this women's rights advocate and author. Artifacts in­clude letters sent to Upton from U.S. Presidents and other dignitaries, historical photographs and articles authored by Upton. The exhibit is presented in partnership with Ohioana Library and will be on view in the Ohio Statehouse Map Room throughout March.

name: Nightmares on High Street: Vanishing on 7th Street
description: An unexplained blackout plunges the city of Detroit into total darkness, and by the time the sun rises, only a few people remain-surrounded by heaps of empty clothing, abandoned cars and lengthening shadows. A small handful of strangers that have survived the night each find their way to a rundown bar, whose gasoline-powered generator and stockpile of food and drink make it the last refuge in a deserted city. With daylight beginning to disappear completely and whispering shadows surrounding the survivors, they soon discover that the enemy is the darkness itself, and only the few remaining light sources can keep them safe. As time begins to run out for them, darkness closes in and they must face the ultimate terror.

name: St. Patrick's Day Screening: Leprechaun
description: One day only for St. Patrick's Day! When Dan O'Grady returns to the U.S. after stealing some Irish leprechaun's pot of gold, he thinks he can settle down and enjoy his newfound wealth. He thought wrong. The leprechaun followed him and O'Grady barely gets away with his life, having locked the little monster in his basement. Ten years later, J.D. and his spoiled daughter Tory move in. By accident, the leprechaun is released and almost immediately the annoying creature starts to look for his gold, not displaying any respect for human life.

description: When a gigantic great white shark begins to menace the small island community of Amity, a police chief, a marine scientist and grizzled fisherman set out to stop it.

name: Nightmares on High Street: Black Death
description: The year is 1348. Europe has fallen under the shadow of the Black Death. As the plague decimates all in its path, fear and superstition are rife. In this apocalyptic environment, the church is losing its grip on the people. There are rumors of a village, hidden in marshland that the plague cannot reach. There is even talk of a necromancer who leads the village and is able to bring the dead back to life. Ulric (Sean Bean), a fearsome knight, is charged by the church to investigate these rumors. He enlists the guidance of a novice monk, Osmund (Eddie Redmayne) to lead him and his band of mercenary soldiers to the marshland, but Osmund has other motives for leaving his monastery. Their journey to the village and events that unfold take them into the heart of darkness and to horrors that will put Osmund's faith in himself and his love for God to the ultimate test.

name: Gasland
description: The largest domestic natural gas drilling boom in history has swept across the United States. The Halliburton-developed drilling technology of "fracking" or hydraulic fracturing has unlocked a "Saudia Arabia of natural gas" just beneath us. But is fracking safe? When filmmaker Josh Fox is asked to lease his land for drilling, he embarks on a cross-country odyssey uncovering a trail of secrets, lies and contamination. A recently drilled nearby Pennsylvania town reports that residents are able to light their drinking water on fire. This is just one of the many absurd and astonishing revelations of a new country called GASLAND.

name: Exhibit: Shared Intelligence: American Painting and the Photograph
admission: Adults $10. Seniors and students $8. Children under 6 free. Free admission on Sunday
description: Inspired by the Georgia O'Keeffe Museum Research Center's 2006 3-day symposium, Painting and Photography in American Art: Sources, Ideas and Influences, 1890s to the Present, this exhibition of 75 paintings and photographs explores the productive and fraught relationship of these two mediums in American modern art that has been ongoing since the last decades of the 19th century. It focuses on the work of painters for whom photography has been essential, among them Robert Bechtle, Chuck Close, Thomas Eakins, Audrey Flack, David Hockney, Georgia O'Keeffe, Ben Shahn, Charles Sheeler, and Andy Warhol. This traveling exhibition also includes works from CMA such as our Norman Rockwell and Kehinde Wiley.

name: Exhibit: For Todd DeVriese: In Celebration of a Beautiful Life
description: Cherished colleague (OSU Associate Professor 1996-2001), spectacular graduate student (MFA 1992), civic leader (Director of the Ohio State Fair arts exhibition; Vice-President and Board member of the Ohio Art League 1995-2000), and always an insightful and prolific artist: for over a decade Todd DeVriese touched the arts community of central Ohio in a myriad of ways. He went on to become Associate Professor and Chair of the Art Department, and later Dean of the College of Arts and Sciences at Zayed University, United Arab Emirates before leading the School of Art at Texas Tech University in Lubbox as Professor and Director. In 2009, Todd joined Minnesota's St. Cloud State University as the Dean of Fine Arts and Humanities where he served until his death last November.  Todd's commitment to higher education and the vital power of the arts was central to his life. With works on loan from private and public collections and the artist's own studio, the Hopkins and Kuhn Galleries are honored to present these exhibitions celebrating the life and art of Todd DeVriese.

name: Exhibit: Street Talk and Spiritual Matters: Aminah's Mt. Vernon Avenue
description: Aminah Robinson's RagGonNons, paintings, drawings, hogmawg sculptures, prints and books about Mt. Vernon Avenue, bring to life the heart of this African-American community that flourished on the eastside of Columbus until the early 1960s. The work typifies Aminah's passion with remembering and documenting the past in order to move forward. Aminah emphasizes the economic vibrancy and social activity of the neighborhood and also raises complex racial and political issues that were at play at the time. At the heart of the exhibition, are the scroll-like Memory Maps in which Aminah records every detail of the lively street life of Mt. Vernon Avenue. The street's storefronts, churches, theaters, and offices are the backdrop for Aminah's depictions of The Brownyskin Man, Umbrella Man, Organgrinder and dozens of other figures that populate the street. Many of these figures are also represented in sculptures, prints, and cloth paintings that demonstrate the artist's use of diverse media and techniques. The Memory Maps became the basis for Aminah's published book, A Street Called Home. Visitors will be able to gain insight into Aminah's creative process by examining her original art for the book and the study that preceded it. The time span represented in the work ranges from the early part of the twentieth century to the 1960s when construction of the interstate highway, urban planning, and civil rights demonstrations dramatically changed the tenor of the neighborhood. In an effort to bring the work alive and provide context for the art, we are video-taping individuals who have memories and stories about the street.

name: Columbus Children's Theatre: Cinderella

Its recreation in 1965 starring Lesley Ann Warren was no less successful y in transporting a new generation to the miraculous kingdom of dreams-come-true, and so was a second remake in 1997, which starred Brandy as Cinderella and Whitney Houston as her Fairy Godmother. Adapted for the stage, with great warmth and more than a touch of hilarity, the hearts of children and adults alike still soar when the slipper fits.

Take in the sweeping views along the lakes, woodlands, and wetlands of these unique lands. Breathe in the fresh air. Sweat a little. Smile a lot. Join hundreds of others in a day not to be missed.

name: Extreme Screen Film: Dolphins
description: Imagine floating in the crystalline, turquoise waters of the Bahamas. Swimming alongside you are some of the most graceful and extraordinary creatures on earth—wild dolphins. From the dazzling coral reefs of the Bahamas to the wind-swept seas of Patagonia, go under the water’s surface for a romp with inquisitive Atlantic spotted dolphins, acrobatic dusky dolphins and the familiar bottlenose dolphin. Follow marine biologist, Dr. Kathleen Dudzinski, Dr. Bernd Würsig and Dr. Alejandro Acevedo-Gutierrez, as they research the communication of wild dolphins with innovative scientific methods. From rarely seen fish-herding behavior to a close-up look at complex communication activities, Dolphins offers a fascinating new perspective on the lives of dolphins and their remarkable intelligence.

name: 5th Annual Voice of the City Vocal Competition
description: The best 20 singers' ages 8 to 21 from around the state will compete. Cash prizes will be awarded, and the competition's winner will receive a grand prize of $1,000.

name: Birth of the Cool: Jazz & Poetry
description: Explore the relationship of jazz and poetry, its rhythmic and lyrical styles and its historical context, particularly in relationship to the cool jazz period of post-war United States.

name: Jazz and Poetry with William Evans
description: Explore the relationship of jazz and poetry, its rhythmic and lyrical styles and its historical context, particularly in relationship to the "cool jazz" period of post war United States.

name: Jazz Arts Group's Inside Track: Trombone Shorty & Orleans Avenue with Stretch Lefty
description: Rare indeed is the artist with the virtuosity to draw the unqualified respect of some of the most iconic legends in jazz and the ability to deliver a high-energy funk rock show capable of mesmerizing international rock stars. A virtuoso prodigy trombonist, brilliant trumpet player, and soulful, charismatic singer, Trombone Shorty commands the stage while emanating an elegance and class gleaned from his successful studies at the prestigious New Orleans Center for the Creative Arts.

name: The Columbus Symphony: Beethoven's "Eroica"
description: Guest conductor Mei-Ann Chen will lead the Columbus Symphony in their final program of the 2010-11 classical season. Featuring guest cellist Nathaniel Rosen and guest violinist Axel Strauss, the program will include "the three Bs" of classical music - Bach (Ricercare No. 2 from Musical Offering), Beethoven (Symphony No. 3, Eroica), and Brahms (Double Concerto). WOSU's Christopher Purdy will hold a free, pre-concert lecture about the program for ticket holders one hour prior to each performance on the fourth floor of the Ohio Theatre's Galbreath Pavilion.

name: Nashville Singer/Songwriter Series: Irene Kelley with Melissa Greener
venue: Peggy R. McConnell Arts Center of Worthington
description: Musicians and songwriters have been drawn to Nashville, the Music City since the early 1900's, performing and producing songs of many different styles and genres. True to the uniqueness of the music, the MAC is presenting a series of performances, workshops and critiques by those who have risen to the top in the Nashville music business.

name: Birth of the Cool: Jazz & Poetry
description: Explore the relationship of jazz and poetry, its rhythmic and lyrical styles and its historical context, particularly in relationship to the cool jazz period of post-war United States.

name: The Birth of the Cool workshop
description: Birth of the Cool is the name of a compilation album by American jazz musician Miles Davis, but has come to signify a movement in American music. Cool jazz, which became prominent during the Second World War, stands as an important reaction to bebop, (characterized by fast tempos and instrumental virtuosity) in that the music was intricately arranged with a composed sound along with improvised sections. Join Mark Flugge to learn about this important era in American music history - from the arrangements and instrumentation to the historical context and the artists associated with the movement.

name: Sunday At Central: The High Street Four
description: The High Street Four has already performed the complete cycle of Ludwig van  Beethoven and Johannes Brahms string quartets, and now aims to rediscover all of  Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart’s late quartets. The program for this particular concert  explores Beethoven’s String Quartet No. 12 (Op. 127), Mozart’s String Quartet No. 20  (K. 499), and Hugo Wolf’s Italian Serenade. Opus 127 is the first of Beethoven’s late  quartets and has been regarded as one of the composer’s greatest final achievements.  Mozart’s Quartet K. 499, one of a set of six dedicated to Franz Joseph Haydn, is  sometimes referred to as Hoffmeister, as Mozart wrote the piece in honor of his  friend Franz Anton Hoffmeister. The whimsical Italian Serenade marked the beginning  of a strikingly mature turning point in Wolf’s career.

name: OSU 2011 Contemporary Music Festival
description: This year’s festival pays tribute to Composer-In-Residence Donald Harris, who recently retired his professorship at OSU after 22 years of service, and who has made a passionate, prolific 44-year contribution to classical music.

name: 24 Hour Comic Day
description: Wild Goose Creative is at it again with yet another 24-hour event.  Following in the wake of 24-hour Theater, 24-hour poetry, and a collaborative textile arts project called Piecing for Cover, Wild Goose is proud to present 24 Hour Comics.  Our artists will gather on April 2nd and begin creating, with the end goal of finishing 24 hours later with a 24 page original comic.  These comics will be gathered and printed as an anthology.

name: Jerry Seinfeld
description: By popular demand, America's premier comedian is hitting the road in a return to his first love - stand-up comedy. Hailed as "the master stand-up comic of his generation" and "the best comedian of our time" in a Washington Post article by Tom Shales, Seinfeld has an uncanny ability to joke about the little things in life that relate to audiences everywhere.

name: Columbus Comedy Festival
description: Wild Goose Creative, a non-profit arts organization in Columbus, and the Columbus Comedy Collective, an organization of local comedians, are pleased to announce the second annual Columbus Comedy Festival. The Columbus Comedy Festival is open to the public (recommended 18+) and will feature stand-up, sketch comedy, improv, music, video, and more.

name: Romantic Full Moon Canoe Trip
description: Join us to experience canoeing by the light of the moon. On this date we will canoe under the Waxing Crescent Moon. As the Moon moves around the Earth it becomes more illuminated and provides light that reflects off the Hocking River. In addition to the moon, we also provide tiki torches for each canoe to help navigate the river. The tiki torches also help in viewing the wildlife that will be settling in for the night. We push off at sunset and descend back to the canoe livery for an evening of relaxation. We will depart from the Canoe Livery an hour before sunset to Trip 1 Crockett's Run. The trip is approximately 5 miles and 2 hours. We float back to the canoe livery and a roaring bonfire, roast smores, and enjoy a night of live entertainment.

name: Columbus Commons Grand Opening
address: High Street between State and Rich, Columbus, OH 43215
description: Located in the center of downtown, Columbus Commons will be a six-acre pedestrian-friendly gathering space with a grassy park, walking paths and a covered stage all surrounded by flower beds and trees. The project is being built on site of the former City Center mall. Overtime, Columbus Commons will transform into a full-fledged neighborhood consisting of multi-story buildings with residential units above street-level retail, office buildings and entertainment venues. A grand opening is planned for May 26, 2011.

name: Flaming Torchlight Canoe Trip
description: Join us to experience canoeing by the light of the moon. On this date we will canoe under the Waxing Crescent Moon. As the Moon moves around the Earth it becomes more illuminated and provides light that reflects off the Hocking River. In addition to the moon, we also provide tiki torches for each canoe to help navigate the river. The tiki torches also help in viewing the wildlife that will be settling in for the night. We push off at sunset and descend back to the canoe livery for an evening of relaxation. We will depart from the Canoe Livery an hour before sunset to Trip 1 Crockett's Run. The trip is approximately 5 miles and 2 hours. We float back to the canoe livery and a roaring bonfire, roast smores, and enjoy a night of live entertainment.

name: New Behind-the-Scenes Tours: Civil War Collections
description: Participants will get an exclusive, guided tour through the Ohio Historical Society’s Civil War objects and collections that aren’t on exhibit and are stored in areas not open to the public. This tour will focus on the flags, weapons, military accessories and clothing related to the Civil War era in and around Ohio .

name: Civil War Lecture
description: Lessons of the American Civil War Through Music.

name: Ride of Silence: Columbus (Bicycle)
description: The Ride of Silence is a slow group ride, akin to a funeral procession, in total silence. The ride is a safe, responsible, professional and mature response to the aggressiveness, intimidation, and carnage that cyclists face on the roads we ride. It is a means to: remember and mourn those killed by motorists, raise awareness that our community has, and supports, a large population of cyclists, show the public that cyclists are not going to stop riding on the roads, point out that we ask for respect from motorists, remind motorists that we wish only to SHARE the roads. Riders should gather on the South Side (State St.) of the Statehouse.

name: Tours of the historic Kelton House Museum & Garden
description: Costumed tour guides lead visitors through the 1852 home of Fernando & Sophia Kelton.

name: Photography Workshop: Macro and Close-Up Photography
description: Photographer Vincent Nobel will lead an interactive discussion to explore the intimate side of nature with a one-day workshop for macro and close-up photography.

name: Short North Gala
description: The Gala is a highly experiential affair that immerses guests in the flavors and spirit of the Arts District. The evening begins with cocktails, hors' dourves and entertainment in the Greek Orthodox Cathedral's garden courtyard. Short North bars, taverns and spirit district businesses feature their specialty cocktails. Following cocktails, the celebration transitions to the Cathedral's ballroom where PageTech Ltd., Zen Genius and the galleries of the Short North reshape the space with light, sound, projection, decor and art. The evening shifts to a higher gear as acclaimed Short North chefs take center stage to create a one-night-only culinary adventure of samplings of their best dish.

name: Charles Kleibacker Endowed fund for Excellence
description: The Kleibacker Series: Showcasing Excellence in Art, Culture & Design kicks off with a reception in the Museum's newly renovated Derby Court followed by a presentation by celebrated fashion designer Isabel Toledo and author, illustrator and sculptor Ruben Toledo.

name: Papergirl Columbus
description: Paper Girl is a show, an urban action (the distribution of the rolls of art), a bicycle workshop and a party. In a nutshell it is: participatory, analog, non-commercial and impulsive. Anyone can participate, you can submit artwork and/or help distribute.  Papergirl is distributed like a newspaper, but consists of original artwork rolled in a tube.  You submit artwork in person or via mail, we have a show, we roll the artwork in to tubes, we get together on our bicycles to distribute the work around town to anyone.  The work is not for sale; it is given to the public by chance for free. It is intended to take art distribution out of the galleries and into the streets, via direct delivery to the public in the style of the American paperboy.

name: A Night with Captain Sig & Hillstrand Brothers of Deadliest Catch
description: Captains Johnathan and Andy Hillstrand of the Time Bandit, along with Captain Sig Hansen of the Northwestern, will be making an appearance in Columbus! During these one-of-a kind events, the captains will take the audience through some toughest situations they've had to face on the high seas. Hear how it really goes down straight from the captains themselves!

name: Global Watchdogs: Reporter Safety, Social Media & the Future of Journalism
description: Peter Hiscocks has worked extensively around the world with broadcast journalists and private and state broadcasting organizations. A former journalist on a number of British national newspapers, he worked with the BBC for more than 21 years - from radio reporter to television executive - and has won a number of awards for his work in news and current affairs.

name: Midwest Fair Trade Fest
description: Global Gallery and Ohio Students for Fair Trade will be hosting the first ever Midwest Fair Trade Fest to celebrate World Fair Trade Day! This day long festival and conference will embrace culture and educate our community on Fair Trade practices. Our event will feature cultural performances from a wide range of international dance and musical groups, Fair Trade and Green vendors, renowned speakers on Fair Trade and sustainability issues, and ethnic foods from Global Gallery's Global Kitchen.

name: COSI After Dark
description: For ages 21 and over, with great exhibits, great drinks, and great fun. Includes parking and $4 in food/drink vouchers.

name: Sunbury Memorial Day Flea Market
description: Come to Sunbury and visit more than 150 vendors offering timeless treasures, crafts, antiques, plants and food. Antique shops surround the square and two other flea markets are held nearby.

name: U.S. Women's National Team vs. Japan
address: One Black & Gold Boulevard, Columbus, OH 43211

name: Comedy Town Improv
description: Comedy Town Improv featuring Shake-n-Bake, a special mash-up of the short form troupes Fake Bacon and The Shimmy Shake Project, doing their patent-pending set of games, songs, and shenanigans.

name: Exhibit: Fur, Fins, & Feathers
admission: Adults $10. Seniors and student 6 and older $8. Children 5 and under free. Admission is free every Sunday.
description: Fur, Fins, & Feathers, a family-friendly exhibition about animals in art, showcases works from CMA's permanent collection. This diverse exhibition includes a variety of media and styles such as Innuit stone carvings, wooden African headdresses, contemporary photography, and American folk art prints. Fur, Fins, & Feathers includes many works which visitors may not have seen before. Enhanced programming related to the exhibition will include hands-on activities, tours, and visits from other community organizations such as Children's Theater and the Columbus Zoo and Aquarium.

name: African American Heritage Festival
venue: Throughout The Ohio State University campus
description: The annual festival traditionally brings thousands of visitors to Columbus and is a time for people of all ages and walks to celebrate African-American history and culture.

name: OSU 2011 Contemporary Music Festival
description: This year's festival pays tribute to Composer-In-Residence Donald Harris, who recently retired his professorship at OSU after 22 years of service, and who has made a passionate, prolific 44-year contribution to classical music.

name: Children's Art Studio
venue: Peggy R. McConnell Arts Center of Worthington
description: Explore traditional Japanese arts including Sumi Painting, Origami paper folding, and more.

name: Columbus Children's Theatre Cinderella Ball
admission: $100 Adult, $50 Students, ages 13-20, and $25 Children 13 and under.
description: Families are invited to bring children and participate in the wonder and excitement of a royal event. All in attendance will dine with Cinderella and the Royal Court. The evening includes a silent auction, dancing, and court jesters who will entertain throughout the evening. Additionally, each princess in attendance will have an opportunity to try on the glass slipper.

name: Family Adventures
description: Share ideas, laugh, and play games during this docent-guided experience. Your family team may embark on a scavenger hunt, imagine yourselves inside a painting, or discover a work of art that tells a family story. Family Adventures are a great way to share quality time and make new memories together.

name: Second Sundays at Kelton House: Trails of Hope
description: A series of historical re-enactments depicting the struggles for freedom on the Underground Railroad.

name: Victorian Tea at Kelton House: April Showers Tea
description: Throughout the year, the Kelton House offers Victorian-inspired teas with a tasteful sampling of savories and sweets reminiscent of 19th century ladies' get-togethers. The menu for each Tea is different, but is always accompanied by traditional Earl Grey tea.

name: Tourism at the Ohio Penitentiary
admission: Adults $8. Seniors $7. Children 6-12 $4. Includes admission to the Ohio Historical Center.
description: Liz Plummer of the Ohio Historical Society's Archives/Library is your guide for a trip to the years before 1930, when touring the Ohio Penitentiary was a highlight of any visit to Columbus. For 25 cents you could stroll the prison yard, take a paddleboat ride, see the electric chair, and buy ice cream and postcards.

name: Family Adventures
description: Share ideas, laugh, and play games during this docent-guided experience. Your family team may embark on a scavenger hunt, imagine yourselves inside a painting, or discover a work of art that tells a family story. Family Adventures are a great way to share quality time and make new memories together.

name: Home School Days
description: Home School Days 2011 will commemorate the 150th anniversary of the American Civil War. Bring the Canal Era to life with the history tour called Civil War on the Home Front. Special Home School Days pricing and self-guided tours.

name: Eco-Thon at The Wilds
description: Immerse yourself in the beautiful environment of the Wilds. Serious runners and casual walkers alike are invited to participate in the 10K Trail Run, 5K Trail Run or 5K Trail Walk through the beautiful environment of the Wilds to help support the important conservation science and education programs that the Wilds offers. Take in the sweeping views along the lakes, woodlands and wetlands of these unique lands.

name: Wonderland Science Fair
description: We know you remember the third grade. We're inviting you to re-live the fun. Come with our invention. It's a science fair! Would-be scientists and at-home tinker's here is your chance to experiment in public.

name: Shadowbox Live: Fantasies
description: This spring, escape reality and enter a realm with no boundaries with Shadowbox Live's newest themed show Fantasies. Deliciously delusional original sketch comedy and rock 'n' roll prove that in Fantasies anything is possible.

name: Sophia's Secret
description: Tour the historic Kelton House Museum, with its wonderful collection of 19th century furnishings and decorative arts. Be greeted at the door by Sophia Kelton who will let you in on the family secret. You'll be sworn to secrecy before you leave after hearing the punishment handed out to abolitionists like the Keltons.

name: Tour and Tea with Sophia
description: The Keltons were a prosperous Columbus family that left a home full of artifacts that tell the story of 19th century Columbus life. After being greeted at the door by Sophia Kelton, you'll tour her beautifully furnished Victorian home and then be invited to afternoon tea with finger sandwiches and trifle.

name: Tours of the Historic Kelton House Museum & Garden
description: Costumed tour guides lead visitors through the 1852 home of Fernando & Sophia Kelton.

name: Civil War Comes to Columbus Tour
description: Even though there were no battles fought in Columbus, Ohio, during the Civil War, the City was knee-deep in plans and actions regarding it. Come along with Capital City Tours as we walk in the footsteps of Union soldiers and doomed Confederate prisoners, fiery abolitionists and desperate runaways, heroes, villains and ordinary people struggling to survive one of the most extraordinary times in our nation's history. Brother against brother, father against son. Never has this country been socially strained as much. Join us as we explore Columbus' Civil War past.

name: Music @ the MAC: Jim Volk
venue: Peggy R. McConnell Arts Center of Worthington
description: Jim's "Blue Wheels" has been traveling nation-wide with great critical acclaim and daily airplay across the country. Recently, the song Mistress Of The House was awarded first place in the solo instrumental category and the album second place in the Just Plain Folks 2002 music awards. Volk received five nominations in the largest music awards event in history out of nearly 8,000 album and over 100,00 song submissions. Jim has performed at the MAC before and we are happy to have him back. Presented in conjunction with the Ohio Fingerstyle Guitar Club

name: Exhibit: Controversy: Pieces You Don't Normally See
description: Controversy features five objects, including electric chair from the old Ohio Penitentiary, a Ku Klux Klan robe and hood, a sheepskin condom, a crib-bed cage that restrained patients at a state mental institution and a thumb mitt once used to prevent children from sucking their thumbs. The approach to the exhibit is unusual because it focuses on a limited collection of objects and provides limited interpretation of the objects for the visitor. Programs, scheduled each month throughout the run of the exhibit, will explore topics ranging from the creation of the exhibit to the meaning of objects to social issues connected to each of the items on display. By providing opportunities for shared dialogue and reflection, the Ohio Historical Society hopes to foster a better understanding of the past and how historical events, topics and issues impact our life today.

name: Don't Spit In The Finger Bowl
admission: Adults $8. Seniors $7. Children 6-12 $4. Includes admission to the Ohio Historical Center.
description: Join us as we walk through the 19th century discovering the etiquette and manners of our early American society, though our European cousins referred to Americans as rude, crude, back woodsy and socially unacceptable.

name: Living History
admission: Adults $8. Seniors $7. Children 6-12 $4. Includes admission to the Ohio Historical Center.
description: Encounter live people from Ohio's past among our exhibits, who'll shed light on history from a personal point of view.

name: Opening Day: Ohio Village Muffins Vintage Baseball vs. Columbus Capitals
description: Enjoy baseball the way it was meant to be played-no gloves, no spitting, no swearing-no kidding! There's nothing like the experience of a vintage game to take you back in time.

name: The 1913 Flood
description: For five days in March 1913, incessant rain across Ohio brought flooding, death and destruction to the Miami and Scioto River valleys. Tom Rieder of the society's Archives/Library tells how this horrific natural disaster changed the face of Ohio, through photographs, first person accounts and other resources.

name: Ohio Civil War 150 Brunch
description: Meet Wes Cowan on the PBS's History's Detectives, speaker for a brunch benefiting conservation of Civil War flags in the Ohio Historical Society's care, who'll talk about why our state's Civil War story is just as important today as it was 150 years ago.

name: Ohio Civil War 150 Commemoration Kickoff
address: Broad St.& High St, Columbus, OH 43215
description: Be there as the Ohio National Guard, Civil War 150 Commission, Ohio Historical Society and Ohio Statehouse kick off Ohio's Civil War sesquicentennial commemoration by recreating the 1861 mustering of troops for the 1st Ohio Infantry. See Civil War and modern military displays.

name: Community Conversation: Why an Exhibit on Controversy?
description: This is the first major discussion event in conjunction with the exhibit. Panelists who were involved in the creation of the exhibit will discuss why the exhibit was planned for now and what the process has been like.

name: New Behind-the-Scenes Tours: Civil War Collections
description: Participants will get an exclusive, guided tour through the Ohio Historical Society's Civil War objects and collections that aren't on exhibit and are stored in areas not open to the public. This tour will focus on the flags, weapons, military accessories and clothing related to the Civil War era in and around Ohio .

name: Sneak Peeks: Civil War Collections
description: Take an exclusive small-group behind-the-scenes tour of Civil War objects in the Ohio Historical Society's collections, focusing on flags, weapons, military accessories and clothing.

name: Genealogy Workshop: Records from Ohio's Prisons, Asylums and Children's Homes
description: Records of Ohio's state-operated and other public institutions can offer family historian's valuable information. Learn how to search records of the Penitentiary, State Reformatory, Women's Reformatory, behavioral, healthcare and developmental disabilities institutions. Boys and Girls Industrial Schools, School for the Deaf, and children's homes.

name: Ohio Village Muffins Vintage Baseball vs. Mansfield Independents
description: Enjoy baseball the way it was meant to be played-no gloves, no spitting and no swearing-no kidding! There's nothing like the experience of a vintage game to take you back in time.

name: Women Who Fought in the Civil War
admission: Adults $8. Seniors $7. Children 6-12 $4. Includes admission to the Ohio Historical Center.
description: Learn about the women who served their country during the Civil War.

name: Archaeology Projects
admission: Adults $8. Seniors $7. Children 6-12 $4. Includes admission to the Ohio Historical Center.
description: Meet an Ohio Historical Society archaeologist and hear about some recent projects.

name: Columbus, Cocktails and Culture
description: We have partnered with CYP for a unique tour that is part of their culture series. Enjoy a historic downtown bus tour (with 3 special stops along the way at Historical Buildings) and a locally catered pre-tour reception at the Columbus Historical Society gallery featuring Middle West Spirits, Yellow Brick Pizza, Angry Baker, and appearance by a local magician!

name: Packing Up Your Winter Coat
description: Tips in packing up textiles.

name: Music @ the MAC: Quartet Toujours
venue: Peggy R. McConnell Arts Center of Worthington
description: Chamber Music Connection will be presenting a special concert in the Main Gallery. The evening's program will consist of Chamber Music Connection Competition Ensembles featuring Quartet Toujours and additional outstanding chamber groups from CMC.

name: Carpe Diem: Banjo Mojo
description: Discover the hypnotically beautiful sound of banjo and strings, with a program ranging from renaissance madrigals to traditional old-timey folk songs. Graeme Boone (Ohio State University) is a magician, creating unique colors and textures that weave together with the strings for an unforgettable evening.

name: OWU Music Department presents Opera Theater
venue: Jemison Auditorium-Sanborn Hall, Ohio Wesleyan University

name: Six String Concerts: Irene Kelley
venue: Peggy R. McConnell Arts Center of Worthington

name: Jefferson's Signature Series
description: Join us as Jefferson Academy of Music presents the Jefferson's Signature Series of chamber music concerts in Cardinal Health Auditorium. In April immerse yourself in selections from QUBE, a string quartet with German pianist Maria Staeblein.

name: Sunday At Central: The High Street Four
description: The High Street Four has already performed the complete cycle of Ludwig van  Beethoven and Johannes Brahms string quartets, and now aims to rediscover all of  Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart's late quartets. The program for this particular concert  explores Beethoven's String Quartet No. 12 (Op. 127), Mozart's String Quartet No. 20  (K. 499), and Hugo Wolf's Italian Serenade. The whimsical Italian Serenade marked the beginning  of a strikingly mature turning point in Wolf's career.

name: Music @ the MAC: Standard Time
venue: Peggy R. McConnell Arts Center of Worthington
description: Led by Matt Ellis, Standard Time is a group with Worthington roots and the members have toured nationally. A five piece acoustical ensemble, Standard Time serves up hip jazz standards for your listening pleasure.

name: Wild West at Wild Goose!
description: Over the past two years the country music scene in Columbus has grown from a once a month show featuring small handful of rotating guests to a close-knit community that hosts regular musical events and featuring bands that boast booking calendars extending far into 2012. The movement recently culminated in a Johnny Cash tribute show that saw over 400 people come through the doors of The Shruken Head!

name: CityMusic: Beyond the Pale
description: For over a decade Toronto's Beyond the Pale has been making its distinctive brand of boundary-busting Eurofolk fusion, mixing Klezmer, Balkan, and Romanian styles with an eclectic range of North American influences.

name: Women of Faith: Imagine
description: Up to 10,000 women are expected to gather from Columbus and the surrounding areas for a much-needed opportunity to connect with one another and be encouraged as a diverse array of music artists, authors, and performers take the stage in a weekend designed to offer a refreshing getaway filled with laughter and hope. Attendees will not only hear from long-time Women of Faith speakers, but also become acquainted with new voices on the Women of Faith roster.

name: Exhibit: Expressions of Goodwill
venue: Peggy R. McConnell Arts Center of Worthington
description: Expressions of Goodwill, is an exhibition showcasing the work of the Columbus Goodwill Art Studio & Gallery. Artists with disabilities and other barriers have collaborated with each other, professional artists and art educators to discover new skills and explore new techniques based on their own strengths and desires.

name: Outside the Transmogrifier: Todd Hickerson and Juan Carrera
description: A year ago ceramacist Todd Hickerson asked painter Juan Carrera to share the space at Gallery 831 with him for 'Outside the Box.' After the overwhelmingly positive response the show received, with the favorable review Paintings, boxes are oddly complimentary and even a 'Best of 2010: ART' nod in The Other Paper, the boys of Clayspace were compelled to bring their 2 man show back for an all new installment of raku-fired boxes and abstract expressive paintings. Playing off of the [box] once again, 'Outside the Transmogrifier' humorously references the fictional device made out of a box, used by comic strip characters, Calvin and Hobbes.

name: Introductory Potter's Wheel Class
description: This class will cover basic throwing techniques as well as trimming, glazing, texturing, and use of colored slips.

name: After School Class for Teens
description: Bring your ideas or find them here and explore your creativity with clay. This class will use structural and hand building techniques to create functional and nonfunctional expressive ceramic works.

name: Face2Face: 25 Years of Art and Community
description: Studios on High Gallery celebrates its 25th Anniversary with, "Face 2 Face, 25 Years of Art and Community," an exhibition of new works by current members and alumni, showcasing the gallery's history and longevity in the Midwest art scene.

name: Perkins Observatory
description: Star gazing with the 32-inch Schottland Telescope.

name: Equine Affaire
admission: Adult $14 or a 4-day pass $48. Child $8 or a 4-day pass $28.
description: The nation's premiere equine exposition & equestrian gathering will feature four days of educational clinics, seminars, and demonstrations by top professionals in the horse industry, as well as an extensive trade show, Breed Pavilion, Youth Pavilion & evening entertainment. The Pfizer Fantasia is a Musical Celebration of the Horse (separate ticket required).

name: Fuel Cells and Other Emerging Technologies for a Smarter, Green Future
venue: Schimmel/Conrades Science Center, Ohio Wesleyan University

name: Immigrantification: Global Immigration and Landscape Changes
venue: Hamilton-Williams Campus Center, Ohio Wesleyan University
description: The 26th Annual Joseph and Edith Vogel Lecture featuring OWU assistant professor of geography David Walker, Ph.D.

name: Uncorked! Wine Club
description: If you enjoy wonderful wine, fabulous food, and entertaining tales of art, this is the place to be. On the first Thursday of every month, the Museum features wine and food pairings inspired by a painting or an artist in a relaxed social setting. The program includes wines provided by our wine purveyor, delicious food tastings from Chef Don Wood, and art vignettes by the Museum staff.

name: REBOOT: Mike Rozzi & Josh Manning
description: REBOOT is a reunion between Josh and Mike after a 3 year hiatus not working alongside each other in a common studio and symbolizes a re-start of interaction and influence between the 2. REBOOT is an exhibition of functional ceramics: platters, bowls, pitchers and jars.

name: Clay Bird Houses Workshop
description: 3 Saturdays in April, participants in this 3-part workshop will design, construct and decorate a birdhouse with clay. Students will construct their castles using clay slabs and basic hand building techniques. Texture and colored slips will be used for decoration. Glaze will be applied at the final session.

name: OFGC Pickin' Parties
venue: Peggy R. McConnell Arts Center of Worthington
description: Over the first year of the McConnell Art Center's existence, Ohio Fingerstyle Guitar Club members have been instrumental in helping to get the Thursday Night Concert Series off the ground - as both audience members and performers. In that time, the MAC has become the unofficial "home" of the OFGC.

name: Raku Party
description: Participants will glaze a handmade piece of pottery and watch as it's fired in our raku kiln by resident artist Todd Hickerson. The work is heated to 1850 degrees F, then the kiln is opened and the work is removed with tongs and placed in metal cans filled with combustible material. The cans are then covered and the fire reacts with the glaze to create iridescent and metallic effects on the pottery. Finally the pieces are submerged in water and guests can take their work home with them.

name: Jury Room Jeopardy
description: Join the Jury Room, North Market Spices and Columbus Historical Society in this high-energy night to jump-start your week! Come test your trivia skills or just come to learn something new!

name: Alaina Sheer Discusses Future of Marketing as Career
description: The Woltemade Center for Business, Economics and Entrepreneurship presents Alaina Sheer discussing the future of marketing as a career.

name: A Polar Affair
description: Polar Bears Aurora and Anana play host to this special night at Polar Frontier. This business casual event is a great way to learn more about Polar Bears and the Arctic ecosystem with guest speaker Robert W. Buchanan, President and CEO of Polar Bears International. Ticket includes 2 drink tickets, appetizers, buffet dinner, Polar Bear Keeper Talk and presentation by Robert W. Buchanan. A portion of the proceeds benefit Polar Bears International.

name: Columbus Neighborhoods: King-Lincoln
description: Join us as WOSU Public Media presents this advance screening of Columbus Neighborhoods: King-Lincoln. Learn more about this neighborhood's history and discover the treasures, stories and landmarks found throughout Columbus. Once considered the cultural and commercial heart of Columbus for African Americans, the King-Lincoln neighborhood is poised for rebirth. It still echoes with the joyous sounds of the storied musicians who played its clubs and theatres and the din of bustling streets lined with thriving businesses. The documentary also features CMA director Nannette Maciejunes talking about the neighborhood's rich visual arts heritage.

name: Face2Face: 25 Years of Art and Community
description: Studios on High Gallery celebrates its 25th Anniversary with, "Face 2 Face, 25 Years of Art and Community," an exhibition of new works by current members and alumni, showcasing the gallery's history and longevity in the Midwest art scene.

Couples will interact with Wedding Professionals, enjoy complimentary food and drinks at three unique downtown Columbus venues, all while being entertained with great music. This is the same class that is offered on site at Wright Patterson Air Force Base, Ft Monmouth, Aberdeen Proving Ground, NASA Glenn Research and others.

description: The Garden Club of CMA invites you to an evening with Marvin Duren. Owner of Marvin's Organic Gardens, Duren will talk about Ohio plant material that is garden worthy, tough, and durable. He also will discuss organic, natural, and safe garden practices. Marvin's Organic Gardens includes a Dutch-designed tempered glass greenhouse where Ohio native perennials, shrubs, and trees, as well as woodland and prairie plants, rarely found at other area nurseries, are grown. In 2003, Marvin's Organic Gardens earned the only USDA organic certification in the tri-state area that guarantees strict organic growing methods are followed and that synthetics or chemicals are never used.

description: "Please join us for an magical night of art and jazz. Muse Gallery will be featuring local artists Mel Rea, Mary Paula Wiggins, Bob Coates, Mike Elsass, Ann Kim, Sare, and Daid Senecal. description: Show features include an indoor kayak demo pool and certified instructors from Columbus Outdoor Pursuits, as well as ongoing seminars on subjects including car-topping equipment and techniques, camping tent selection, rigging kayaks for fishing, selecting the right mountain bike, and new product intros and reviews. name: Extreme Screen Film: Dolphins
description: Imagine floating in the crystalline, turquoise waters of the Bahamas. Swimming alongside you are some of the most graceful and extraordinary creatures on earth - wild dolphins. From the dazzling coral reefs of the Bahamas to the wind-swept seas of Patagonia, go under the water's surface for a romp with inquisitive Atlantic spotted dolphins, acrobatic dusky dolphins and the familiar bottlenose dolphin. Follow marine biologist, Dr. Kathleen Dudzinski, Dr. Bernd Wursig and Dr. Alejandro Acevedo-Gutierrez, as they research the communication of wild dolphins with innovative scientific methods. From rarely seen fish-herding behavior to a close-up look at complex communication activities, Dolphins offers a fascinating new perspective on the lives of dolphins and their remarkable intelligence.

name: Gasland
description: Fracking is coming to Ohio. Learn all about it. The largest domestic natural gas drilling boom in history has swept across the United States. The Halliburton-developed drilling technology of fracking or hydraulic fracturing has unlocked a Saudia Arabia of natural gas just beneath us. But is fracking safe? When filmmaker Josh Fox is asked to lease his land for drilling, he embarks on a cross-country odyssey uncovering a trail of secrets, lies and contamination. A recently drilled nearby Pennsylvania town reports that residents are able to light their drinking water on fire. This is just one of the many absurd and astonishing revelations of a new country called Gasland.

Who will win the spot of Designer of the Year? The competition is deadly. When one Designer dies, all clues point to her biggest competitor. description: Sit back, relax, and join fellow yelpers every Tuesday at Camelot Cellars for Yelp Wine Tuesdays where each week, a specially selected and priced red and white wine will be chosen for your merriment!

name: Jazz Arts Group's Inside Track: The Birth of the Cool
description: As jazz's bebop movement flourished during the late 1940s with its fast-paced rhythms from virtuosos like trumpeter Dizzy Gillespie and saxophonist Charlie Parker, trumpeter Miles Davis headed off in a new direction. Taking cues from the innovations learned in Parker's group, Davis, along with his nonet, recorded 12 songs in a two-year span that, when released together on one album, became known as Birth of the Cool. In 1949, arranger Gil Evans's New York basement apartment, where various jazz musicians had gathered, became ground zero for the nonet's formation. For the three recording sessions that took place Jan. and April 1949 and March 1950, Davis used the unlikely instruments of French horn and tuba, something first brought to light by the Claude Thornhill Orchestra, of which Evans was the principal arranger. Davis also enlisted the more traditional baritone and alto saxophones, trumpet, trombone, piano, bass and drums to complete the nonet. This instrumentation, coupled with the likes of Davis on trumpet, baritone saxophonist Gerry Mulligan, pianist John Lewis, alto saxophonist Lee Konitz and drummers Kenny Clarke and Max Roach, created a warm, relaxed, albeit "cool," sound that would become the standard for West Coast jazz.

name: Center Stage Players: [title of show] - yes that's the name of the show!
description: Jeff and Hunter, two struggling writers, hear about a new musical theatre festival. However, the deadline for submissions is a mere three weeks away. With nothing to lose, the pair decides to try to create something new with the help of their friends Susan, Heidi and Larry on the eighty-eights. With the cast in place, Jeff and Hunter begin a conversation about what to write about. Eventually, Jeff suggests they write about what to write about. They make a pact to write up until the festival's deadline and dream about the show changing their lives. [title of show]-taken from the space on the festival's application form which asks for the [title of show]-follows Hunter and Jeff and their friends on their journey through the gauntlet of creative self-expression. In the span of 90 minutes they write and perform their show at the festival and learn lessons about themselves as people, friends and artists. [title of show] is, above all, a love letter to the musical theatre-a uniquely American art form-and to the joy of collaboration. The musical received a Tony Award® nomination for Best Book of a Musical in 2009.

name: Exhibit: Homage to Bearden: Piecing it Together
description: Romare Bearden (1911-1988), an American artist of African-American heritage, is widely acknowledged as one of the most talented and original visual artists of the twentieth century. Original Romare Bearden works from private collections highlight this exhibition. Selected collage artists from Ohio provide accompanying 2 & 3 - dimensional work.

name: Exhibit: Shared Intelligence: American Painting and the Photograph
admission: Adults $10. Seniors and student 6 and older $8. Children 5 and under free. Admission is free every Sunday.
description: Inspired by the Georgia O'Keeffe Museum Research Center's 2006 3-day symposium, Painting and Photography in American Art: Sources, Ideas and Influences, 1890s to the Present, this exhibition of 75 paintings and photographs explores the productive and fraught relationship of these two mediums in American modern art that has been ongoing since the last decades of the 19th century. It focuses on the work of painters for whom photography has been essential, among them Robert Bechtle, Chuck Close, Thomas Eakins, Audrey Flack, David Hockney, Georgia O'Keeffe, Ben Shahn, Charles Sheeler, and Andy Warhol. This traveling exhibition also includes works from CMA such as our Norman Rockwell and Kehinde Wiley.

name: Exhibit: Wrinkles: Stephanie Rond and Dan Gerdeman
description: Ray's Living Room is pleased to present a two-person exhibition of new work by Stephanie Rond and Dan Gerdeman. Both artists make work that may be humorous and funny but also has an element of grit in as well.
