name: Exhibit: Energy through Eternity
description: Fresh A.I.R. Gallery is pleased to present Energy through Eternity, sculptures by Chappelle Letman. Mr. Letman resides in Cleveland, Ohio and received his B.F.A. from the California College of the Arts and is a sculptor by default of his disability. Employed as a mason, book illustrator, and painter he was affected by blindness later in life. Although an artist previously, he feels his disability of sight loss has given him his true artistic vision. He says being a sculptor allows him to unfold his wings and take flight. In this flight he is able to connect with the life force energy of Mother Earth, her peoples' emotions and feelings, and God the Creator. His sculptures then become living, breathing representations of his winged journeys and connect the viewer to the life force energy of the Universe.

name: Exhibit: For Todd DeVriese: In Celebration of a Beautiful Life
description: Cherished colleague (OSU Associate Professor 1996-2001), spectacular graduate student (MFA 1992), civic leader (Director of the Ohio State Fair arts exhibition; Vice-President and Board member of the Ohio Art League 1995-2000), and always an insightful and prolific artist: for over a decade Todd DeVriese touched the arts community of central Ohio in a myriad of ways. He went on to become Associate Professor and Chair of the Art Department, and later Dean of the College of Arts and Sciences at Zayed University, United Arab Emirates before leading the School of Art at Texas Tech University in Lubbox as Professor and Director. In 2009, Todd joined Minnesota's St. Cloud State University as the Dean of Fine Arts and Humanities where he served until his death last November. Todd's commitment to higher education and the vital power of the arts was central to his life. With works on loan from private and public collections and the artist's own studio, the Hopkins and Kuhn Galleries are honored to present these exhibitions celebrating the life and art of Todd DeVriese.

name: Exhibit: Controversy: Pieces You Don't Normally See
description: Controversy features five objects, including electric chair from the old Ohio Penitentiary, a Ku Klux Klan robe and hood, a sheepskin condom, a crib-bed cage that restrained patients at a state mental institution and a thumb mitt once used to prevent children from sucking their thumbs. The approach to the exhibit is unusual because it focuses on a limited collection of objects and provides limited interpretation of the objects for the visitor. Programs, scheduled each month throughout the run of the exhibit, will explore topics ranging from the creation of the exhibit to the meaning of objects to social issues connected to each of the items on display. By providing opportunities for shared dialogue and reflection, the Ohio Historical Society hopes to foster a better understanding of the past and how historical events, topics and issues impact our life today.

name: Echoes in Time Theatre: John Johnston Indian Agent: Should They Stay or Should They Go?

Created by B.H.B for Brothers Helping Bruthas the Hip Hop Expo is an event that showcases upcoming talent and provides a forum for networking artists, industry entrepreneurs, and hip hop enthusiasts. New this year, Asian culinary classes will be offered at Franklin Park Conservatory May 22-24.

name: Thurber House Literary Series: Justin Cronin
description: Justin Cronin also author of The Summer Guest and Mary and O'Neil, will appear.

name: Introduction to Land Office Records in Ohio
description: Do you think that your ancestor may have bought land from the United States government or received a Revolutionary War bounty? This course describes the differences between a bounty, a direct sale, a grant, and a homestead, and provides a description of how land was divided in Ohio. The course points out where in Ohio lands were available to Revolutionary War veterans, describes how to determine who claimed Revolutionary bounty lands, and how to locate individual claims. Original records will be used to illustrate grants and surveys. All seven original land surveys will be covered. This is a broad introduction to land records and will serve those just beginning research in this area.

name: Underwater Archaeology
admission: Adults $8. Seniors $7. Children 6-12 $4. Includes admission to the Ohio Historical Center.
description: Learn about the mysteries found underwater.

name: Launch Party for Fairer Than Morning
address: Cleveland Ave. and Main St., Westerville, 43082
description: The first book of Rossalyn Elliott's Hanby trilogy will be launched with a community party. The Otterbein Choir will be singing Benjamin Hanby's songs. Refreshments will be served.

name: Community Conversation: History: the Good, the Bad and the Ugly
description: This conversation will focus on whether or not objects are inherently controversial or whether time, culture, and society dictate the meaning of objects.

name: Community Conversations: History: The Good, the Bad and the Ugly
admission: Adults $8. Seniors $7. Children 6-12 $4. Includes admission to the Ohio Historical Center.
description: Second in a series of community conversations on topics inspired by the special exhibit Controversy: Pieces You Don't Usually See. Panelists consider whether some objects are inherently controversial or whether time, culture and society dictate their meaning.

name: New Behind-the-Scenes Tours: Civil War Collections
description: Participants will get an exclusive, guided tour through the Ohio Historical Society's Civil War objects and collections that aren't on exhibit and are stored in areas not open to the public. This tour will focus on the flags, weapons, military accessories and clothing related to the Civil War era in and around Ohio .

name: Sneak Peeks: Civil War Collections
description: Take an exclusive small-group behind-the-scenes tour of Civil War objects in the Ohio Historical Society's collections, focusing on flags, weapons, military accessories and clothing.

name: Small Talk
admission: Adults $8. Seniors $7. Children 6-12 $4. Includes admission to the Ohio Historical Center.
description: Informal small-group discussion related to the exhibit Controversy: Pieces You Don't Normally See.

name: More Land Office Records in Ohio
description: This course will identify where public land offices were located in Ohio. You will learn about records kept at each office that provide necessary information to determine who first purchased records kept at each office that provide necessary information to determine who first purchased land and when payments were made. Emphasis is on the description of land survey (field notes and measurements), entry, and payment records at the Ohio Historical Center and how to best use them.

name: Pushing the Surface Exhibit
description: This exhibit showcases contemporary art quilts from the United States as well as abroad. Twenty-six artists will participate.

name: Columbus Food Adventures: Gluten Free Dessert Tour
venue: Starts at Pistacia Vera in German Village
description: We will start our gluten free dessert tour at Pistacia Vera in German Village where their famous macarons, confections flourless tortes and pate de fruits are all gluten free. You'll have a chance to see behind the scenes and learn about their ingredients and craftsmanship. Our next stop will be Cherbourg Bakery in Bexley, a dedicated gluten and nut free bakery that opened early this year. Cherbourg Bakery's lemon slices have already won them many fans. From there we will head north to Clintonville to another dedicated gluten free bakery Food For Good Thought. Food For Good Thought is a unique business as it also aims to provide supported employment to individuals with autism. You can read more about their story on The Metropreneur. From there we will head to Jeni's Ice Creams where the majority of the flavors are gluten free. Some of the ice cream sandwiches, made with macaroons are also gluten free. As we traditionally do with our dessert tour we'll finish at Cameron Mitchell's M with a dessert cocktail conjured up by maestro mixologist Cris Dehlavi (there will be a non-alcoholic drink option available for those under 21 or who do not wish to consume alcohol).

name: Celebrity Bartender at Camelot Cellars Winery
description: Celebrity Bartender Night at Camelot Cellars Winery is back. This time come to Camelot Cellars and have your wine poured by Christian Christian of YelpColumbus. A charity donation will be made to a charity to be named later based on 10% of bar sales and a $1 per bottle purchased from the evening.

name: Exhibit: Happiness: Quilted Expressions
address: Riffe Center, 77 S. High St., Columbus, OH 43215
description: Organized by the Quilt Surface Design Symposium Foundation, the 36 artists' works of happiness have been expressed in the quilt medium in various forms. Some have shared their joy by re-creating a scene, capturing a moment in time with a snapshot of a delicious instant in their memory. Others have found their contentment and peace in the actual process of creating their art: the stitching, the sewing, the literal act of translating their viewpoints or feelings into a quilt, be it a political statement, a moment of humor or a delight in space.

name: Exhibit: Street Talk and Spiritual Matters: Aminah's Mt. Vernon Avenue
admission: Adults $10. Seniors and student 6 and older $8. Children 5 and under free. Admission is free every Sunday.
description: Aminah Robinson's RagGonNons, paintings, drawings, hogmawg sculptures, prints and books about Mt. Vernon Avenue, bring to life the heart of this African-American community that flourished on the eastside of Columbus until the early 1960s. The work typifies Aminah's passion with remembering and documenting the past in order to move forward. Aminah emphasizes the economic vibrancy and social activity of the neighborhood and also raises complex racial and political issues that were at play at the time. At the heart of the exhibition, are the scroll-like Memory Maps in which Aminah records every detail of the lively street life of Mt. Vernon Avenue. The street's storefronts, churches, theaters, and offices are the backdrop for Aminah's depictions of The Brownyskin Man, Umbrella Man, Organgrinder and dozens of other figures that populate the street. Many of these figures are also represented in sculptures, prints, and cloth paintings that demonstrate the artist's use of diverse media and techniques. The Memory Maps became the basis for Aminah's published book, A Street Called Home. Visitors will be able to gain insight into Aminah's creative process by examining her original art for the book and the study that preceded it. The time span represented in the work ranges from the early part of the twentieth century to the 1960s when construction of the interstate highway, urban planning, and civil rights demonstrations dramatically changed the tenor of the neighborhood. In an effort to bring the work alive and provide context for the art, we are video-taping individuals who have memories and stories about the street.

name: Papergirl Columbus
description: Paper Girl is a show, an urban action (the distribution of the rolls of art), a bicycle workshop and a party. In a nutshell it is: participatory, analog, non-commercial and impulsive. Anyone can participate, you can submit artwork and/or help distribute. Papergirl is distributed like a newspaper, but consists of original artwork rolled in a tube. You submit artwork in person or via mail, we have a show, we roll the artwork in to tubes, we get together on our bicycles to distribute the work around town to anyone. The work is not for sale; it is given to the public by chance for free. It is intended to take art distribution out of the galleries and into the streets, via direct delivery to the public in the style of the American paperboy.

name: Captain Sig & Hillstrand Brothers of Deadliest Catch
description: Captains Johnathan and Andy Hillstrand of the Time Bandit, along with Captain Sig Hansen of the Northwestern, will be making an appearance in Columbus! During these one-of-a kind events, the captains will take the audience through some toughest situations they've had to face on the high seas. Hear how it really goes down straight from the captains themselves!

name: Pecha Kucha
description: Each speaker will follow the international Pecha Kucha format of showing 20 images and speaking about each image for 20 seconds. Presenters include food educator Rachel Tayse Baillieul; branding designer Justin Bryant; Kate Dowell and Eric Rausch from ARTillery Ohio; performance artist Heidi Madsen; Mike Minnix with Eartha Limited; animal activist Lynne Petitti; poet Hannah Stephenson; architect Eric Thompson; and chef Magdiale Wolmark.

name: Family Day Workshop
address: Riffe Center, 77 S. High St., Columbus, OH 43215
description: Linda Fowler and Tracy Rieger will help children ages 6- 17 create a cloth collage using fusible construction techniques and embellishments to create pattern and design. Registration is required as space is limited; all children must be accompanied by a registered adult.

name: Fashion Night
description: The Scott J Salon Artistic Team from New York City, together with the Aveda Institute Columbus Student/Educator Team, will sponsor Earth Jam 2011 Fashion Night Benefit.

name: PASCO presents Fiesta Filipina
venue: Peggy R. McConnell Arts Center of Worthington
description: The Philippine American Society of Central Ohio (PASCO) is proud to present Fiesta Filipina. Fiesta Filipina is a premiere traditional Filipino performing dance company based in Toronto, Canada.

name: the Memorial Golf Tournament
description: Come watch the stars come out when the world's best golfers come to Dublin, Ohio for the internationally celebrated PGA Memorial Golf Tournament. The course, located at Muirfield Village Golf Club, was designed by Jack Nicklaus and opened on Memorial Day in 1974. Each year the tournament is dedicated to the memory of a person, living or dead, who has played the game with conspicuous honor.

name: Spring Flea
description: Columbus Flea's open-air market in the Short North, featuring Columbus vendors selling troves of one-of-kind treasures, will feature booths stuffed with handmade jewelry and art; vintage clothing; records; housewares; t-shirts; and so much more. Local DJs will provide the soundtrack, while shoppers dig their way through the hodge-podge paradise, eat great food from local restaurants and sip an iced coffee in the glorious (we hope) sunshine. It's exactly the kind of communal happening Columbus has been waiting for, and remember, proceeds will go to charity! So, come on out and shop, sell, or do both! We would love for you to be a part of it!

name: A Day in the Loop
description: Come to the Mid-Ohio Sports Car Course for a special half-day, high performance driving experience! Learn the physics and dynamics of driving, then get behind the wheel of an Acura TSX A-SPEC sport sedan. Test your skills in high performance drill - skid car, slalom and high-speed breaking and turning. The day culminates with an on-track lapping session around 2.4-mile, 15-turn road course. $200 per person includes driving course, lunch and your photo with a car. Can't attend the driving course? Join us for the Bob Evans Lap & Lunch! Ride around the race track at speed with a  professional driver. Get your picture taken with a car and enjoy lunch with afternoon session participants. $50 per person.

name: U.S. Women's National Team vs. Japan
address: One Black & Gold Boulevard, Columbus, OH 43211

name: Ohio Village Muffins Vintage Baseball vs. Columbus Buckeyes
description: Enjoy baseball the way it was meant to be played-no gloves, no spitting and no swearing-no kidding! There's nothing like the experience of a vintage game to take you back in time.

name: Ohio Village Muffins Vintage Baseball vs. Wood County Infirmary Inmates
description: Enjoy baseball the way it was meant to be played-no gloves, no spitting and no swearing-no kidding! There's nothing like the experience of a vintage game to take you back in time.

name: CATCO: Evil Dead: The Musical
description: Five college students go to an abandoned cabin in the woods, and accidentally unleash an evil force that turns them all into demons. It's all up to Ash (a housewares employee, turned demon killing hero), and his trusty chainsaw to save the day. Blood flies. Limbs are dismembered. Demons are telling bad jokes - and all to music.

name: Shadowbox Live: Best of Shadowbox
description: Catch up on the shows you missed and revisit your favorites with The Best of Shadowbox 2011. Only the most popular-by-demand sketches and songs make it into this all-star line-up for a fast-paced, side-splitting show.

name: Curtain Players: Dinner with Friends
description: Gabe and Karen are globetrotting food writers who enjoy entertaining their guests with delicious food and colorful stories of their culinary travels. They introduced playboy Tom to artist Beth a dozen years ago, hoping the introduction would result in a marriage as successful as their own. Gabe and Karen are hosting Beth at a dinner after their recent trip to Italy, when Beth breaks the news that Tom has left her. Dinner with Friends won the Pulitzer Prize for Drama in 2000.

name: SRO Theatre Company: Evita
description: Evita, Argentina's controversial First Lady is the subject of this musical masterpiece. As a young girl Eva escaped her dirt-poor existence for the bright lights of Buenos Aires. With her ambition and charisma, she was a starlet at twenty-two, the president's mistress at twenty-four, First Lady at twenty-seven and dead at thirty-three. Eva Peron, saint to the poor, was reviled by the aristocracy and mistrusted by the military was destined to leave a fascinating legacy unique to the 20th century.

name: Echoes in Time Theatre: Together, Yet Separate
description: In 1817, the Society of Separatists of Zoar began in Tuscarawas County, Ohio, and was one of the most successful communal societies in America until it disbanded in 1898. When the civil War erupted, the Zoarites, who were pacifists, paid $300 each for replacement volunteer soldiers. However, 12 men did go voluntarily and returned to the Zoar community changed forever by the war and other influences. Come listen as one Zoarite who went to war tells their story of being together, yet separate.

name: Michael Jackson THE IMMORTAL World Tour by Cirque du Soleil
venue: Value City Arena at the Jerome Schottenstein Center
description: A riveting fusion of visuals, dance, music and fantasy that immerses audiences in Michael's creative world and literally turns his signature moves upside down, Michael Jackson THE IMMORTAL World Tour unfolds Michael Jackson's artistry before the eyes of the audience. Aimed at lifelong fans as well as those experiencing Michael's creative genius for the first time, the show captures the essence, soul and inspiration of the King of Pop, celebrating a legacy that continues to transcend generations.

name: Opera Columbus: The Pirates of Penzance
description: Leap year often causes all kinds of troubles, and in Gilbert & Sullivan's famous operetta, The Pirates of Penzance, the every-four-year occurrence accomplishes exactly that! The story centers around Frederic, who, having just celebrated is 21st year, is released from his apprenticeship to a band of tender-hearted pirates. Never mind that his apprenticeship as a pirate is a mistake in the first place!

name: Columbus Gay Men's Chorus: Broadway Bound
description: Broadway comes calling! Relive some of your favorite musicals from past and present as CGMC brings to the stage the scintillating melodies and beautiful sounds from hit Broadway shows. The Lincoln Theatre will once again be the location for this fantastic show and will continue to serve as CGMC's home.

name: Dark Woods Theatre Company: Evil Dead The Musical
description: All seats are in what is known as the Splatter Zone. This means you will get blood on you during the performance. Some of you will be covered in blood from head to toe. Others will only have a few splashes on them. Don't worry; our blood is a recipe with fabric softener and other safe non-toxic ingredients. It washes out. Based on Sam Raimi's 80s cult classic films, EVIL DEAD tells the tale of 5 college kids who travel to a cabin in the woods and accidentally unleash an evil force. And although it may sound like a horror, it's not! The songs are hilariously campy and the show is bursting with more farce than a Monty Python skit. EVIL DEAD: THE MUSICAL unearths the old familiar story: boy and friends take a weekend getaway at abandoned cabin, boy expects to get lucky, boy unleashes ancient evil spirit, friends turn into Candarian Demons, boy fights until dawn to survive.

name: Royal Shakespeare Company: Hamlet
description: Ohio State University will present a Royal Shakespeare Company production of Hamlet for young people here in the summer. The Columbus run will be the North American premiere of the company's acclaimed British production, a 70-minute version created for young people and families as an introduction to the Bard. The piece will be performed by members of the same ensemble who will appear in five full-length Shakespeare productions in July and August in New York, presented in association with OSU.

name: The Actors' Theatre of Columbus: A Midsummer Night's Dream,
description: This production will be co-directed by Beth Kattelman and Dee Shepherd This is one of Shakespeare's most beloved comedies and a return to the first play ever produced by Actors' Theatre of Columbus.

name: Upper Arlington Music in the Parks
description: The Cultural Arts Division invites you to enjoy our free summer concert series, Music in the Parks, Thursdays, 7:00-8:30p.m. June through August, 2011. This free concert series takes place outdoors on the New! UA Arts Stage at the Amelita Mirolo Barn at Sunny 95 Park. Bring a lawn chair or a blanket. In the event of rain, the concert will be moved inside the Amelita Mirolo Barn while concerts at community parks will be canceled. The summer concert series is a success through the generous support of the Ohio Arts Council, Pagetech Ltd. and Huffman's Market.

name: Fireside Fridays
description: Circle round the campfire the first Friday of every month after Music in the Park. We'll be telling campfire stories, going for a night hike, gazing at the stars, and eating campfire snacks

name: Family Classes: Backyards for Wildlife
description: Our family classes give you an opportunity to create fun memories with your entire family. We realize that the time spent with your family is limited and precious and these classes are designed as an outing that any age can enjoy. Hands-on activities and animal visitors are included in each monthly topic.

name: Plein Air at the Ohio Statehouse
address: Broad St.& High St., Columbus, OH 43215
description: Join dozens of plein-air artists as they converge on Capitol Square to celebrate the 150th anniversary of the Ohio Statehouse. Artists throughout Ohio will "choose a spot" on Capitol Square and paint in the tradition of plein air. En plein air is a French expression which means "in the open air", and is particularly used to describe the act of painting outdoors.

name: Second Sundays at Kelton House: Trails of Hope
description: A series of historical re-enactments depicting the struggles for freedom on the Underground Railroad.

name: Sundays at Scioto Summer Concert Series
description: The 28th annual DAC Sundays at Scioto summer concert series will take place each Sunday evening for eight weeks. This showcase for local and regional performing artists includes something for almost every musical taste, from Latin salsa to country rock and funk to swing.

name: Victorian Tea at Kelton House: Summer Social Tea
description: Throughout the year, the Kelton House offers Victorian-inspired teas with a tasteful sampling of savories and sweets reminiscent of 19th century ladies' get-togethers. The menu for each Tea is different, but is always accompanied by traditional Earl Grey tea.

name: Juneteenth Celebration
description: This celebration offers fun for the entire family in celebration of the Emancipation Proclamation, and recognizes the struggle by African Americans for freedom. Juneteenth, or June 19th, 1865, is considered the date when the last slaves in America were freed. Although the rumors of freedom were widespread before this, actual emancipation did not come until General Gordon Granger rode into Galveston, Texas and issued General Order No. 3, on June 19th, almost two and a half years after President Abraham Lincoln signed the Emancipation Proclamation.

name: Pride Festival
address: Corner of Goodale Blvd. And Park St., Columbus, OH 43201
description: The largest pride event in the Midwest, the Pride Festival annually attracts more than 100,000 people with its marketplace, food court, family area and music. A brunch will conclude the festival weekend at 11 a.m., Sunday at The Westin downtown. The parade begins at noon Saturday from downtown to Goodale Park.

name: Gospel Sail-A-Bration
description: Gospel music and entertainers from around the state will perform free to the public.

name: Skate for Hope
description: Skate for Hope is a premier figure skating event benefiting breast cancer research and awareness. Current National and World figure skating champions will join Central Ohio skaters for a spectacular show.

name: Zoofari
description: This annual, adult-only fundraiser features nearly 100 central Ohio restaurants and bars serving appetizer portions of their signature dishes and specialty drinks. Guests "graze" their way while enjoying live entertainment on stages scattered throughout the grounds. Come with friends, wine and dine your business associates, entertain your out-of-town guests, or reward hard-working employees - don't miss Columbus' best summer party!

name: Origins Game Fair
description: Enjoy board games, card games, role-playing, miniatures, classic games and more at the annual Origins International Game Expo. Shop the 200-plus vendors in the exhibit hall. Tour the art show featuring some of the best fantasy artists from through Ohio and around the world. Enjoy informative seminars with topics such as world history, game development and games in education. With more than 4,000 events, it's one of North America's largest game conventions. There also are special programs for parents and other non-gaming family members. Game sessions run 24 hours daily.

name: 4th Friday: Safety Fest
description: It's another fantastic Fourth Friday Celebration in Uptown Westerville! The Westerville Visitors Bureau has teamed up with the Westerville Fire and Police Departments to present "Safety Fest" featuring helpful information about health and safety. Enjoy music, street vendors, children's activities and family fun!

name: Family Friday Night
description: COSI stays open late for family-friendly fun the last Friday of every month! You can explore science, discover fun, and stay late! General admission is only $8 after 5 p.m. and includes all of COSI's permanent exhibitions plus a movie on the 7 story Extreme Screen theater, a savings of $11.75!

name: Dublin Kiwanis Annual Frog Jump
description: The Kiwanis Club hosts one of the oldest event in the good old summertime. More than 1,000 young frog jockeys participate in several age divisions, with thousands of spectators cheering on their favorite frog. Competition includes multiple playoff rounds, followed by a championship. There are loads of prizes to enhance the competition. It's an old-fashioned slice of city Americana that's packed with photo opportunities, human interest and good, clean fun.

name: Ray Lamontagne and the Pariah Dogs
An Evening with Davy Jones, Micky Dolenz, & Peter Tork of the Monkees
Kenny Chesney
address: One Black & Gold Boulevard, Columbus, OH 43211

name: Columbus Arts Festival
description: Discover the art at the 2011 Columbus Arts Festival in downtown's Discovery District. Surrounded by the Columbus Museum of Art, the Columbus College of Art and Design and Columbus State Community College, the Columbus Arts Festival is the city's welcome-to-summer event, pairing the finest artists and craftspeople from around the country and the world with continuous entertainment including hands-on art activities, musical performances and great food from area restaurants.

name: Park Street Festival
description: This year, we're back and better than ever with live music, great food and entertainment for kids and adults of all ages. The Park Street Festival is a collaboration of unique foods and drinks from local vendors and the many entertainment venues located in the Park Street District.

name: CAMP Blues
description: Join Sean Carney and the Sean Carney Band for CAMP Blues, a weeklong ensemble experience focusing on learning about and playing the blues. The course will focus on guitar, bass and drums, exploring those instruments' respective roles in blues music and developing participants' instrumental skills and techniques. Instructors will discuss basic theory, ear training and improvisation with respect to their instrument and practical application in the ensemble setting. Students will hear recorded examples with directed listening and will be given names of recordings to listen to in the future.

name: Creekside Blues & Jazz Festival
admission: Adults $3. Children under 12 free. Military free with ID.
description: This music festival is the showcase for the best blues and jazz music in Ohio, if not the Midwest. Music isn't all that this renowned event has to offer. Centered around Creekside Park and Olde Gahanna, the Creekside Blues & Jazz Festival promises something for everyone with more than 90 hours of entertainment, Jog for Jazz, Sunday Jazz Brunch, Musical Discovery Zone, amusement rides, vendors, and of course, great food!

name: Fred Bailey Sings Stories of Hope and Struggle
description: Fred Bailey's singing voice is not sweet. Instead, it's gritty, ragged, and rough. But that's good. Because the 70 year old Clintonville performer sings songs about chemical factory workers stricken by lung disease, Vietnam war veterans plagued by battle demons, sailors lost at sea, skeletons of ramshackle Okie homesteads abandoned during the Dust Bowl years, and park rangers trapped by forest fires.

name: CAMP Blues 2
description: Join Sean Carney and the Sean Carney Band for CAMP Blues, a weeklong ensemble experience focusing on learning about and playing the blues. The course will focus on guitar, bass and drums, exploring those instruments' respective roles in blues music and developing participants' instrumental skills and techniques. Instructors will discuss basic theory, ear training and improvisation with respect to their instrument and practical application in the ensemble setting. Students will hear recorded examples with directed listening and will be given names of recordings to listen to in the future.

name: CAMP Rock
description: Get ready to rock! CAMP Rock is for individuals who play guitar, bass, drum set or sing. Each day will include listening to great rock recordings, jamming' with your ensemble and sectional rehearsals with camp participants and great professional musicians. At the end of the week, each ensemble will be able to play and perform at least one song.

name: Vaud-Villities: The Best of Vaud-Villities
description: Vaud-Villities, an annual music spectacular, is the oldest and largest musical production in the United States.

name: ComFest
address: Corner of Goodale Blvd. And Park St., Columbus, OH 43201
description: A favorite of locals, ComFest is a free festival of juried music, food and art that promotes unity. Concerts start around noon daily.

name: IMPROVisation
description: Explore the rhythmic, melodic and harmonic concepts of jazz in this weeklong performance oriented camp. We'll spend most of our time playing the music with less emphasis on lecture. Have fun, develop your musical abilities, and improve your improvisational skills!

name: No Charts! Ensemble and IMPROVisation Bundle
description: Bundle the "No Charts!" Ensemble and IMPROVisation camps and spend your whole day listening, learning and playing music at the Jazz Academy. Participants are welcome to pack a lunch and eat in the Jazz Academy lounge.

name: No Charts! Ensemble with Jay Miglia
description: Leave your reading glasses at home! The "No Charts!" Ensemble is all about using your ears! This course is designed to introduce students to playing their instruments by ear, an experience that will open new avenues of creativity for every participant. Every day we will memorize a simple tune or two and improvise without reading notes or worrying about jazz theory. The band is open to students entering middle through high school who play "Big Band" instruments: alto, tenor and baritone saxophones, trumpet, trombone, guitar and bass, piano/keyboard, vibes and drum set.

name: Little Germany: Canals, Breweries & Charming Houses
description: The Great Southern Hotel was the architectural pinnacle of taste, culture, and acumen, and in many ways a high point of business for the city's largest ethnic group. Germans had been settling there since the very founding of the city. Explore the architecture, traditions, and stories that still define Columbus.

name: Community Conversation: Parenting: From Thumb Covers to Tiger Moms
description: This conversation will focus on parenting, especially current controversies that have swirled around different approaches to parenting.

name: New Behind-the-Scenes Tours: Civil War Collections
description: Participants will get an exclusive, guided tour through the Ohio Historical Society's Civil War objects and collections that aren't on exhibit and are stored in areas not open to the public. This tour will focus on the flags, weapons, military accessories and clothing related to the Civil War era in and around Ohio .

name: Corvettes at Roscoe Cruise-In
description: Over 200 Corvettes will converge in Roscoe Village at this event hosted by the Classic Glass Corvette Club. Stroll through the streets of Roscoe Village to the tunes of 50's and 60's music as you admire your favorite car and talk to its proud owner.

name: Blast from the Past Summer Camp
description: Be a Time Traveler and join us on a trip through time at the Ohio Historical Center and the Ohio Village. Through hands-on activities and games geared for children ages 6-8 and 9-11 campers will travel through Ohio's past. They will work on a simulated archeological excavation, will learn about how ancient peoples and early settlers used native plants and animals, explore Ohio's role in the Civil War and learn to work and play in the Ohio Village.

name: History of the Boulevard Block Party
Little Germany: Canals, Breweries & Charming Houses
description: The Great Southern Hotel was the architectural pinnacle of taste, culture, and acumen, and in many ways a high point of business for the city's largest ethnic group. Germans had been settling there since the very founding of the city. Explore the architecture, traditions, and stories that still define Columbus.

name: Civil War Lecture: Mr. Lincoln's Camera Man: An Afternoon with Matthew Brady
description: Celebrate the 150th anniversary of the Civil War with a monthly lecture series, featuring such topics as Civil War music, photography, fashion, ghost stories and others.

name: Wendy's International Triathlon and Duathlon
address: 3615 S. Old State Rd., Lewis Center, 43015
description: Come to the beach and cheer on the athletes or join in the excitement of a triathlon.

name: Romantic Full Moon Canoe Trip
description: Join us to experience canoeing by the light of the moon. On this date we will canoe under the Waxing Crescent Moon. As the Moon moves around the Earth it becomes more illuminated and provides light that reflects off the Hocking River. In addition to the moon, we also provide tiki torches for each canoe to help navigate the river. The tiki torches also help in viewing the wildlife that will be settling in for the night. We push off at sunset and descend back to the canoe livery for an evening of relaxation. We will depart from the Canoe Livery an hour before sunset to Trip 1 Crockett's Run. The trip is approximately 5 miles and 2 hours. We float back to the canoe livery and a roaring bonfire, roast smores, and enjoy a night of live entertainment.

name: WaterFire
description: Please join the community for a unique spectacle, bringing together friends to enjoy music, bonfires and riverfront entertainment downtown. WaterFire begins at dusk and is a one-of-a-kind experience creating an opportunity for everyone to enjoy an evening out with the arts.

name: Flaming Torchlight Canoe Trip
description: Join us to experience canoeing by the light of the moon. On this date we will canoe under the Waxing Crescent Moon. As the Moon moves around the Earth it becomes more illuminated and provides light that reflects off the Hocking River. In addition to the moon, we also provide tiki torches for each canoe to help navigate the river. The tiki torches also help in viewing the wildlife that will be settling in for the night. We push off at sunset and descend back to the canoe livery for an evening of relaxation. We will depart from the Canoe Livery an hour before sunset to Trip 1 Crockett's Run. The trip is approximately 5 miles and 2 hours. We float back to the canoe livery and a roaring bonfire, roast smores, and enjoy a night of live entertainment.

name: Paws in the Plaza
description: Join other dogs as they bring their owners to stroll through the paths, river walks, pet friendly shops, and visiting vendors and businesses in downtown Olde Gahanna. Exhibits vary monthly including free nail trimmings, animal communicator, caricature artist, souvenir photos, raffles, giveaways, artist sketches, rescues and more!

name: Exhibit: The Language of Art
description: The Language of Art features visual art complemented by ekphrasis poetry, the graphic, often dramatic description of a visual work of art in poem. Selected artwork will be assigned to a poet, who will produce a poem that reflects their experience with the art.

name: Exhibit: COMnGRAF 3: Breaking Borders
description: COMnGRAF 3: Breaking Borders is a series of exhibitions that showcase Hip-Hop culture through the cross-cultural influence between Comic Book Art and Graffiti Art. This exhibition will showcase the collaborative grouping together of both sequential and aerosol art by mainstream comic book artists and legendary graffiti artists. Simply stated, it is "the fusion of two cultures" celebrating the influence each has on the other.

name: Exhibit: Worthington Quilts
description: An exhibition of fiber works by Kris Worthington. Quilt's inspired by Worthington's emotional and spiritual journey, incorporating the Japanese shibori method of dyeing, hand and machine stitching, beading and collage techniques. Worthington's quilts portray life, landscape and abstract images.

name: Exhibit: Currents: Stephanie Syjuco
admission: Adults $10. Seniors and student 6 and older $8. Children 5 and under free. Admission is free every Sunday.
description: Stephanie Syjuco has adopted the tactics of counterfeiting, re-appropriation, and fictional fabrications to address questions of cultural biography, labor, and capitalism. Recent projects include re-creating several 1950s Modernist furniture pieces by French designer Charlotte Perriand but using cast-off material and rubbish gathered in Beijing; starting a global collaborative project with crochet crafters to counterfeit high-end consumer goods; photographing models of Stonehenge made from cheap Asian imported food products; and instituting a live and on-site reproduction facility to bootleg and display works of art found at the Frieze Art Fair.

name: Columbus Commons Market
address: Between State and Rich St., Columbus, OH 43215
description: Farmers will be permitted to sell directly from their vehicle, while merchants will receive no cost validated parking in the Columbus Commons Main Parking Garage.

name: Exhibit: Accessible Expressions Ohio
description: The Accessible Expressions Ohio visual art exhibit and tour began in 1996. This program provides professional development opportunities for artists to create, exhibit and sell their art and raises awareness of all abilities by presenting art by people with disabilities in inclusive settings. Beginning each fall artists submit an application and photographs to a call for art. From the photos, a select number of pieces are chosen to form the exhibition.

name: Exhibit: Re-Union: David Bamber and Andrew F. Scott
description: Reunions imply a coming together for family and friends based on a connection or association. Such is the case for artists David Bamber of Columbus and Andrew F. Scott, a professor of sculpture at the Savannah, Ga., College of Art and Design. The artists first met as graduate students at The Ohio State University, became studio mates in the sculpture department and began a collaborative association that would span 18 years of sharing the same creative space.

name: Major League Gaming Pro Circuit
admission: Spectator Passes $25. Halo Reach Team Pass $280. Call of Duty: Black Ops Team Pass $240. Starcraft 2 Player Pass $70.
description: The world's largest competitive video game event is coming to Columbus. Major League Gaming will hold the 2nd live competition of the 2011 Pro Circuit in Columbus from June 3-5 at the Columbus Convention Center. Over 1000 players will square off playing some of the most competitive titles available including Halo: Reach for Xbox 360, StarCraft 2 for PC, and for the first time on the Pro Circuit - Call of Duty: Black Ops for PlayStation3. Players and spectators will experience an all new Pro Circuit set up including three giant main stages and hundreds of gaming stations. Attendees will have the opportunity to visit an array of booths featuring meet and greets with the Pros, the latest products from MLG partners, pre-release access to games and more.

name: Short North Gallery Hop
address: North High Street from Goodale Boulevard to Fifth Avenue, Columbus, OH 43201
description: The first Saturday of every month, thousands of visitors converge on the strip, the epicenter of the High Street experience. They come to celebrate art and partake in an evening of sights, sounds, food, shopping, and cosmopolitan fun. Countless art experiences. District specials. Prize drawings. Ramped up entertainment. Unexpected surprises. Join us for an unforgettable experience.

name: American Heart Association Presents Kids at Heart Training Camp
2nd Saturdays
description: Join us the 2nd Saturday of the month at Creekside Park & Plaza from June-September! GP&R will be hosting children's and adult activities; including crafts, games, trivia, and art displays.

name: ARTSpeak
description: The Gahanna Department of Parks & Recreation is excited to announce the latest addition to the 2nd Saturday's summer event, ARTSpeak! This indoor/outdoor showcase celebrates local artists and their talents, while providing attendees a firsthand opportunity to learn about and experience the creation of artwork.

name: BIA Parade of Homes
description: This event showcases Central Ohio's best and brightest in the area of homebuilding, home design and landscaping.

name: Columbus Discovery Tours
description: Explore Columbus with CHS! Travel through Downtown, Victorian Village, Franklinton, German Village, Short North, King-Lincoln District, Franklin Park and much more as you hear stories of national significance, international intrigue, and local lore. Over 200 years of history, growth, and development will be explored in this 90-minute tour.

name: COSI After Dark
description: For ages 21 and over, with great exhibits, great drinks, and great fun. Includes parking and $4 in food/drink vouchers.

name: Easton Art Affair
description: Join us for a unique and enjoyable shopping experience at the annual Easton Art Affair, an outdoor fine art and fine craft show held on the streets of the beautiful Easton Town Center. This outstanding event features 125 juried artisans and boasts a wide variety of art and craft, including acrylic, oil and watercolor paintings, pottery, metal sculpture, fine jewelry, glass and much more.

name: German Village Haus und Garten Tour
description: Visitors are cordially invited for this daylong celebration of innovative design and award-winning restorations. Guests can explore the sites at their own pace, while stopping to enjoy the gardening demonstrations, shopping for unique home and garden accessories in the Marketplatz and watching members of the Central Ohio Watercolor Society paint their masterpieces for the annual watercolor competition.

name: Tour de Grandview Cycling Classic
description: The Tour de Grandview Cycling Classic is Ohio's premier cycling event, attracting an international field of more than 100 professional cyclists to Central Ohio each year, as well as hundreds of cycling enthusiasts and spectators. It features two days of world-class bicycle racing through the streets of suburban Grandview, as well as a number events and activities for spectators and cyclists alike.

name: The Morning Sports Report
description: Hear the inside scoop on the Columbus sports scene. This breakfast event features high-profile sports industry leaders, as well as representatives from the Columbus Clippers, Columbus Blue Jackets, Columbus Crew and The Ohio State University.

name: Ohio Chautauqua in Westerville
description: This five-day event combines living history, music and entertainment, education, theater and audience interaction. This Civil War-themed series presented by the Ohio Humanities Council will feature adult and children's programming each day and a musical group and historical presentation each evening. The slate of speakers includes actors portraying Abraham Lincoln, Harriet Tubman, Mary Edwards Walker (Battlefield Surgeon), Mary Boykin Chestnut (diarist in the Confederate South) and Major Martin Delaney (the first African American to reach that rank in the Union Army).

name: Park Street Festival
description: This year, we're back and better than ever with live music, great food and entertainment for kids and adults of all ages. The Park Street Festival is a collaboration of unique foods and drinks from local vendors and the many entertainment venues located in the Park Street District.

name: Stop and Smell the Roses
description: Stop and smell the roses during a rose-filled weekend of educational and artistic exhibits featuring 11,500 roses in peak bloom at the Park of Roses. Take a guided tour of the gardens and watch various art clubs painting throughout the gardens. Enjoy soothing music during your stroll and talk with rosarians and horticulturists from the Columbus Rose Foundation, Columbus Rose Club and Park of Roses volunteers, who will be available to answer questions on the selection, planting and care of roses, perennials and herbs

name: Powell Festival
description: Load up the car and join us for fun at the annual Powell community gathering. Ten free musical performances, educational stations, animal and mascot visits, train rides, games, rides, merchant displays, food court, beer garden and much more.

name: Powell Farmers Market
description: Located in the City of Powell Municipal Bldg. Parking Lot Produce, Cookies, Pies, Chutneys, Baked goods, Honey, Syrup, Arts, Crafts, Flowers, Plants, your favorite Farmers.

name: OHSAA Track & Field Championships
venue: Jesse Owens Memorial Stadium, The Ohio State University

Columbus Clippers Baseball vs. Rochester Red Wings
Columbus Crew vs. Real Salt Lake
address: One Black & Gold Boulevard, Columbus, OH 43211

address: One Black & Gold Boulevard, Columbus, OH 43211

name: Ohio Village Muffins Vintage Baseball Triple Header
description: Enjoy baseball the way it was meant to be played-no gloves, no spitting and no swearing-no kidding! There's nothing like the experience of a vintage game to take you back in time.

Columbus Clippers Baseball vs. Gwinnett Braves
