description: Enjoy baseball the way it was meant to be played-no gloves, no spitting and no swearing-no kidding! There's nothing like the experience of a vintage game to take you back in time.

name: Columbus Clippers Baseball vs. Toledo Mud Hens
Friday Flicks! Jurassic Park
description: Jurassic Park. Enjoy outdoor movies on our big screen this summer at Creekside Park.

name: Short North Yard Sale: City's Largest Yard Sale
description: The daylong treasure hunt takes place in the neighborhoods in and around the Short North, including Victorian Village, Harrison West, Italian Village, Dennison Place, and The Circles. More than 150 homes participated in last year's Short North Yard Sale, making it the largest yard sale in Columbus.

name: Wild West at Wild Goose!
description: Over the past two years the country music scene in Columbus has grown from a once a month show featuring small handful of rotating guests to a close-knit community that hosts regular musical events and featuring bands that boast booking calendars extending far into 2012. The movement recently culminated in a Johnny Cash tribute show that saw over 400 people come through the doors of The Shruken Head!

name: Clave: The Key: A Rhythmic Journey from Africa to the New World
description: Join jazz and Latin-jazz artist Bobby Sanabria as he uses the five-beat rhythm of the clave as the key to unlock the roots of Afro-Cuban music and reveals the voices of the ancestors. Playing a wide variety of percussion instruments and a full drum set, Sanabria takes audiences on a poly-rhythmic musical journey through history. Influenced by history, politics and religion, the rhythms of Africa create the rich array of musical styles we now call Latin music with an emphasis on a shared musical tradition and a mutual respect for all cultures. Bringing us into present day America, Sanabria will demonstrate how the five-beat clave remains at the core of such musical styles as rock & roll and hip-hop.

name: Experience the Avenue: A Columbus East Side Jazz Tradition
description: The Society for Creative Art and Talent (S.C.A.T.) will explore the effect of the Jazz Era on our very own city. . At this performance and discussion-based event, guests will have the chance to experience ragtime, blues and an assortment of other jazz subgenres through live musical recreations, dancing and discussions held by local jazz painter Mike Fields and noted jazz social historian and educator Connie Boykin. Light refreshments and drinks will be provided.

name: The Dublin Singers: For the Love of It All!
description: Under the direction of Mary Fran Cassidy, with accompaniment by Kearney Lykins, III, the concert celebrates love in its many forms: love of music, nature, romance, children, God, Country, and much more.

name: Chamber Music Columbus: Fry Street Quartet
description: Founded in Chicago in 1997 under the mentorship of the cellist of the renowned Vermeer Quartet, the Fry Street Quartet explores the medium of the string quartet and its life-affirming potential, receiving prestigious awards and rave reviews around the world.

name: Gaming Anime Punch Style (GAPS) Coliseum: Rock Band
description: Bring just yourself or a full band and show us that you deserve to be on top in our 'battle of the bands'-style competition. Each band will be judged on song difficulty, accuracy and most of all stage presence.

name: Mouth of the Wolf Theater Group presents: Blooms & Butterflies
description: Campers will present a Blooms & Butterflies Production, led by Mouth of the Wolf Theater Group. This public performance is a culmination of our week long kid's acting camp.

name: Celebrate Spring with Max of Max and Ruby
description: Celebrate Spring with Max of Max and Ruby. Join the mischievous costumed character bunny, Max, as he listens to one of this favorite spring time stories.

name: Hiking the Appalachian Trail with Jeff Alt
description: The OSU Mountaineering Club and Clintonville Outfitters are proud to bring Jeff Alt to speak about his experience hiking the Appalachian Trail. Please join us to listen to Jeff share more about "A Walk For Sunshine", his award winning adventure story that will fill you with inspiration to go after your dreams. Jeff Alt takes you along every step of his amazing 2,160-mile Appalachian Trail adventure filled with humor and inspiration. Now, he includes practical advice to plan your own hiking adventure.

name: Kid Only Zone!: Quick Breads
description: Muffins, biscuits and pancakes--oh my! Learn to make tasty treats from scratch, including Apple Oat Muffins and Blueberry Buttermilk Pancakes, and then enjoy your creations!

name: 4th Friday: Uptown Alive
description: Uptown Westerville is Alive with Art, History and Shopping! Since April is Celebration of The Arts Month, we'll focus on the performing, visual and other art endeavors that give Westerville its rich flavor. With extended shopping hours in Uptown Westerville's unique shops, 4th Friday is the perfect time to spend the evening shopping and enjoying all the activities, music and food that make 4th Friday such a wonderful community event. Arts and Crafts vendors will offer a variety of unique products, the Westerville Police and Fire Departments offer displays for children, the Westerville Public Library reads stories right Uptown and there is always great live entertainment.

name: Spring-In to the Village!
description: After a long, dismal winter, take time to refresh yourself, your home and your garden during Spring-In to the Village. Enjoy a stroll through the village, special promotions, home and garden demonstrations, extended hours, plus the great food and entertainment planned for this exciting celebration.

name: Columbus Children's Theatre: The Three Little Pigs mini show
description: Join the performers from Columbus Children's Theatre as the perform excerpts from the widely funny and popular adaptation of this beloved tale.

name: Wonderland Columbus Science Fair
description: Re-live the fun from third grade and participate in a science fair for ages 13 & up! A family-friendly display of scientific and creative innovation, the Wonderland Columbus Science Fair offers would-be scientists and at-home tinkerers a chance to experiment and show off their inventions in public.

name: Glass Axis Spring Sale and Workshops
description: Join Ohio's premier artists for a weekend of art glass, just in time for Mother's Day! Hundreds of glass art pieces are on sale, ranging from blown glass vessels to exquisite jewelry; from colorful sculpted glass flowers to stained glass panels.

name: Open House at The Meadery
description: Come tour Ohio's only meadery during our Saturday Open House at The Meadery. We make mead, a specialty wine made from honey ranging from dry to sweet in traditional, melomels, and metheglins. Mead is the drink of the gods, cherished from the time of the Pharaohs to the Emperors of China. Come learn by tasting it in Columbus!

name: Perkins Observatory
description: Star gazing with the 32-inch Schottland Telescope.

name: REBOOT: Mike Rozzi & Josh Manning
description: REBOOT is a reunion between Josh and Mike after a 3 year hiatus not working alongside each other in a common studio and symbolizes a re-start of interaction and influence between the 2. REBOOT is an exhibition of functional ceramics: platters, bowls, pitchers and jars.

name: Exhibit: Face2Face: 25 Years of Art and Community
description: Studios on High Gallery celebrates its 25th Anniversary with, "Face 2 Face, 25 Years of Art and Community," an exhibition of new works by current members and alumni, showcasing the gallery's history and longevity in the Midwest art scene.

name: ABC 6 "On Your Side" Job Boot Camp
Conversations & Coffee: Pastel Portraits and Critters in Clay
description: Experience Face2Face in person at this Conversations & Coffee. Artists Judy Hoberg, Denise Romecki and Teda Theis will be talking about their paintings and ceramics and their Studios on High gallery. Denise and Teda are curators for the Face2Face Exhibit at the Cultural Arts Center.

name: BalletMet 7 Deadly Sins Open Rehearsal
description: These open rehearsals provide a glimpse into the creative process and a sneak peek of an upcoming production. After the rehearsal, guests can participate in a question and answer session with the artists.

name: Earth, Paws and Claws
description: Hop over to the Columbus Zoo and Aquarium and join us for our annual Eggs, Paws and Claws Event with an Earth Day twist. This event returns bigger and better then ever. Now with more treat stations, kid friendly entertainment and seasonal themed animal enrichment activities than ever before. Don't miss a visit with the Bunny!

name: Ohio Artists Show
description: Please join us for an magical night of art and jazz. Muse Gallery will be featuring local artists Mel Rea, Mary Paula Wiggins, Bob Coates, Mike Elsass, Ann Kim, Sare, and Daid Senecal. Circle Galleries will be featuring select artists David Hostetler, Sue Cavanaugh, and Juliellen Byrne. New works will be displayed for the show, and select works at Circle Galleries will only be available for a short time. Most artists will be in attendance the night of the opening, catering will be provided by Two Caterers, and the incredibly talented Arnett Howard will be here playing jazz with Club Dave in the courtyard

name: KYP Watershed Distillery Tour
address: 1145 Chesapeake Ave. Ste. D., Columbus, OH 43212
description: Looking for something new to do? Join the Komen Young Professionals for an evening of delicious fun in Grandview with an exclusive tour of the Watershed Distillery followed by an always-good time at Brazenhead! The evening will begin at the Watershed Distillery in Grandview. Watershed opened last year and we are getting a special tour of the facility with commentary on the process of making Gin and Vodka. Following the tour will be a tasting of both spirits!

name: Talk To Focus: Louise Bourgeois
description: On the occasion of a Wexner Center exhibition featuring the work of Louise Bourgeois, the next Lambert Family Lecture will celebrate the life and work of this highly influential artist and 1999 Wexner Prize recipient who passed away last year at the age of 98. Jerry Gorovoy and Germano Celant: Remembering Louise, featuring two people close to Bourgeois.

name: 2011 Decorators' Show House
description: The Spanish-revival style home was built in 1928. It sits on almost two acres.

name: Mind, Body & Soul
description: The King Arts Complex and the Ward Family YMCA will present "Mind, Body & Soul" during April - Minority Health Month in Ohio. This community event will provide health information in a positive and fun atmosphere. This day of arts therapy, fitness activities, performances and presentations is free and open to the public.

name: Sprout
description: The first of it's kind, this interactive gallery show will feature artwork from students of the Columbus Artmobile, 5th Avenue International K-8 School and Columbus International HS. Also on display will be decorative musical instruments made from found objects by the students of Freedom Trail Elementary and led by Olentangy art teacher and local artist Rob Jones. There will also be a free workshop for guests to create their own works of art, using household and found objects as well as recycled materials.

name: Ohio State University Football Spring Game
admission: Tickets are $7 in advance and $15 on Saturday
description: The Ohio State football team holds its annual spring scrimmage. The football action will be in an offense vs. defense format, with both units battling for the right to wear the scarlet jerseys for August practice. The Ohio State men's lacrosse team will host Fairfield in an ECAC Lacrosse League game at 11 a.m. in the first portion of the doubleheader, with the football scrimmage beginning at 1:30 p.m. The Big Ten Network will televise both contests. Gates will open at 10 a.m., and the popular FanFest will begin at 10:30 outside St. John Arena. The Jesse Owens Classic in track and field will begin at 6 p.m. Saturday at Jesse Owens Memorial Stadium and will resume Sunday at noon.

name: Historic Tavern Tours: The Irish & German Experience
description: Our popular Historic Tavern Tours return in April with visits to three taverns associated with the Irish and German populations of Columbus. Drinks are not included in the ticket price, but sparkling narration, historic gossip, and architectural knowledge of the taverns and their environs is cheerfully included, along with shuttle service between each tavern. Time at each tavern for enjoying the atmosphere and socializing before moving along to the next stop

name: Lights, Camera, LeVeque
description: The Citadel was produced by Columbus Landmarks Foundation with support from an Ohio Humanities Council grant.  Built first as the American Insurance Union Citadel (or AIU Building), one of Columbus's most beloved and certainly architecturally distinct buildings has a fascinating dichotomy of idealism and egotism, architectural hubris and down-to-earth drama.

name: Historic Tavern Tours: The Irish & German Experience
description: Our popular Historic Tavern Tours return in April with visits to three taverns associated with the Irish and German populations of Columbus. Drinks are not included in the ticket price, but sparkling narration, historic gossip, and architectural knowledge of the taverns and their environs is cheerfully included, along with shuttle service between each tavern. Time at each tavern for enjoying the atmosphere and socializing before moving along to the next stop

name: Forbidden City
description: You have seen the movie (we hope), now live the experience. Take a behind-the-scenes tour of the LeVeque Tower and the Palace Theater to places few people get to see. Do you know how the zodiac is connected to the history of the LeVeque? Why the sidewalks on Broad Street are always clear? That there are penthouses in the LeVeque and a hotel attached to the Palace? That animals showered below the stage before their debuts? So much to learn and only a few hours in which to see it all. Tours are small and advance tickets are a must.

name: Center Stage Players: [title of show] - yes that's the name of the show!
description: Jeff and Hunter, two struggling writers, hear about a new musical theatre festival. However, the deadline for submissions is a mere three weeks away. With nothing to lose, the pair decides to try to create something new with the help of their friends Susan, Heidi and Larry on the eighty-eights. With the cast in place, Jeff and Hunter begin a conversation about what to write about. Eventually, Jeff suggests they write about what to write about. They make a pact to write up until the festival's deadline and dream about the show changing their lives. [title of show]-taken from the space on the festival's application form which asks for the [title of show]-follows Hunter and Jeff and their friends on their journey through the gauntlet of creative self-expression. In the span of 90 minutes they write and perform their show at the festival and learn lessons about themselves as people, friends and artists. [title of show] is, above all, a love letter to the musical theatre-a uniquely American art form-and to the joy of collaboration. The musical received a Tony Award® nomination for Best Book of a Musical in 2009.

name: Earth Day Screening: Fuel
description: One week only in honor of Earth Week. Director Josh Tickell takes us along for his 11-year journey around the world to find solutions to America's addiction to oil. A shrinking economy, a failing auto industry, rampant unemployment, an out-of-control national debt, and an insatiable demand for energy weigh heavily on all of us. Fuel shows us the way out of the mess we're in by explaining how to replace every drop of oil we now use, while creating green jobs and keeping our money here at home. The film never dwells on the negative, but instead shows us the easy solutions already within our reach.

name: Nightmares on High Street: Wrecked
description: Adrien Brody stars as a man who awakens in a mangled car-wreck at the bottom of a steep cliff. Injured and trapped inside, with no memory of how he got there or who he is, he must rely on his most primal instincts to survive. But as he attempts to free himself from the carnage and escape an impossible situation, a darker side is revealed. Even if he manages to survive, the man may have to face the horrible consequences of an earlier, forgotten life.

name: Comedy Town Live Improv Showdown
description: Comedy Town Showdown is a special comedy competition featuring head-to-head improv teams. The audience awards the crown in this monthly competition for ultimate local improv bragging rights. Admission is just $5.

name: Exhibit: Image Self: Women in Art
description: Department of Art Professor and 2008 Guggenheim Fellow Ardine Nelson developed a collaborative project with 23 students that address the question, How does one understand self through image? Throughout the summer and fall Nelson created large-scale formal studio portraits of students. Each student was given a copy of her portrait, and full liberty to alter it-in any manner she chose-to more fully and corporeally capture and reflect her understanding of self. Support provided by the Department of Women's Studies and the Coca-Cola Critical Difference for Women Research on Women, Gender and Gender Equity Grant.

name: Exhibit: Art in the House
description: The Art in the House exhibition displays an eclectic array of artwork produced by children participating in the Greater Columbus Arts Council's Art in the House program. Using the Frank Museum of Otterbein College's Ceremonial Objects & West African Artifacts exhibition as a point of inspiration, the young artists worked with the support of four master teaching artists to create works of art that are directly influenced by cultural objects from around the world.  About the Art in the House Program: Master teaching artists, working with younger apprentice artists, provide educational arts programming to hundreds of children ages 5-11 at settlement house sites in the Art in the House program per year, for a cumulative total of nearly 4,000 program contacts.

name: Exhibit: Focus on Four
venue: Peggy R. McConnell Arts Center of Worthington
description: Showcase of Worthington high school's student art. Each year four high school art students from Worthington City Schools are selected to display their work throughout the Peggy R. McConnell Arts Center of Worthington; two students from Worthington Kilbourne and two from Thomas Worthington. This year Caitilin Watters and Michael Raab represent Worthington Kilbourne, and Thomas Worthington is represented by Jenny Danko and Caitie Sheban.

name: Exhibit: Matthew Johns, Kate Rhoades, and Cameron Sharp
venue: ROY G BIV Gallery for Emerging Artists
description: ROY G BIV Gallery is proud to present the work of Matthew Johns, Kate Rhoades, and Cameron Sharp.

name: 2011 Senior Fine Art Majors Exhibit
venue: Richard M. Ross Art Museum, Ohio Wesleyan University

name: The Next Stage: Staged Readings of New Plays
description: The reading will feature Tech Out by Martel Coleman (BA Theatre) and Village Idiot by Jayson Troutman (BA Theatre). Stick around to discuss the work in a post-show conversation moderated by Jen Schlueter, assistant professor in the Department of Theatre. Light refreshments will be provided.

name: The Next Stage: Staged Readings of New Plays
description: The reading will feature Same Winners Every Time by Ann Glaviano (MFA Fiction) and Waterboard Executive and Kentucky Waltz by Dominic Russ (MFA Fiction). Stick around to discuss the work in a post-show conversation moderated by Jen Schlueter, assistant professor in the Department of Theatre. Light refreshments will be provided.

name: Art in the House Exhibition Reception
description: The OSU Urban Arts Space is thrilled to present the Greater Columbus Arts Council's Art in the House Exhibition. Come support and celebrate this exhibition of children's artwork with the young artists and families, curators and members of the Greater Columbus Arts Council

name: The Next Stage: Staged Readings of New Plays
description: The reading will feature Up, Up, Over the Town, and the Men Who Move as One by Cate Fricke (MFA Fiction) and Territory by Clayton Clark (MFA Poetry). Stick around to discuss the work in a post-show conversation moderated by Jen Schlueter, assistant professor in the Department of Theatre. Light refreshments will be provided.

name: Kitchen Fundamentals: Pies
description: You CAN make pie from scratch! In this hands-on class, Pastry Chef Laura Robertson-Boyd will take you step-by-step through the process of making and baking pie from scratch, teaching you all the tips and tricks you need to know to make it, well. . . Easy as pie! We will test and compare several different recipes for pie dough, examining why and how each recipe works. At the end of class, each participant will leave with their own pie to bake at home.

name: ProMusica Youth & Family Day
description: Join ProMusica Chamber Orchestra and Franklin Park Conservatory for an interactive, family-friendly concert. The concert will feature a variety of chamber music, including a string quartet, brass quintet, and woodwind quintet. Arrive before the performance for a chance to explore and participate in family-friendly activities, including make-your-own shakers, conducting lessons, and other hands-on activities. The program will also include a chance to meet the musicians and explore different instruments in a musical instrument "petting zoo."

name: Adopt-a-Butterfly
description: Treat Mom to a hands-on experience releasing a tropical butterfly into the Pacific Island Water Garden. A Conservatory guide will show you how to release the butterfly properly and share cool facts about these amazing insects. Quantities limited, available on a first come basis.

name: Make Your Own: Jams and Jellies
description: In this hands-on workshop, learn how to transform the season's freshest fruits into jams and jellies and water-bath can them for long-term preservation. Each participant will go home with a sample jar and the confidence to can at home. Featuring Rachel Tayse Baillieul.

name: The Magpie Consort
description: The Magpie Consort, a choral ensemble of 20 voices, with delightfully eclectic repertoire spanning many centuries and different parts of the world, will honor moms with a special presentation of their spring concert, The Garden. Featuring songs about spring flowers, summer dreams, magpie chatter, nightingales, dusk and dawn, Magpie Consort is sure to help create a special memory for Mom and the entire family.

name: PreSchool Zone: Eggs
admission: $20 price includes one child and one adult
description: Eggs are a unique package of culinary possibilities. We will explore the nutrition and taste of yolks and whites while cooking up an egg frittata and yolk-painted egg shaped cookies. We will even use the eggshells to plant a grass garden.

name: Mamapalooza Columbus Spring Festival 2011
description: The first 100 Moms to arrive will receive a fantastic goodie bag! 10% of proceeds will benefit Amethyst Inc. Columbus strives to empower mothers by creating two mom-centered, indoor/outdoor, family-friendly events per year in Central Ohio!

name: Bring Back the Monarch Day!
description: Join us in learning how to grow milkweed, the host plant for monarch butterflies. Kids will make milkweed mud balls that can be planted in their home garden.

name: Make Your Own: Pasta
description: Making fresh pasta is an undertaking with delicious rewards. Participants will make ricotta gnocchi, egg noodle, and semolina pasta. A light pasta dinner will follow including sauces with seasonal ingredients. Featuring Rachel Tayse Baillieul.

name: Family Style: Cookies from Scratch
admission: $25 price includes one child and one adult
description: In this fun, hands-on course, parents and children will work together to make delicious cookies from scratch, including Chocolate Chip Cookie "Pizza," Death by Chocolate Cookies, and Snicker doodles. Pastry Chef Laura Robertson-Boyd will share her favorite childhood recipes she learned from her mom, along with her professional secrets for making perfect cookies from scratch. Featuring Laura Robertson-Boyd.

name: Guest Chef Series: Asian Festival- Japanese Home Cooking
description: Marilou Suszko is the author of Farms and Foods of Ohio: From Garden Gate to Dinner Plate (Hippocrene 2007), a regular contributor to Our Ohio Magazine and local PBS program, and has a new book, The Locavore's Kitchen out this summer. There is so much more to Japanese cooking than sushi and steakhouse teppan-yaki! Japanese cuisine, or washoku, has its focus on quality ingredients and different means of preparation. Please join us in our celebration of the Asian Festival with a sampling of foods representative of Japanese home style cooking. Four dishes will be demonstrated.

name: Guest Chef Series: Asian Festival- Flavors of the Philippines
description: Marilou Suszko is the author of Farms and Foods of Ohio: From Garden Gate to Dinner Plate (Hippocrene 2007), a regular contributor to Our Ohio Magazine and local PBS program, and has a new book, The Locavore's Kitchen out this summer. Filipino cuisine is mainly influenced by three other cuisines… Spanish, Chinese, and Malaysian. Filipino cooking is best taught through demonstration. It entails a great deal of peeling, slicing, chopping, sautéing and other food preparation activities. Join our celebration of Asian Festival with this demonstration of four dishes representing the three strong influences. Featuring Alma Saddam, PhD, RD.

name: Kid Only Zone!: Wood-Fired Pizza
description: We will teach kids basic cooking skills by making all of the components of a personal pizza. We will make the dough from scratch, prepare homemade tomato sauce, add vegetable toppings and bake them in our wood-fired oven. Each child will then get to enjoy his or her own personal creation!

name: Ohio Nature Education: Animals We Love to Hate
description: Featuring the animals that are most often feared and disliked, bats, spiders, snakes, and possums, this program dispel myths and includes fun facts about how these animals are beneficial. Includes live animals.

name: Tim McGraw W/ Luke Bryan & the Band Perry
venue: Value City Arena at the Jerome Schottenstein Center

name: Lynyrd Skynyrd and ZZ Top
venue: Value City Arena at the Jerome Schottenstein Center

name: Lady Bird and the Vultures feat. Twenty One Pilots
Runway for the Ballet
description: You're invited to experience today's finest summer fashions mixed with BalletMet's artistic style. The show features BalletMet dancers and a sampling of BalletMet designed costumes.

name: North Market Artisan Sundays
description: Columbus, Ohio - Our mission at the North Market is to bring you the best of everything local from merchants, farmers and musicians to outstanding local artisans and crafters. On the first and third Sundays from May through October the outdoor pavilion will be host a splendid array of artisans peddling their handmade local wares. Shoppers will find a unique mix of artwork, glass, handbags, jewelry, plush, soaps, stationery, textiles and other distinctive locally created goods.

name: Kitchen Fundamentals: Basic Knife Skills
description: Using the right tool for the job can make cooking easier, faster and more efficient. In this hands-on class, learn proper techniques for cutting and chopping a variety of vegetables, fruits, and herbs. At the end of class, use the produce you chopped to make fresh salsa (if you would like to use your own knives, please bring a Chef's knife and a paring knife). Featuring Laura Robertson-Boyd.

name: PreSchool Zone: Herbs
admission: $20 price includes one child and one adult
description: Fresh and dried herbs add flavor and nutrition to cooking. We will go on a sensory treasure hunt to find herbs in the Conservatory's edible gardens. Back in the kitchen, we will make pesto, herbed vegetable dip, hot tea from dried herbs, and a planter of herb seeds to take home.

name: Make Your Own: Honey
description: Honey is an ingredient in medicine and foods from ancient times to present. After a short tour of the Franklin Park Conservatory apiary, participants in this class will learn how to use honey to treat illness, sweeten recipes and ferment into home-brewed mead. Featuring Rachel Tayse Baillieul.

name: Make Your Own: Red, White
description: Make your parties more festive by learning classic wine and cheese pairings with three easy dishes to complement any appetizer plate.

name: Kid Only Zone!: All about BURGERS!
description: Drop the kids off for a dinner "experiment," comparing traditional hamburgers to turkey burgers and homemade veggie burgers. We'll also make healthy oven fries: a welcome alternative to fast food!

name: Family Style: Berries
admission: $25 price includes one child and one adult
description: Cooking together is berry wonderful! In this workshop, adult/child pairs will make a salad with berries, a blueberry turkey burger (vegetarian option available if noted with registration), and fresh berry shortcake. During class we will also tour the Conservatory's berry house. Featuring Rachel Tayse Baillieul.

name: YACHT with Light Asylum
description: YACHT's core duo of Jona Bechtolt (formerly with The Blow) and Claire L. Evans bring their disco-with-a-smile action to the Wex. Aided by a full band they'll deliver the throbbing grooves of The Afterlife and I'm in Love With a Ripper to delight local fans itching to dance. The musical axis that links Portland, Oregon, with Marfa, Texas, is at the heart of YACHT's artful electro-sound.

name: Three-Acts to Successful Screenwriting
description: Learn to craft your own screenplays by mastering the most common storytelling structure used in film and television. In this interactive workshop series, participants will acquire the skills to balance character development and plot advancement through the three-act format.

name: Pay Day and Limelight
description: Set in London on the eve of WWI, Limelight is Chaplin's vivid evocation of the lower-class music halls where his career as a comedian began. Chaplin plays the alcoholic clown Calvero who mentors a young dancer (Claire Bloom) after he prevents her suicide. The film's can't-miss climactic scene features a reunion between Calvero and his old partner, played by Buster Keaton, Chaplin's contemporary and fellow comedian and director, in the only time the two shared the screen.

name: Chamber Music Columbus: Cavani String Quartet
description: The Cavani String Quartet have long been a favorite of local audiences. Chamber Music Columbus and the Chamber Music Connection (CMC) are sponsoring a concert by the Cavani String Quartet to kick off the CMC's Spring Weekend Festival at Ohio Wesleyan University in Delaware. The Spring Festival Weekend allows students of any ability level, school age through adult, to participate in coachings and workshops with the Cavani String Quartet and CMC Faculty.

name: The Pleasure of the Cup: Drinks of the Speakeasy
description: Join us in a trip back through time to a world of "blind pigs," bathtub gin and flappers. As you visit select Ohio Village buildings, listen to cool jazz tunes and sample some favorite drinks of the Prohibition era, like the "Mary Pickford" and "Satan's Whiskers." Be sure to watch out for the Anti-Saloon League members or, worse yet, the police! Must be 21 years of age.

name: Columbus Children's Choir 15th Anniversary Birthday Concert
description: All nine CCC choirs will perform in Capital University's Mees Hall in the spirit of this season's theme, The World of Music.

name: Junip
description: Swedish singer/songwriter Josa Gonza¡lez has packed the house here as a solo exemplar of today's forward-looking folk trends on two past visits. Now he returns as part of the trio Junip, with Tobias Winterkorn providing organ grooves or swooping synth lines and drummer Elias Araya.

name: Music @ The MAC: The Shaw Brothers
description: Our Thursday Night Concert Series continues with The Shaw Brothers. Andy and Chris Shaw started playing acoustic gigs together back in 2004. The brothers played Andys original tunes, and that quickly evolved into the Andy Shaw Band. The bands reggae, rock, and pop sounds have been a mainstay for the 2 for the last 4 years, and perform on a regular basis. Now, with the success of the band, Andy and Chris have gone back to their roots, in a sense, to perform and write new acoustic material. These songs are a mix of all of the styles they enjoy, but mainly folk and acoustic in nature.

name: Cold Cave
venue: Mershon Auditorium, Wexner Center for the Arts
description: The dark-toned experimental synth pop of Cold Cave is quickly garnering new fans with its driving industrial beats and sweeping melodic sense. Icy-edged precursors like Human League, New Order, and Throbbing Gristle echo in their sound while Cold Cave find their own ways into the heart of darkness with lyrics juxtaposing images of beauty with harsh, raw vistas. Expect to hear many of Cold Cave's latest noir paeans drawn from Cherish the Light Years, their recently released CD for the Matador label. The recording is already being tipped as a breakout for the group.

name: Spring Clean-Up & Road-Side Repair Workshop
description: Join Wild Goose Creative at Franklinton Cycleworks to dust off your bikes, and get ready to ride this spring! Come celebrate National Bike Month at Wild Goose Creative!

name: Speak Easy Move it!: Stories of Locomotion
description: This month's Speak Easy is titled "Move It! Stories of Locomotion." Come to hear stories about what happens to people when they get from place to place.

name: Tea with Andrea Cheng
description: Andrea will read from her work including her newest book, Where Do You Stay? Bring any questions you have about Andrea's books, her writing process, publishing, anything you would like to know! We will enjoy an informal conversation with the author. Light refreshments will be provided. All attendees will receive a free READ poster and other goodies.

name: One-Day Master Class
description: The man behind the beloved column, "So To Speak," will lead a master class in humor and column writing for a limited number of enrollees in this special Thurber House Adult Writing Workshop. Enrollment is on a first-come, first-served basis, and is limited to 25 students.

name: Temple on the Hill: The Statehouse & Its Neighbors
description: The Statehouse Square has formed the heart of Columbus, founded to be a capital city in 1812. Planned to be a seat of democracy, this Greek temple on the hill is surrounded by other architecturally and historically interesting buildings - an early skyscraper, historic theaters, a re-emerging classic department store, even a church with a stained glass window of Ohio Stadium. Come find out how the heart of the city came to be.

name: Community Conversations: History: The Good, the Bad and the Ugly
description: Second in a series of community conversations on topics inspired by the special exhibit Controversy: Pieces You Don't Usually See. Panelists consider whether some objects are inherently controversial or whether time, culture and society dictate their meaning.

name: Civil War Lecture: Lessons of the Civil War Through Music
description: Celebrate the 150th anniversary of the Civil War with a monthly lecture series, featuring such topics as Civil War music, photography, fashion, ghost stories and others.

name: Small Talk: A Group Discussion
admission: Adults $8. Seniors $7. Children 6-12 $4. Includes admission to the Ohio Historical Center.
description: Informal small-group discussion related to the exhibit Controversy: Pieces You Don't Normally See.

name: More Land Office Records in Ohio
description: This course will identify where public land offices were located in Ohio. You will learn about records kept at each office that provide necessary information to determine who first purchased records kept at each office that provide necessary information to determine who first purchased land and when payments were made. Emphasis is on the description of land survey (field notes and measurements), entry, and payment records at the Ohio Historical Center and how to best use them.

name: Mystery Tour
description: Guided bus tours of three historic taverns in Columbus in the downtown area. In honor of Preservation Month, we are not telling the location of the long-established watering holes - but they are all treasures. You just have to trust us, but we think you will be fascinated by their contributions to the urban landscape and their back stories. Some have always been taverns and others have had a variety of lives. Drinks are not included in the price of the tour, but historical gossip, fun facts to share with your friends and relatives, and architectural chatter come with the ticket.

Planned to be a seat of democracy, this Greek temple on the hill is surrounded by other architecturally and historically interesting buildings - an early skyscraper, historic theaters, a re-emerging classic department store, even a church with a stained glass window of Ohio Stadium. Come find out how the heart of the city came to be.

name: Historic Eastside Restaurant Tour
description: We are partnering with Columbus Food Adventures for a historic east side restaurant tour.
