Some have always been taverns and others have had a variety of lives. Drinks are not included in the price of the tour, but historical gossip, fun facts to share with your friends and relatives, and architectural chatter come with the ticket.

name: Viva Las Vino!
description: An exciting evening featuring fine wines. Guests may attend the High Roller Tasting for a top-notch tasting experience as well as the Players Club tasting ideal for the young professional learning the nuances of wine appreciation. Guests will also enjoy a silent auction and delicious hors d'oeuvres.

name: Too Many Cooks
description: Too Many Cooks features local chefs and culinary artists and provides a space to feature their passion, whatever it may be. Whatever your interest you are bound to find something that resonates at Too Many Cooks. Join us the second Sunday of every month for an intimate conversation with the food artisans that are making Columbus a tastier place to live.

name: Knife Skills: Practical Cooking Class with Chef RB
description: Using the right tool for the job can make cooking easier, faster and more efficient. Learn proper techniques for cutting and chopping vegetables, fruits, and herbs. At the end of class, use the produce you chopped to make fresh salsa. (If you would like to use your own knives from home, please bring a Chef's knife and a paring knife.) Each class is taught by Chef Laura Robertson-Boyd and takes place at Wild Goose Creative.

name: Taste of Dine Originals
description: Our signature annual event, Taste of Dine Originals, is one of Ohio's best food and wine events, featuring tastings and samplings from 50regional restaurants, 30 vineyards, 2 craft breweries, and a couple of micro distilleries Whether you're a seasoned foodie or an intrigued beginner, chefs, brew masters, and winery representatives welcome you as they mix useful knowledge with exquisite samples of their art. The silent auction features cooking lessons, private dinners, special events, works of art, and rare bottles of wine.

name: Cause Collaborative
description: Cause Collaborative: Conversation, Q + A, and Cocktails for the Columbus Nonprofit Community. Brought to you by: Community Shares of Mid Ohio & Fulcrum Creatives. Topics include: Building & Maintaining Brands for Nonprofits Non-Traditional Fundraising, Cost of Free (Hazards of Relying too Heavily on Volunteers). Includes: Light breakfast & coffee, three guided Q + A sessions with Columbus nonprofit experts and peers, lunch by Freshbox Catering (veggie options available), and networking with cocktails. Each person in attendance will receive a workbook to use during the event with speaker bios, contact info & space for note-taking.

name: North Market Celebrates 15th Apron Gala
description: It's time to summon up your creative side and assemble, abscond with or otherwise acquire an apron for the gastronomically legendary North Market Apron Gala. We're not apron authorities, but through the years we've witnessed waist-tied attire that runs the gamut from naughty to nice, vintage to topical, unbiased to political and even some that resembled colorful creatures (the late, great Fred Holdridge and his flamingo, for instance). One of the nicer things about wearing an apron to the affair (aside from the prizes to be won) is that it nicely camouflages any inflated midsections that may arise from the fabulous feasting to be done. So get ready to tie one on at the 15th annual fundraiser for the North Market Development Authority.

name: Exhibit: Matthew Cherubini and Doo-Sung Yoo
venue: ROY G BIV Gallery for Emerging Artists
description: ROY G BIV Gallery is proud to present the work of Matthew Cherubini and Doosung Yoo.

name: Exhibit Reception: 2011 MFA Thesis Exhibition
description: Join the artists and curators to experience the diverse and dynamic work of this year's Masters of Fine Arts candidates in OSU's Department of Art. Light refreshments and drinks will be provided.

name: Footsteps Dance Co.: Love in the City
description: Footsteps Dance Co. presents their end-of-the-year outreach event Love in the City at the McConnell Arts Center.

name: Exhibit: Relics of Nature
description: Char Norman, associate professor and associate provost, at the Columbus College of Art and Design, is an accomplished fiber artist specializing in papermaking and fiber sculpture.

name: The Kid and The Gold Rush
description: Treat mom to an afternoon at the movies with two classics sure to please all ages! This Mother's Day matinee features two of Chaplin's most memorable and best-loved films.

name: A King in New York and The Circus
description: One of Chaplin's last two films, A King in New York, which features his final staring role, joins the hilarious classic The Circus for this screening. A King in New York was shot in Britain, since Chaplin was barred from reentering the U.S. He plays an impoverished monarch trying to get back on his feet in Manhattan. A scathing portrait of American culture, targeting everything from the House Un-American Activities Committee (HUAC) to Cinemascope to rock 'n' roll, the film was not released in the U.S. until the 1970s. (110 mins., 35mm)

name: Chronicle of a Disappearance and Divine Intervention
description: The autobiographical Chronicle of a Disappearance won the award for best first film at the Venice Film Festival. A series of mostly unconnected scenes depict, according to Suleiman, a journey in search of what it means to be Palestinian."" The director appears as E.S., a man who returns to the West Bank after spending 12 years in New York City. (88 mins., 35mm)

name: Close-Up
description: Iranian director Abbas Kiarostami's breakthrough masterpiece is a captivating ode to cinema that sees a young man arrested on charges of impersonating the well-known Iranian filmmaker Mohsen Makhmalbaf. Real people from the case play themselves in this stunning fusion of fiction and documentary, which is now widely regarded as one of the major films of the late 20th century. Veteran Japanese filmmaker Akira Kurosawa voiced the wonder shared by many when he commented, ""Kiarostami's films are extraordinary. Words can't relate my feelings. See his movies and then you'll see what I mean. (98 mins., 35mm)

name: Behind Enemy Lines: The Real Charlotte Grays
description: Jenny Morgan's acclaimed documentary Behind Enemy Lines: The Real Charlotte Grays examines the SOE's (Special Operations Executive) female agents in Nazi-occupied France during World War II. Four (of the then-surviving eight) women are featured in interviews, and two are movingly reunited with wartime comrades. The documentary was made for Britain's Channel 4. (52 mins., video)

name: Art Spiegelman Dick Tracy, Chester Gould, and More
description: Art Spiegelman shares his appreciation for comics' most famous police detective, Dick Tracy, as well as the art of the character's creator, Chester Gould, who wrote and drew the strip for more than four decades in this lecture.

name: City Lights and Modern Times
description: Chaplin developed sound effects and music for these not quite talkies, two of his most effective mixtures of comedy and pathos.

name: Poison
description: See Todd Haynes's controversial masterpiece, which won the Grand Jury Prize at the 1991 Sundance Film Festival, in a new print released for its 20th anniversary. Director Haynes has gone on to create Oscar nominees Far From Heaven and I'm Not There and the much-hyped HBO mini-series Mildred Pierce. This second thrillingly cinematic feature was among the most fervently debated films of the 1990s and a trailblazing landmark of queer cinema. Inspired by the writings of Jean Genet, Poison audaciously interweaves a trio of transgressive tales that range in tone from that of a mock TV documentary to that of a delirious 1950s' sci-fi melodrama. (85 mins., 35mm)

name: Erie
description: Erie consists of entrancing single-take, 16mm black-and-white sequences filmed in and around the communities surrounding Lake Erie. Scenes explore African American migration from the South to the North, contemporary conditions, everyday tasks and labors, theater, and famous art objects. Erie has been described as a revelation - full of images of pure poetry on Turner Classic Movies' blog and has been seen and honored at film festival awards around the world. (85 mins., Kevin Jerome Everson, video)

name: Columbus Moving Image Art Review 7 Spring 2011
description: The Columbus Moving Image Art Review (CMIAR) is a screening event for local Columbus Ohio artists. The CMIAR was developed by two local moving image artists who wanted to create a way for the seventh art of film to return to a more appropriate presentation medium of the cinema house as opposed to being featured as an exhibit or installation in a gallery.

name: Ohio Village Muffins Vintage Baseball Triple Header
description: Enjoy baseball the way it was meant to be played-no gloves, no spitting and no swearing-no kidding! There's nothing like the experience of a vintage game to take you back in time.

name: NCAA National Track & Field Championships
description: NCAA Division III National Outdoor Track & Field Championships, featuring nearly 800 collegiate athletes.

name: Exhibit: Quilts and Kiln
description: An exhibition of fiber works by Kris Worthington and ceramics by Alicia McGinty and Mark Nagel. Quilt's inspired by Worthington's emotional and spiritual journey, incorporating the Japanese shibori method of dyeing, hand and machine stitching, beading and collage techniques. Worthington's quilts portray life, landscape and abstract images.

name: Ceramics: Handbuilding & Potter's Wheel
description: This 8 week class demonstrates the use of basic handbuilding techniques to create functional and decorative ceramic pieces. Students will learn how to make platters, planters, vases and bowls using clay slabs and coils. Surface decoration using texture, colored slips, and glazing will be covered. Students will also have an opportunity to learn basic throwing techniques on the potter's wheel.

name: Introductory Potter's Wheel Class
description: This 8 week introductory class taught by clayspace resident artist Todd Hickerson covers basic throwing and glazing techniques. Students will learn how to wedge clay, center, make cylinders, bowls, and plates, and how to alter thrown pieces. Class time includes informal discussions, demonstrations and hands on instruction.

name: Camp Mary Orton Open House
description: Discover the Treasures of Camp Mary Orton 6th Annual Open House

name: Monday Night Live
description: Travis Hoewischer and Wild Goose Creative present a first-of-its-variety variety show, featuring some of the best creative comedy minds and brilliant musicians the capital city contains. No show will be the same, but each may include live and filmed sketches, improv and standup comedy, as well as other one special musical guest for each show. MNL will be hosted once monthly, on every first Monday.

name: Conversations & Coffee: Sandy Reddig, pastels; Debbie Jackson, polymer clay
description: Explore Sandy's delightful pastel paintings and learn about Debbie's polymer clay jewelry.

name: Move It! Stories of Locomotion
description: Move It! Stories of Locomotion is a live open mic storytelling event where you can come and listen to or share all sorts of travel tales. Come celebrate National Bike Month at Wild Goose

name: Intermediate Potter's Wheel
description: his 8 week intermediate throwing class taught by resident artist Todd Hickerson offers an opportunity for more experienced students to improve and expand their skills. Todd provides project ideas and inspiration along with excellent technical assistance. Class time includes informal discussions and demonstrations as well as hands on instruction. Students are encouraged to explore their interests and work at their own pace.

name: An Old Fashioned Talent Show
description: The Art League/Houston House Arts Center will be putting on an "Union County's Got Talent - An Old Fashioned Talent Show

name: Be Our Guest: Finding Creative Time + Space
description: Visual artists, writers, composers, performance artists, choreographers and more - this is for you! Learn about the hundreds of artists' residency opportunities available for artists of all kinds and every career stage, in your backyard and across the globe. Find out what distinguishes them, the best way to apply, and how to maximize your experience. The Alliance of Artists Communities is the national and international association of artists' residency programs - organizations that provide artists of any discipline with dedicated time and space for the creation of new work. The Alliance represents a field of more than 500 residency programs in the U.S. and over 1,000 worldwide. Believing that the cultivation of new art and ideas is essential to human progress, the Alliance's mission is to advocate for and support artists' communities, in order to advance the endeavors of artists.

name: Conversations & Coffee: Cody F. Miller, Artist, Biblical Narratives
description: Cody Miller, Art Instructor and Resident Artist with Good Will Art Studio and Gallery, discusses Mixed Media.

name: Slab Building
description: This exciting eight-week hand building class instructed by clayspace artist Todd Hickerson offers students an opportunity to design and construct boxes, platters, and large vessels with clay slabs. There is a strong emphasis on surface decoration using texture and colored slips as well as glazing and firing.

name: Independent Study
description: This class offers advanced students an opportunity to pursue individual interests with instructor support and class discussions.

name: Live Arts Concert
address: Broad St.& High St., Columbus, OH 43215
description: The evening program will consist of artists creating works in their medium to live chamber, jazz and folk rock music. Performing musicians will include Qube String Quartet, Christian Howes Jazz Trio and The Bruise Brothers. Participating Visual Artists include Todd Camp, Juan Carrera, Brittany Stigler, Todd Hickerson and others. Guests will bid on items in a silent auction and will also be able to bid on the art that is created live at the event. Heavy hors d’oeuvres will be served and a cash bar will be available.

name: Pinchflat: A Bike Poster Blowout
description: Come celebrate National Bike Month at Wild Goose Creative! Pinchflat is a bike poster blowout featuring limited edition, affordable artwork by Columbus artists. Come for art, music, a bike ride, food, and fun!

name: Happiness Quilted Expressions Family Day Workshop
description: The Riffe Gallery will hold a Family Day Workshop. Curators Linda Fowler and Tracy Rieger will help children ages 6 - 17 create a cloth collage using fusible construction techniques and embellishments to create pattern and design.

name: Conversations & Coffee: Dianne Efsic, Mixed Media
description: Learn about Mixed Media with Dianne as she discusses her Serenity: Moonscapes and being a Loft Gallery Artist.

name: The Past & Future of Bicycle Propaganda
description: Come join in on a discussion with Meredith Joy of Yay Bikes! This event is a part of National Bike Month at Wild Goose Creative.

name: An Old Fashioned Talent Show
description: The Art League/Houston House Arts Center will be putting on an "Union County's Got Talent - An Old Fashioned Talent Show

name: 24th Anniversary Gala: An Evening of Glitz & Glamour
description: The King Arts Complex annual anniversary gala is the "spring" event to attend. It is a party with a purpose to support the ongoing educational and performance activities. Great music, spirited dancing, multiple entertainment venues, worldly cuisines and specialty themed drinks make this an event that will infuse you with the magic of soul.

name: Kevin Jerome Everson Artist's Talk
description: In this talk Kevin Jerome Everson presents several of his acclaimed short films. Many of the films were filmed in Cleveland and Everson's hometown, Mansfield. He'll also discuss how he seeks to explore the lives of working-class African Americans by combining scripted and documentary elements with a keen formalism.

name: DIY Bike Light Workshop
description: Learn how to make your own bike light as part of National Bike Month happening at Wild Goose Creative.

name: Conversations & Coffee: Tom Dodge, Dispatch photographer
description: Photography for a great daily newspaper.

name: Gathering of Playwrights
description: Join local playwrights, theatre representatives, technical artists, performers and others interested in new work production for a lunch-time discussion that aims to create and continue dialogue between playwrights and the community.

name: Marcon
description: Marcon is the Midwest’s premier fantasy and science fiction convention. The event features something for everyone interested in the fantasy or science fiction genre from art,costuming, filk and gaming to literary, media, science and video, plus children’s programs, an art show, and a dance and masquerade.  A dealer’s room is set aside for those wishing to expand their science fiction, comic book, jewelry or costuming collections.

name: Music in the Parks
description: The Cultural Arts Division invites you to enjoy our free summer concert series, Music in the Parks, June through August, 2011. This free concert series takes place outdoors on the New! UA Arts Stage at the Amelita Mirolo Barn at Sunny 95 Park. Bring a lawn chair or a blanket. In the event of rain, the concert will be moved inside the Amelita Mirolo Barn while concerts at community parks will be canceled. Concert patrons can enjoy cool creamy free ice cream treats thanks to Huffman's Market.

name: Michael Jackson THE IMMORTAL World Tour by Cirque du Soleil
venue: Value City Arena at the Jerome Schottenstein Center
description: A riveting fusion of visuals, dance, music and fantasy that immerses audiences in Michael's creative world and literally turns his signature moves upside down, Michael Jackson THE IMMORTAL World Tour unfolds Michael Jackson's artistry before the eyes of the audience. Aimed at lifelong fans as well as those experiencing Michael's creative genius for the first time, the show captures the essence, soul and inspiration of the King of Pop, celebrating a legacy that continues to transcend generations.

name: Butterfly Festival
description: Join us and The Very Hungry Caterpillar in reading his story and exploring his world. Kids can try all of the food that the Caterpillar ate along with some edible leaves from our garden. Kids will participate in an obstacle course.

name: The Columbus Symphony Popcorn Pops: American Salute
venue: The lawn at Chemical Abstracts Service
description: Sing, dance, and monkey around with the Columbus Symphony at three special family concerts recommended for children ages 3-12. Children will enjoy free popcorn and free pre-concert activities including face painting, art projects, playing with musical instruments, and more.

name: Umphrey's McGee and Black Joe Lewis & The Honeybears
Michael Chapman with William Tyler
description: Michael Chapman is an English cult legend that began his career on the Cornish folk music circuit in 1967. He soon signed on with UK prog-rock label Harvest (also home to Pink Floyd, Syd Barrett's solo work, and Roy Harper, among others), where he recorded four influential albums, including the recently reissued folk-rock landmark Fully Qualified Survivor, which featured future Bowie collaborator Mick Ronson.

name: Robert Plant and the Band of Joy
Creekside Blues & Jazz Festival
admission: Adults $3. Children under 12 free. Military free with ID.
description: This music festival is the showcase for the best blues and jazz music in Ohio, if not the Midwest. Music isn't all that this renowned event has to offer. Centered around Creekside Park and Olde Gahanna, the Creekside Blues & Jazz Festival promises something for everyone with more than 90 hours of entertainment on 5 stages, Jog for Jazz, Sunday Jazz Brunch, Musical Discovery Zone, amusement rides, vendors, and of course, great food!

name: Fred Bailey Sings Stories of Hope and Struggle
description: Fred Bailey's singing voice is not sweet. Instead, it's gritty, ragged, and rough. But that's good. Because the 70 year old Clintonville performer sings songs about chemical factory workers stricken by lung disease, Vietnam war veterans plagued by battle demons, sailors lost at sea, skeletons of ramshackle Okie homesteads abandoned during the Dust Bowl years, and park rangers trapped by forest fires.

name: The Columbus Symphony Picnic with the Pops: The Jazz Ambassadors
venue: The lawn at Chemical Abstracts Service
description: The Jazz Ambassadors is the United States Army’s premier touring jazz orchestra. This internationally acclaimed organization travels thousands of miles each year to present jazz, America’s national treasure, and carry a message of patriotism and goodwill to audiences worldwide.

name: The Columbus Symphony Picnic with the Pops: The Music of Michael Jackson
venue: The lawn at Chemical Abstracts Service
description: Michael Jackson" takes you through each era of this storied performer from “ABC,” “I'll Be There,” and “Got to Be There” through “Beat It,” “Thriller,” “Rock With You,” “The Way You Make Me Feel,” and many, many more. Join conductor Larry Baird and the Columbus Symphony for an evening filled with fabulous music spanning 40 years of Michael Jackson's influential and celebrated career!

name: Jeni's Splendid Ice Creams at Home Book Party
description: This is the first book by Columbus ice cream queen (and longtime Wexner Center fan/member), Jeni Britton Bauer. Guests will have the opportunity to receive a signed copy of the book plus food, cash bar and complimentary specialty cocktail from Middle West Spirits, live music from hard-charging soul outfit Charles Walker and the Dynamites, and, of course, plenty of delicious ice cream.

name: How Object Collections Compliment Paper Record Research
description: Your great-great grandmother taught grades 1-8 in a one room schoolhouse. Have you wanted to see the McGuffey's Reader she might have used? Your great-grandfather worked at Roseville Pottery in Zanesville, Ohio. Would you like to see a dish that he might have created? This class will show how objects in the Ohio Historical Society's collections might help you understand the lives lived by people documented in paper record research. This class will introduce you to searching for objects of interest in the Ohio Historical Society's Online Collection Catalog.

name: Little Germany: Canals, Breweries & Charming Houses
description: The Great Southern Hotel was the architectural pinnacle of taste, culture, and acumen, and in many ways a high point of business for the city's largest ethnic group. Germans had been settling there since the very founding of the city. Explore the architecture, traditions, and stories that still define Columbus.

name: Courthouse Research Seminar: Probate, Recorder, Auditor and Clerk of Courts
description: The county courthouse can be a veritable gold mine of information. There are will and estate files, land records, tax duplicates, and criminal and civil cases. It seems so intimidating to know which office to go to and what records to ask for. This expanded four hour seminar will guide the genealogist through the maze of courthouse offices to find records of interest.

name: How to Handle Object Collections
description: Have you wondered how to care for the china or the antique chair that have been kept in your family for generations? How to handle them and proper lighting and temperatures will be discussed.

name: History of the Boulevard Block Party
Little Germany: Canals, Breweries & Charming Houses
description: The Great Southern Hotel was the architectural pinnacle of taste, culture, and acumen, and in many ways a high point of business for the city's largest ethnic group. Germans had been settling there since the very founding of the city. Explore the architecture, traditions, and stories that still define Columbus.

name: Small Talk
description: Informal small-group discussion related to the exhibit Controversy: Pieces You Don't Normally See.

name: Tour de Grandview Cycling Classic
description: The Tour de Grandview Cycling Classic is Ohio's premier cycling event, attracting an international field of professional cyclists to Central Ohio each year, as well as hundreds of cycling enthusiasts and spectators. It features world-class bicycle racing through the streets of suburban Grandview, as well as a number events and activities for spectators and cyclists alike.

name: The Morning Sports Report presented by Marathon
description: Hear the inside scoop on the Columbus sports scene. This breakfast event features high-profile sports industry leaders, as well as representatives from the Columbus Clippers, Columbus Blue Jackets, Columbus Crew and The Ohio State University.

name: ARTSpeak
description: The Gahanna Department of Parks & Recreation is excited to announce the latest addition to the 2nd Saturday's summer event, ARTSpeak! This indoor/outdoor showcase celebrates local artists and their talents, while providing attendees a firsthand opportunity to learn about and experience the creation of artwork.

name: BIA Parade of Homes
address: Off Hyatts Road in Southern Delaware County, Delaware, 43015
description: This event showcases 11 of Central Ohio's best and brightest in the area of homebuilding, home design and landscaping.Be sure to visit when the History Channel's American Pickers visits.

name: Columbus Discovery Tours
description: Explore Columbus with CHS! Travel through Downtown, Victorian Village, Franklinton, German Village, Short North, King-Lincoln District, Franklin Park and much more as you hear stories of national significance, international intrigue, and local lore. Over 200 years of history, growth, and development will be explored in this 90-minute tour.

name: MadLab: Theatre Roulette 2011
description: With their 12th annual Theatre Roulette, MadLab, now settled into their new space, returned to their usual method of operation for Roulette. They received 566 submissions and from that group of scripts, 10 were selected. 1 was written by a MadLab ensemble member (Jennifer Feather Youngblood), another by their former artistic director Chris Lane, 3 more by playwrights who have had plays performed at Roulette in the past (Christopher Lockheardt, Donald Dewey, and Mark Harvey Levine) with the remaining 5 from playwrights who had no previous Roulette experience. Auditions were held in January. 22 actors were cast in 30 roles. Four of them will make their MadLab debuts (Mony Carpenter, Vince Reese, Hilary Shelton, and Damian Synadinos). This will be David Tull's Roulette debut. 13 of MadLab's 25 ensemble members accepted roles with many accepting multiple parts. The Columbus Foundation, GCAC, Scion, and OAC support MadLab throughout the year. Following each playwright name is the city they live in and previous Roulette appearances. As always, the Roulette shows are split into 3 nights, shown in a rotating basis, until the final day when all 10 shows are presented. The names for the nights this year are Queen of Hearts, One-Eyed Jacks, and Suicide Kings.

name: Phoenix Theatre: Playboy of the Western World
description: First performed at the Abbey Theatre in Dublin in 1907, this classic Irish comedy is the foundation of much of modern Irish theatre. Christy Mahon, the playboy or trickster of the title runs away from his family farm and arrives in County Mayo claiming to have killed his father. The locals are as mesmerized by his story as modern audiences are by reality TV shows. They are more interested in his ever-increasing details than in justice for his murderous deed. Through the many laughs and comic interactions Synge reminds us of his characters' humanity with all of their faults and defects.

name: Thiossane West African Dance Institute: Celebrating Traditions
Columbus DanceArts: The Legend of the Scarlet Shoes
Shadowbox Live: Back to the Garden
description: Shadowbox Live's original musical documentary about the Woodstock Festival, Back to the Garden was the troupe's most popular musical to date. It was extended multiple times, running for an entire year and touching thousands of people with its message of peace and love. A special one night only, outdoor performance brought 3500 hundred people to Schiller Park, giving those in attendance a truly authentic feeling Woodstock experience.

name: Magpie Consort: The Garden
description: A program of music, dance, and poetry celebrating spring flowers, summer dreams, fruit trees, bumble bees, and the song of birds. Featuring music by Clement Janequin, Thomas Morley, Vaughan Williams, John Dowland, Jackson Hill, Abbie Betinis, Sheena Phillips, and others, plus folk songs from Venezuela, England, Scotland, and Bulgaria. With guests Jeff White (percussion), Eugene Braig (guitar), and Meghan Western (dance), and Ohio-grown flowers by Nancy Kangas.

name: Usher
venue: Value City Arena at the Jerome Schottenstein Center
description: Special Guests Dev and The Cataracs & Tinie Tempah.

name: Swingin' Tuesdays
address: 401 N. Front St. Suite 95, Columbus, OH 43215
description: SwingColumbus brings you the best of live bands and fun DJs to fill the floor with dancers every week! Jazz standards, New Orleans, blues, soul, and rock and roll will get you swinging!

name: Three-Acts to Successful Screenwriting
description: Learn to craft your own screenplays by mastering the most common storytelling structure used in film and television. In this interactive workshop series, participants will acquire the skills to balance character development and plot advancement through the three-act format.

name: Live Arts Concert
address: Broad St.& High St., Columbus, OH 43215
description: The evening program will consist of artists creating works in their medium to live chamber, jazz and folk rock music. Performing musicians will include Qube String Quartet, Christian Howes Jazz Trio and The Bruise Brothers. Participating Visual Artists include Todd Camp, Juan Carrera, Brittany Stigler, Todd Hickerson and others. Guests will bid on items in a silent auction and will also be able to bid on the art that is created live at the event. Heavy hors d'oeuvres will be served and a cash bar will be available.

name: The Mad Men - A Night of Crooner Standards
venue: Peggy R. McConnell Arts Center of Worthington
description: The Mad Men are four current (and/or past) members of Phil Dirt and the Dozers, the ultra popular Columbus based 50's and 60's rock n' roll band, who have formed a smaller specialty group to perform Frank Sinatra style crooner swing music.

name: Magpie Consort: The Garden
description: A program of music, dance, and poetry celebrating spring flowers, summer dreams, fruit trees, bumble bees, and the song of birds. Featuring music by Clement Janequin, Thomas Morley, Vaughan Williams, John Dowland, Jackson Hill, Abbie Betinis, Sheena Phillips, and others, plus folk songs from Venezuela, England, Scotland, and Bulgaria.

name: Leonid Polonsky and Friends
description: Chamber masterpieces performed by three extraordinary musicians, violinist Leonid Polonsky (acting concertmaster, Columbus Symphony Orchestra), violist Yuri Gandelsman (former Principal, Israel Philharmonic, former member, Fine Arts Quartet), and pianist Janna Gandelsman. Repertoire will include Shostakovich's Sonata for Viola and Piano, Op. 147, Mozart's Duo for Violin and Viola in G major, K. 423, and selections from Bruch's Pieces for Violin, Viola, and Piano, Op. 83.

name: Pulitzer-Prize-Winning Composer David Lang
description: This one-hour surge of postmodern music will serve as a retrospective of Lang's most riveting works, including Cheating, Lying, Stealing for bass clarinet, cello, piano, and three percussionists; Heroin for voice and cello with video footage of Lou Reed by Doug Aitken; so called laws of nature for four percussionists; Press Release for solo bass clarinet; revolutionary etudes for saxophone quartet; lend lease for piccolo and percussion; Born to be Wild for solo percussionist; and Table of Contents for two percussionists. Participating musicians include members of the OSU New Music Collective, the OSU Percussion Ensemble, and the Pendulum Duo (Joseph Krygier and Susan Powell).

name: Artists, Interrupted Spring Ohio Conference
description: This is a conference for the woman who balances the various roles of artist, caretaker, mother, protector, friend, wife, partner, and dreamer. It is a chance for her to take a timeout from her busy life and spend a few hours discussing, working, collaborating, and playing with other female artists who face these difficult but joyful and important "interruptions".

name: Chamber Jazz at the Museum with Mark Flugge
admission: $20 for adults, $15 for seniors, and $7 or students
description: Join us for great jazz in the newly renovated Cardinal Health  Auditorium. In May, enjoy "Chamber Jazz Greatest Hits" featuring Mark  Flugge and Friends.

name: The Columbus Symphony: Columbus All City Orchestra
description: The Columbus All City Orchestra is made up of 62 high school musicians from Columbus City Schools. They are coached by Columbus Symphony musicians or educators from other school districts, and have been rehearsing with Peter Stafford Wilson since mid-March. This concert is free and open to the public, and the program will include: Beethoven's Egmont Overture Brahms' Hugarian Dances No. 5 & 6 Bizet's Carmen Suite No. 1 Grieg's Norwegian Dance No. 1 Smetana's Dance of the Comedians Williams' Harry Potter Symphonic Suite Mozart's Violin Concerto No. 3 in G major, Allegro mvt.

name: Summer Fridays: Transit Arts
address: Broad St.& High St., Columbus, OH 43215
description: Summer Fridays is a lunch-time outdoor performing arts series presented on the West Plaza (High Street) of the historic Ohio Statehouse each Friday be­tween Memorial Day and Labor Day weekends. Summer Fridays at the Statehouse provides an opportunity for the public and downtown commu­nity to gather on Capitol Square to experience some of Columbus' diverse arts groups and to visit the beautiful Capitol building.

name: Exhibit: Art in the House
description: The Art in the House exhibition displays an eclectic array of artwork produced by children participating in the Greater Columbus Arts Council's Art in the House program. Using the Frank Museum of Otterbein College's Ceremonial Objects & West African Artifacts exhibition as a point of inspiration, the young artists worked with the support of four master teaching artists to create works of art that are directly influenced by cultural objects from around the world. About the Art in the House Program: Master teaching artists, working with younger apprentice artists, provide educational arts programming to hundreds of children ages 5-11 at settlement house sites in the Art in the House program per year, for a cumulative total of nearly 4,000 program contacts.

name: Exhibit: Face2Face: 25 Years of Art and Community
description: Studios on High Gallery celebrates its 25th Anniversary with, "Face 2 Face, 25 Years of Art and Community," an exhibition of new works by current members and alumni, showcasing the gallery's history and longevity in the Midwest art scene.

name: Exhibit: Eat, Drink & Be Merry
description: The Atrium Gallery at the OSU Hillel Foundation is pleased to announce its new exhibition, Eat, Drink & Be Merry, on view in the months of March and April, 2011. The artwork in the show explores eating, drinking, parties, celebrations, and good times. Curated by Amy Neiwirth, Eat, Drink & Be Merry features artwork by 12 Columbus artists in a variety of 2-dimensional media.

name: Exhibit: Greater Columbus Arts Council Visual Arts Recipients
admission: Adults $10. Seniors and student 6 and older $8. Children 5 and under free. Admission is free every Sunday and July-August.
description: The exhibition highlights the recipients of the 2010 Greater Columbus Arts Council Individual Artist Fellowship Awards and Dresden Residencies. The 2010 Individual Artist Fellowship recipients are Mary Jo Bole, Jill Gallenstein, Lynda McClanahan, and Steven Thurston. The exhibitions also features works by Michael Hays, and Danielle Julian Norton, recipients of the 2010 Dresden Residency. The Individual Artist Fellowship program provides unrestricted grants to artists of outstanding talent and ability who currently live in the City of Columbus and/or Franklin County, and have done so for at least one year.

name: Annual Senior Art Exhibition
description: The culmination of four years of study, this show features 14 studio art majors and covers a wide range work, from painting to photography, using digital and dimensional materials.

name: Art Challenges
admission: Adults $10. Seniors and student 6 and older $8. Children 5 and under free. Admission is free every Sunday.
description: Visit the Art Challenges station in the galleries to participate in  exciting, art-based games that highlight a CMA artwork or collection.  Compete against friends and family members or challenge the scores  posted by other visitors. All are welcome to participate, and prizes are  certainly part of the fun.

name: Copper Enameling with Kristin Ellis
description: Open to beginning through advanced students, this class is an introduction to the process of firing finely ground colored glass to copper surfaces. Students can make vessels, pictures and jewelry.

name: Exhibit: City Jewels, New Works of Art by Malcolm J.
description: Fresh A.I.R. (Artists in Recovery) Gallery is pleased to present City Jewels, New Works of Art by Kevin Malcolm Jones, A.K.A. Malcolm J.

name: Exhibit: In the Shadows by Crystal Tursich
description: OAL is pleased to present In the Shadows, a photographic documentation of the economic distress in the urban Midwest with a focus on homelessness in central Ohio, featuring artwork by Crystal Tursich and curated by Alex Conrad.

name: Retrospective: Charlie Chaplin
description: One of the most beloved, revered, and controversial film artists of the 20th century, Charlie Chaplin created some of our greatest film comedies, and his Little Tramp endures as one of the most internationally recognizable fictional characters. Born in England, Chaplin quickly became Hollywood royalty with an approach to comedy that emphasized character and pathos over more common varieties of slapstick. Although he enchanted audiences the world over, his tumultuous romantic life and political views were the subject of constant scrutiny by the FBI. Accused of Communist sympathies, he was denied reentry to the United States after attending the premiere of Limelight in England in 1952 and only returned in 1972 to receive an honorary Oscar.

name: Ohio Art League's 100th Annual Spring Juried Exhibition
description: The Ohio Art League's 100th Annual Spring Juried Exhibition features a variety of original works by some of Ohio's leading artists as selected by Todd Slaughter.

name: Exhibit: Jason Snyder, Paul Barnes, Joe Scarano and Roland Tamayo
description: Rivet's May exhibition will feature original works of Jason Snyder, ]Paul Barnes, Joe Scarano and Roland Tamayo.

name: Matchbox Pinhole Camera Workshop
description: Come learn how to turn an old matchbox into a working re-usable camera! We ask that every participant bring their own roll of 35mm film for their camera, all other supplies will be provided by the Space.

name: Art Explorations: Keepsake Lockets
description: Guests at this month's edition of Art Explorations will join OSU Art Education student Stephanie Proffitt in creating lockets using miniature canvases. Participants will explore paint, clay and photography to craft this portable piece of art.

name: Art of Empowerment
description: Muse Gallery is taking this opportunity, in correlation with women (events such as Mother's Day, Women's Fund of Central Ohio, and the release of the movie ""Who Does She Think She Is?), to feature women artists and a male artist whose handling of the female form in art is relevant to the issues of women. Russell Whiting not only showcases the beauty and strength of women, but because of his personal relationship with the issues of women, we at Muse Gallery felt he was the perfect artist to showcase. Russell Whiting's work is generally based on goddesses of Greek and Egyptian Mythology. His newest pieces incorporate wood and steel, a rough assemblage of materials that can imply as much about how women are a combination of influences and experiences, as our specific heritage being a mixture of different parts -- all of which make us interesting.

name: Off Your Glass! A no pedestal, no rules' Glass Exhibition
description: This exhibition is going to be an exciting show of glass installation only! No pedestals! This exhibition is going to be an open submission / selected group show.

name: Drawing in the Galleries
description: Experience CMA in a new way and see art from a different perspective.  Join us and explore the basic elements of drawing while also developing  observational skills and an appreciation for the artistic process. You  will learn as much about seeing as about drawing. This program is  recommended for visitors ages thirteen and older

name: Exhibit: Street Talk and Spiritual Matters: Aminah's Mt. Vernon Avenue
admission: Adults $10. Seniors and student 6 and older $8. Children 5 and under free. Admission is free every Sunday and July-August.
description: Aminah Robinson's RagGonNons, paintings, drawings, hogmawg sculptures, prints and books about Mt. Vernon Avenue, bring to life the heart of this African-American community that flourished on the eastside of Columbus until the early 1960s. The work typifies Aminah's passion with remembering and documenting the past in order to move forward. Aminah emphasizes the economic vibrancy and social activity of the neighborhood and also raises complex racial and political issues that were at play at the time. At the heart of the exhibition, are the scroll-like Memory Maps in which Aminah records every detail of the lively street life of Mt. Vernon Avenue. The street's storefronts, churches, theaters, and offices are the backdrop for Aminah's depictions of The Brownyskin Man, Umbrella Man, Organgrinder and dozens of other figures that populate the street. Many of these figures are also represented in sculptures, prints, and cloth paintings that demonstrate the artist's use of diverse media and techniques. The Memory Maps became the basis for Aminah's published book, A Street Called Home. Visitors will be able to gain insight into Aminah's creative process by examining her original art for the book and the study that preceded it. The time span represented in the work ranges from the early part of the twentieth century to the 1960s when construction of the interstate highway, urban planning, and civil rights demonstrations dramatically changed the tenor of the neighborhood. In an effort to bring the work alive and provide context for the art, we are video-taping individuals who have memories and stories about the street.

name: Drawing in the Galleries
description: Experience CMA in a new way and see art from a different perspective.  Join us and explore the basic elements of drawing while also developing  observational skills and an appreciation for the artistic process. You  will learn as much about seeing as about drawing. This program is  recommended for visitors ages thirteen and older

name: One Work One Hour
admission: Adults $10. Seniors and student 6 and older $8. Children 5 and under free.
description: One Work One Hour is an engaging docent-led conversation about a single  work of art that takes place over the course of one hour. Explore the  meaning of the work of art and see how it connects to your world today.  In May, discuss Robert Delaunay's Air, Iron, and Water in the Picasso  and the Modern World Gallery. In June, discuss Evan Penny's Back of  Kelly in the New Materials Gallery.

name: Art Museum Day
description: Art Museum Day is a national and international day dedicated to  promoting the value of museums in society. CMA will celebrate this  year's Art Museum Day "Museum and Memory" theme with free admission and  a special program connected to the Street Talk and Spiritual Matters  exhibition. Explore the rejuvenated galleries and dynamic Center for  Creativity. Then, at 1:00 pm, bring your family and join us for story  time with beloved artist Aminah Robinson followed by an artist book  signing.

name: Family Adventures
description: Share ideas, laugh, and play games during this docent-guided experience.  Your family team may embark on a scavenger hunt, imagine yourselves  inside a painting, or discover a work of art that tells a family story.  Family Adventures are a great way to share quality time and make new  memories together.

name: Country Presentation: Pakistan
venue: Shelter House at the Whetstone Park of Roses
description: CIP and the UNA will be sponsoring this program on Pakistan, the people and culture. Visiting Fulbright scholar and UNA intern, Ghulam Samad Shah, Sam, will be presenting about his home country this month.

name: Matchbox Pinhole Camera Workshop
description: Come learn how to turn an old matchbox into a working re-usable camera. We ask that every participant bring their own roll of 35mm film for their camera, all other supplies will be provided. Due to limited supplies, reservations for this free workshop are required.

name: Dinosaurs: Explore, Escape, Survive
admission: The Explorasaurus Package: Adults $24.75, Seniors $23.75, Youth $19.75
description: Stomp, crash, and roar your way to COSI this summer as dinosaurs take over the country's No. 1 science center for families, as voted by Parents magazine. Dinosaurs: Explore, Escape, Survive features over 10,000 square feet of prehistoric excitement, from moving animatronic dinosaurs, to advanced computer simulators that let you be a dinosaur, to a huge interactive maze. And don't miss the 3D feature Waking the T-Rex3D : The Story of SUE in COSI's giant screen theater. Experience it all for one great price! The Explorasaurus Package includes COSI exhibits admission and live shows; Dinosaurs: Explore, Escape, Survive; and Waking the T-Rex 3D.

name: Interior Film Screening and Q&A
description: View an exclusive screening of Interiors, a 25-minute dance film that transports a site-specific dance performance to the screen, at the OSU Urban Arts Space on May 28, from 2-3pm. After the screening, guests can participate in a Q&A session with the filmmaker, choreographers and their team of project collaborators to learn about their research and what it was like to create the alternative dance performance.

name: Asian Festival
description: The Asian Festival is a week-long celebration with festivities showcasing the cultural heritage of 15 Asian communities. Visitors to the Asian Festival will experience hands-on art demonstrations, interactive dance performances, Asian music, Tai chi, martial arts workshops, Asian games and Asian cuisine. A special Dragon Boat event will be held May 21 at Genoa Park, complete with live entertainment and food. Go inside COSI to see Asian art. New this year, Asian culinary classes will be offered at Franklin Park Conservatory May 22 and 24.

name: Family Fun Day: Bring Back the Monarch Day!
admission: Adults $11. Seniors and students $9. Children $6. Children under 2 free.
description: Join us in learning how to grow milkweed, the host plant for monarch butterflies. Kids will make milkweed mud balls that can be planted in their home garden.

name: 7th Annual Birding by Ear Weekend
description: This workshop is a great way to learn bird vocalizations, meet new birding friends, see abundant grassland birds, learn to connect habitats with their inhabitants, and explore the uncharted bird spots at the Wilds. Classes and activities are available for beginner, intermediate, and expert birders. This weekend is facilitated by Al Parker, accomplished naturalist and professionally trained wildlife biologist.

name: Avian Photography Weekend
description: Head out on safari in search of migrating birds amid spectacular scenery - without ever leaving Ohio - at the Wilds, designated an "Important Bird Area" by the Audubon Society. At a pace that allows ample time to explore the decisive visual moments, you'll learn photo techniques from expert photographers and build your portfolio of stunning flora, landscapes, and wildlife during this exclusive opportunity. This weekend is facilitated by Jerry Jividen and Barbara Jividen of Naturally Wild Photo Adventures.

name: Zoombezi Bay Sneak Peek Weekend
description: Another fun-filled summer awaits you! Grab your swimsuits and get prepared for the return of the thrilling slides, extreme waves and rivers! The park officially opens daily on May 25.

name: Columbus Commons Grand Opening Weekend
address: High Street between State and Rich, Columbus, OH 43215
description: Capitol South will kick-off the 2011 Columbus Commons Summer Season in style with multiple live music performances, food, drinks, fireworks and the first ever Trophy Thursday, an adult recess activity programmed by Wonderland. The celebration lasts all weekend long! Don't miss Saturday night's screening of Raiders of the Lost Ark, followed by fireworks.

name: Ohio Nature Education: Animals We Love to Hate
admission: Adults $11. Seniors and students $9. Children $6. Children under 2 free.
description: Featuring the animals that are most often feared and disliked, bats, spiders, snakes, and possums, this program dispel myths and includes fun facts about how these animals are beneficial. Includes live animals.

name: Hops, History and Hosters
description: In 1836, German Immigrant Louis Hoster opened the first brewery in Columbus. At the height of the industry there were 5 breweries located in what is now know as the brewery district. As the years passed consolidation, competition and the 18th amendment in 1919 (prohibition) aided in the decline of the industry. Join the Columbus Brewing Company and Columbus Historical Society as we welcome the Great Great Grandson of Louis Hoster, Jay Hoster, to tell the story of Columbus brewing history. As an added bonus, guests will be able to purchase a flight of beer and learn about the beer making process from a CBC brewmaster.

name: Ride of Silence: Columbus
description: The Ride of Silence is a slow group ride, akin to a funeral procession, in total silence. The ride is a safe, responsible, professional and mature response to the aggressiveness, intimidation, and carnage that cyclists face on the roads we ride. It is a means to: remember and mourn those killed by motorists, raise awareness that our community has, and supports, a large population of cyclists, show the public that cyclists are not going to stop riding on the roads, point out that we ask for respect from motorists, remind motorists that we wish only to SHARE the roads. Riders should gather on the South Side (State St.) of the Statehouse.

name: A Taste of Columbus: Historic Restaurants Tour
venue: Starts at the Columbus Historical Society
description: We are partnering with Columbus Food Adventures for a historic east side restaurant tour.

name: Blooms & Butterflies
admission: Adults $11. Seniors and students $9. Children $6. Children under 2 free.
description: Experience the emergence of exotic butterflies and watch their release into Franklin Park Conservatory's Pacific Island Water Garden. Dozens of species from around the world take flight and feed on tropical blooms. The Butterfly Emergence Center and hands-on activities interpret the butterfly's life cycle and in late summer native Monarchs will be featured.

name: HOOT Family Film Series
admission: Free with a suggested donation of a canned good
description: HOOT is a monthly festival of films, music and activities designed for Central Ohio families and children. On the final Saturday of each month, families are invited to enjoy stimulating games, story readings, and music from around the world. The Shazzbots, a popular local kids band, will provide music between short films.

name: PreSchool Zone: Eggs
admission: $20 price includes one child and one adult
description: Eggs are a unique package of culinary possibilities. We will explore the nutrition and taste of yolks and whites while cooking up an egg frittata and yolk-painted egg shaped cookies. We will even use the eggshells to plant a grass garden.

name: Family Fun Day: Dried flower crafts
description: Visit the Conservatory for hands on activities and make-and-take crafts.

name: Family Fun Day: Bird Crafts
description: Families can create paper crane origami and a bird seed craft, with a visit from the Audubon Center.

name: Family Style: Cookies from Scratch
admission: $25 price includes one child and one adult
description: In this fun, hands-on course, parents and children will work together to make delicious cookies from scratch, including Chocolate Chip Cookie "Pizza," Death by Chocolate Cookies, and Snicker doodles. Pastry Chef Laura Robertson-Boyd will share her favorite childhood recipes she learned from her mom, along with her professional secrets for making perfect cookies from scratch. Featuring Laura Robertson-Boyd.

name: Guest Chef Series: Asian Festival- Japanese Home Cooking
description: Marilou Suszko is the author of Farms and Foods of Ohio: From Garden Gate to Dinner Plate (Hippocrene 2007), a regular contributor to Our Ohio Magazine and local PBS program, and has a new book, The Locavore's Kitchen out this summer. There is so much more to Japanese cooking than sushi and steakhouse teppan-yaki! Japanese cuisine, or washoku, has its focus on quality ingredients and different means of preparation. Please join us in our celebration of the Asian Festival with a sampling of foods representative of Japanese home style cooking. Four dishes will be demonstrated.

name: Guest Chef Series: Asian Festival- Flavors of the Philippines
description: Marilou Suszko is the author of Farms and Foods of Ohio: From Garden Gate to Dinner Plate (Hippocrene 2007), a regular contributor to Our Ohio Magazine and local PBS program, and has a new book, The Locavore's Kitchen out this summer. Filipino cuisine is mainly influenced by three other cuisines… Spanish, Chinese, and Malaysian. Filipino cooking is best taught through demonstration. It entails a great deal of peeling, slicing, chopping, sautéing and other food preparation activities. Join our celebration of Asian Festival with this demonstration of four dishes representing the three strong influences. Featuring Alma Saddam, PhD, RD.

name: Kid Only Zone!: Wood-Fired Pizza
description: We will teach kids basic cooking skills by making all of the components of a personal pizza. We will make the dough from scratch, prepare homemade tomato sauce, add vegetable toppings and bake them in our wood-fired oven. Each child will then get to enjoy his or her own personal creation!

name: Family Fun Day: Animals we love to hate
description: Join Ohio Nature Education for a fun educational opportunity featuring the animals that are most often feared and disliked - bats, spiders, snakes, and possums. This program dispels myths and includes natural history facts about these beneficial animals. Includes live animals.

name: Columbus Food Adventures: All Dessert Tour
description: Join us on this van-based tour featuring some of the best desserts in Columbus. This tour will start at the acclaimed Pistacia Vera in German Village, visit the new Sugardaddy's downtown location to sample some of their sumptuous brownies and blondies, and then head north to the Pattycake bakery in Clintonville. Of course no dessert tour of Columbus would be complete without Jeni's splendid ice cream, so we will visit their new Clintonville location to try some of their newest seasonal flavors. Finally, we'll finish our tour with a fabulous dessert cocktail created by mixologist extraordinaire Cris Dehlavi at M Restaurant (there will be a non-alcoholic drink option available for those under 21 or who do not wish to consume alcohol). Please purchase tickets in advance.

name: The Market at 15th & High
description: The largest of its kind in the campus area, the market features fresh, locally grown produce from area farmers, as well as dairy products, meat, breads, and more. New this year: A featured food cart every week.

name: Chef in the Winery Dinner at Signature Wines
description: Local Food meets Local Wine. Experience dinner and a wine pairing like no other in Columbus. You'll enjoy a four course dinner featuring Ohio products prepared by the chefs from Invidia Personal Chefs, paired with wines produced locally by Signature Wines.

name: One-Day Master Class with Joe Blundo
description: The man behind the beloved column, "So To Speak," will lead a master class in humor and column writing for a limited number of enrollees in this special Thurber House Adult Writing Workshop. Enrollment is on a first-come, first-served basis, and is limited to 25 students.

name: Digital Storytelling Workshop Series
description: Do you have a personal story to tell? Are you a non-profit that does important work and want to spread the word? Learn how to create a short (3 minute or less) video. This 3 part series will teach you how to script, storyboard, shoot, create, and edit a short digital story.

name: Paper Making
description: Papermaking will be the program for the monthly meeting of the Calligraphy Guild of Columbus.

name: Eco-Chic Craftacular!
description: Our goal is to have vendors challenge themselves to bring a more "green" concept to some of their wares. This can be done with awareness during all stages of creation.

name: Garth's Auction's Book Signing & Lecture
description: Join us for a meet and greet with Jack E. Adamson, author of The Pottery of Zoar, Ohio and authors of Artistry of a Cabinetmaker by Jospeh Irvin & Paul Locher. These scholars have done some wonderful research on objects from Ohio. Join the discussion, ask questions & let's all learn something new! Refreshments will be served.

name: Fifth Annual Ohio Valley Auction
description: An Auction of Early American Antiques & Decorative Arts

name: Out Takes
description: Out Takes is the Gateway Film Center's monthly GLBT film. The series is a partnership with Stonewall Columbus and all proceeds benefit Stonewall Columbus. Showtime is the first Thursday of every month.

name: Movie Club
description: Love movies? Join CMA Multimedia Producer Jeff Sims for a conversation  about a topic to be illustrated with film clips. The session's focus  will be the use of music in films. We will discuss scenes that just  wouldn't be the same without the music. Clips provided by the audience  will shape the conversation.

name: Art Spiegelman - Dick Tracy, Chester Gould, and More
description: Art Spiegelman shares his appreciation for comics' most famous police detective, Dick Tracy, as well as the art of the character's creator, Chester Gould, who wrote and drew the strip for more than four decades in this lecture.

name: Couple's Workshop
description: Schedule a private lesson on the potter's wheel. Includes instruction, materials, and 2 hours of studio time.

name: Cocktails at the Conservatory
description: Enjoy the botanically-themed monthly featured cocktail or a full bar selection along with small plate hors d-oeuvres. DJs from Encore Entertainment create the musical ambience beginning at 5:30 p.m. At dusk, the Palm House glows with James Turrell's LED installation, Light Raiment II. $10 minimum at the door: receive $10 tokens for food and beverage.

name: Figure Drawing Group
description: This is a casual figure-drawing group for everyone (as long as you're over 18).

name: Cocktails at the Conservatory
description: Visit the Conservatory and view its exhibitions during this weekly after-hours social event. Enjoy a full bar selection, featured cocktails, small plates and live music on the rooftop gardens. 21 and over.

name: The Amiable Association of Articulate Atheists, Agnostics & Adherents
description: Philosophically rigorous (but friendly) discussions about religion.

name: Be Our Guest: Finding Creative Time + Space
description: Visual artists, writers, composers, performance artists, choreographers and more - this is for you! Learn about the hundreds of artists' residency opportunities available for artists of all kinds and every career stage, in your backyard and across the globe. Find out what distinguishes them, the best way to apply, and how to maximize your experience. The Alliance of Artists Communities is the national and international association of artists' residency programs - organizations that provide artists of any discipline with dedicated time and space for the creation of new work. The Alliance represents a field of more than 500 residency programs in the U.S. and over 1,000 worldwide. Believing that the cultivation of new art and ideas is essential to human progress, the Alliance's mission is to advocate for and support artists' communities, in order to advance the endeavors of artists.

name: German Country Presentation at Maifest
description: Come join the Columbus International Program for a German Country Presentation given by Susanne Kross, our German delegate, at Maifest. This exciting cultural event will take place at the Columbus Maennerchor. Music, food, and German entertainment will continue throughout the day.

name: Mamapalooza Columbus Spring Festival 2011
description: Mamapalooza Columbus strives to empower mothers by creating two mom-centered, indoor/outdoor, family-friendly events per year in Central Ohio!

name: Pressed Plates Workshop
description: Participants in this 2 hour workshop will construct and decorate plates with pressed clay. The plates will be textured and decorated with colored slips.

name: Showcase of Remodeled Homes
description: Now in its 22nd year, the BIA Showcase of Remodeled Homes will highlight 16 unique remodeling projects in the central Ohio area.

name: Tree Faces Workshop
description: Participants in this 2 hour workshop will create faces out of clay that can be used to decorate trees or other surfaces. The faces will be decorated with colored slips.

name: Fashion Night
description: The Scott J Salon Artistic Team from New York City, together with the Aveda Institute Columbus Student/Educator Team, will sponsor Earth Jam 2011 Fashion Night Benefit.

name: Hot Nights: Glassblowing Workshop
description: Working alongside gaffers at the Conservatory Hot Shop, create your own colorful piece of blown glass artwork, including candy bowls, ornaments, tumblers and vases. No previous glassblowing experience is necessary. Participants must be at least 16 years old and advance registration required.

name: Taste to Remember
description: Bring your colleagues and friends and join us for a festive prelude to summer at the 9th Annual Taste to Remember. Freshly prepared food and fine wine will delight your senses as you tour the silent auction and vie for the chance to have a local chef dazzle you with a delicious, multi-course meal in your home. Your fabulous night out will benefit Children's Hunger Alliance and the American Culinary Federation-Columbus Chapter scholarship fund. We look forward to seeing you there!

name: The Heads of State
venue: Knowlton Hall, The Ohio State University
description: Jason Kernevich and Dustin Summers left Tyler School of Art in 2002 and soon found themselves designing for the Dillinger Escape Plan. Not getaway routes, but band branding: posters, shirts, hoodies.

name: Columbus Beerfest
description: 75,000 square feet of beer tasting greatness! This year's celebration of all things hoppy and malty has over 175 craft beers for beer fans to try and enjoy.

name: Home Front
description: Artist, Interrupted: A Woman's Art Collective is pleased to present Home Front, an evening celebrating female artists from Columbus, Ohio who balance family and art. From musical theatre to the visual arts Home Front showcases women's creative endeavors in the home through performance and play

name: Day of Dance
description: This event will serve as a fundraiser for the People Helping People Campaign, the financial assistance program of the Y. Come get your groove on and learn some new moves! You'll have great fun for a great cause!

name: The CAPA Gala Fashionably Late Party
description: The Fashionably Late Party is your chance to join in on the CAPA Gala festivities after dinner as we open the Ohio Theatre for drinks, dessert, and dancing!

name: Marcon
description: Marcon is the Midwest's premier fantasy and science fiction convention. The event features something for everyone interested in the fantasy or science fiction genre from art, costuming, filk and gaming to literary, media, science and video, plus children's programs, an art show, and a dance and masquerade. A dealer's room is set aside for those wishing to expand their science fiction, comic book, jewelry or costuming collections.

name: Big Ten Baseball Tournament
description: Cheer on the Big Ten's top baseball teams as they play in Huntington Park, the home of the Triple-A Columbus Clippers.

name: SRO Theatre Company: Evita in Concert
description: Evita, Argentina's controversial First Lady is the subject of this musical masterpiece. As a young girl Eva escaped her dirt-poor existence for the bright lights of Buenos Aires. With her ambition and charisma, she was a starlet at twenty-two, the president's mistress at twenty-four, First Lady at twenty-seven and dead at thirty-three. Eva Peron, saint to the poor, was reviled by the aristocracy and mistrusted by the military was destined to leave a fascinating legacy unique to the 20th century.

name: The Actors' Theatre of Columbus: A Midsummer Night's Dream
description: This production will be co-directed by Beth Kattelman and Dee Shepherd This is one of Shakespeare's most beloved comedies and a return to the first play ever produced by Actors' Theatre of Columbus.

name: Play in the Park Thursday Night
address: High Street between State and Rich, Columbus, OH 43215
description: Thursday Night is the night to stay and PLAY in Downtown Columbus with live music, outdoor games and happy hour. Wonderland will be running Trophy Thursdays, an adult recess featuring fun, competitive schoolyard games like tetherball, wiffle-ball, and more! The Downtown LIVE concert series will be moving the park, along with the Capital Square Kickball League to make Columbus Commons the Thursday night destination for young professionals.

name: Commons for Kids
address: High Street between State and Rich, Columbus, OH 43215
description: Friday mornings are all about kids at Columbus Commons. The free event will kick off with celebrity story time by OSU athletes and coaches, in partnership with the 2nd & 7 Foundation, and will be followed by a fun, interactive children's activity, with everything from jugglers and musicians, to inflatable and face painters. Kids can read, play, and take a free spin on the carousel. The Columbus Metropolitan Library will also bring the book mobile to Columbus Commons from 10am to 2pm, and will be sponsoring free Wi-Fi in the Reading Room.

name: Family Fun Day: Butterfly Festival
admission: Adults $11. Seniors and students $9. Children $6. Children under 2 free.
description: Join us and The Very Hungry Caterpillar in reading his story and exploring his world. Kids can try all of the food that the Caterpillar ate along with some edible leaves from our garden. Kids will participate in an obstacle course.

name: Family Fun: Father's Day Crafts
description: Kids make Father's Day, Dad Rocks, paper weights and paper airplanes.

name: PreSchool Zone: Herbs
admission: $20 price includes one child and one adult
description: Fresh and dried herbs add flavor and nutrition to cooking. We will go on a sensory treasure hunt to find herbs in the Conservatory's edible gardens. Back in the kitchen, we will make pesto, herbed vegetable dip, hot tea from dried herbs, and a planter of herb seeds to take home.

name: Family Fun Day: Gone to the Dogs!
description: Kids participate in dog-themed crafts and story time with a visit from therapy dogs.

name: PBJ & Jazz Summer Series: Matt & Natalie Adams
description: PBJ & Jazz concerts are 1-hour long interactive concerts designed to introduce jazz and American music to young children and their families. Featuring some of Columbus' finest musicians and ensembles, PBJ & Jazz concerts are hosted by retired music educator Rebecca Ogden -- and are a great introduction to live music for the youngest audience member.

name: Family Fundays
address: High Street between State and Rich, Columbus, OH 43215
description: Bring your family to Columbus Commons on the second Sunday of each month for free family programming and entertainment. Each month will have a different programming theme with June slated for Children's health and fitness, featuring a live kids fitness demo with Fit Club. July will focus on kid's literacy and the Columbus Metropolitan Library will be bringing nationally-known performer Jim Gill. August will be all about animals, with a butterfly release into the gardens by Franklin Park Conservatory.

name: Make Your Own: Honey
description: Honey is an ingredient in medicine and foods from ancient times to present. After a short tour of the Franklin Park Conservatory apiary, participants in this class will learn how to use honey to treat illness, sweeten recipes and ferment into home-brewed mead. Featuring Rachel Tayse Baillieul.

name: Make Your Own: Red, White and Bleu
description: Make your parties more festive by learning classic wine and cheese pairings with three easy dishes to complement any appetizer plate.

name: Kid Only Zone!: All about Burgers
description: Drop the kids off for a dinner "experiment," comparing traditional hamburgers to turkey burgers and homemade veggie burgers. We'll also make healthy oven fries: a welcome alternative to fast food!

name: The Columbus Symphony Popcorn Pops: American Salute
venue: The lawn at Chemical Abstracts Service
description: Sing, dance, and monkey around with the Columbus Symphony at three special family concerts recommended for children ages 3-12. Children will enjoy free popcorn and free pre-concert activities including face painting, art projects, playing with musical instruments, and more.

name: Kids Cooking: Berries
admission: $25 price includes one child and one adult
description: Cooking together is berry wonderful! In this workshop, adult/child pairs will make a salad with berries, a blueberry turkey burger (vegetarian option available if noted with registration), and fresh berry shortcake. During class we will also tour the Conservatory's berry house. Featuring Rachel Tayse Baillieul.

name: Summer Fridays: Idiot Boys
address: Broad St.& High St., Columbus, OH 43215
description: Summer Fridays is a lunch-time outdoor performing arts series presented on the West Plaza (High Street) of the historic Ohio Statehouse each Friday be­tween Memorial Day and Labor Day weekends. Summer Fridays at the Statehouse provides an opportunity for the public and downtown commu­nity to gather on Capitol Square to experience some of Columbus' diverse arts groups and to visit the beautiful Capitol building.

name: First Tuesdays Songwriter's Circle
venue: Peggy R. McConnell Arts Center of Worthington
description: Come join the songwriter's circle @ the MAC! We will spend a little time discussing some general guidelines and some more time playing. Bring your instrument.

name: Summer Fridays: Arnett Howard
address: Broad St.& High St., Columbus, OH 43215
description: Summer Fridays is a lunch-time outdoor performing arts series presented on the West Plaza (High Street) of the historic Ohio Statehouse each Friday be­tween Memorial Day and Labor Day weekends. Summer Fridays at the Statehouse provides an opportunity for the public and downtown commu­nity to gather on Capitol Square to experience some of Columbus' diverse arts groups and to visit the beautiful Capitol building.

name: Creekside Blues & Jazz Festival
admission: Adults $3 or $8 weekend pass. Children under 12 free. Military free with ID. Free June 19 from noon-2 p.m. to anyone donating a non-perishable food item.
description: This music festival is the showcase for the best blues and jazz music in Ohio, if not the Midwest. Music isn't all that this renowned event has to offer. Centered around Creekside Park and Olde Gahanna, the Creekside Blues & Jazz Festival promises something for everyone with more than 90 hours of entertainment on five stages, Jog your Jazz Off and the Jog Your Jazz Off Kids Fun Run, Sunday Jazz Brunch, Musical Discovery Zone, amusement rides, vendors, and of course, great food!

name: Summer Fridays: Franklin Xpress
address: Broad St.& High St., Columbus, OH 43215
description: Summer Fridays is a lunch-time outdoor performing arts series presented on the West Plaza (High Street) of the historic Ohio Statehouse each Friday be­tween Memorial Day and Labor Day weekends. Summer Fridays at the Statehouse provides an opportunity for the public and downtown commu­nity to gather on Capitol Square to experience some of Columbus' diverse arts groups and to visit the beautiful Capitol building.

name: The Columbus Symphony Picnic with the Pops: The Jazz Ambassadors
venue: The lawn at Chemical Abstracts Service
description: The Jazz Ambassadors is the United States Army's premier touring jazz orchestra. This internationally acclaimed organization travels thousands of miles each year to present jazz, America's national treasure, and carry a message of patriotism and goodwill to audiences worldwide.

name: Summer Fridays: Columbus Gay Men's Chorus
address: Broad St.& High St., Columbus, OH 43215
description: Summer Fridays is a lunch-time outdoor performing arts series presented on the West Plaza (High Street) of the historic Ohio Statehouse each Friday be­tween Memorial Day and Labor Day weekends. Summer Fridays at the Statehouse provides an opportunity for the public and downtown commu­nity to gather on Capitol Square to experience some of Columbus' diverse arts groups and to visit the beautiful Capitol building.

name: The Columbus Symphony Picnic with the Pops: The Music of Michael Jackson
venue: The lawn at Chemical Abstracts Service
description: Michael Jackson" takes you through each era of this storied performer from "ABC," "I'll Be There," and "Got to Be There" through "Beat It," "Thriller," "Rock With You," "The Way You Make Me Feel," and many, many more. Join conductor Larry Baird and the Columbus Symphony for an evening filled with fabulous music spanning 40 years of Michael Jackson's influential and celebrated career!
